# Path identity W2: absences and mounts — what a removal or a witness drop is licensed against (Implementation Plan)

> **For agentic workers:** this plan is dispatched as a wave to a `ccrc-worker` session. Follow the `ccrc-worker` skill for the protocol (ack, claims, asks, wave-done). To execute the tasks, REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Programme:** path-identity, **wave 3 of 4** (the spec's W2). It follows W1a (run 399, the server's id gate) and W1b (run 433, ccd's id fix), and comes before W3.
- **Run: not opened yet.** The coordinator opens it and dispatches it only after #384, #397 and #410 have merged, W1b's run has closed, and the four consents of R38 are in the brief. Its deviation numbers were issued on 2026-10-16, before the plan was committed, and are defined singly in §Deviations found (R37, as amended). A number for a departure the wave finds is issued at its fix round.
- **Deploy class: AGENT-FIRST, fleet box first.** This is `ccrc rollout`'s default order, without `--server-first` (R14). `ccd/ccd` changes, and so do `shared/api.ts` and the server. Nothing is re-derived from `raw`. In the window between the two boxes, an old server drops `meas.leaf` at ingest (its reviver has no such key):
  - an UNCUT collect `done` it stored reads keyless after the upgrade and ends, as every collect row ends today;
  - a collect `done` the encoder CUT (its `leaf` kept, every other meas field dropped) is stored keyless with `truncated` set, so after the upgrade it reads truncated-keyless and keeps its item to the 7-day horizon.

  Both fail closed or end as today; neither ends a line early. The as-built note states the window, both halves. Fleet first is chosen because ccd then writes `leaf` and admits asides before the server relies on either. A server-first order was also safe. Neither the PWA nor the agent changes. The wire is additive, with no `FLEET_PROTO` bump and no coord.db migration (`measJson TEXT` already exists).

**Goal:** after this wave:
- **A witness dies only on a proven absence, on the recorded device, beside no slot, and only in the generation that was read** (TR3 A, TR4 A).
  - The tail's three witness drops all go through ONE generation-exact `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop`.
  - That helper parses the witness, asks the device the witness recorded (`_ws_collect_root_dev`) and lists the quarantine slots of the id (`_ws_collect_slots_of`). It then proves again that the leaf is absent, and drops exactly the parsed generation. It uses the collector's compare-and-drop where a NOREPLACE move exists, and a re-read field compare everywhere else (R1).
  - Its answer is `complete`, `kept` or `unmeasured`, with the reason. It prints nothing (R6; P15). `_ws_tmproot_remove` and both step-6 arms propagate that answer into `tmpRootKept`/`tmpwhy`. No caller suppresses it.
- **No removal crosses a mount** (TR5 C).
  - `_ws_leaf_remove` asks the mount question directly after its device compare, before the owner bits, the checkout question and normalise. It asks again directly before `rm`.
  - The reclaim and expiry tail asks the same question before `keep_of`, and again before the forced removal, of every standing nested checkout (step 3) and of the child's own worktree (step 4).
  - All of these asks go through ONE helper that reuses `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`, and Darwin skips them through one guard.
- **A kept-leaf item ends only when its leaf was removed** (TR1 A, TR2 A).
  - The collector's two `done` lines carry `meas.leaf` (`removed` or `absent`), and `_lc_json` keeps that key through its truncation ladder and its last-resort line.
  - The server ends the temp-root half of the item on `removed`, or on an uncut keyless row from an older ccd.
  - It keeps the item on `absent`, with a clause naming the path. It fails closed on a cut keyless row and on a malformed `leaf`.
- **An orphaned compare-and-drop aside is recovered under the full ladder** (TR6 A).
  - The server's population admits an id that a parseable aside name is for (S2).
  - ccd's audit judges a sole parseable aside as the witness, read-only (Option X).
  - The verb restores it under the reap lock before its fork, and the reclaim/expiry tail restores it before step 6. The restore is `link`, then a dev:ino proof, then `rm`.
  - An ambiguous, malformed or competing aside answers the new per-leaf probe word `aside`.
- **The smaller fixes.**
  - The floor knob's zero strip is one regex capture, so it runs in linear time (TR7 A).
  - A back-link with an inner NUL is refused (TR8 A).
  - Six late recycled-spawn boundaries are pinned (TR12 B).
  - The C13 sibling entry and the maker under BSD argument order are pinned, and the collect-why cases assert before the 300-byte cut (items 32 to 36).
  - Five carries ride this wave (R36), and two slugs found after drafting close with it (R41, R42). `comments-say-ccd-scans-the-session-value` closes narrowed, which leaves the residual `registry-id-l0-comments-say-ccd-scans-the-session-value`.

## Global Constraints

Each line binds every task.

- **Fixtures and fixture HOMEs only.**
  - No test or scratch command runs ccd against the live `$HOME`. Every ccd call goes through `makePrHarness` or `makeCcdHarness`.
  - Never touch tmux, `~/.cc-sessions`, `~/.cc-limits`, `~/.cc-tmp` or `claude-session@*`. The one exception is the counts Task 0 Step 5 reads, under R34.
  - Quote every path, and never pass an unquoted `~` to a ccd verb.
- **The spawn census.**
  - Every new file whose name matches `/^ccd.*\.ts$/` falls under `ccd-workspaces.test.ts`'s containment scan. It spawns bash only through the harness (`h.sh`, `h.run`), never with a direct `execFileSync('bash'`.
  - Every new `ccd-collect-*.test.ts` falls under `git-env-strip.test.ts`'s SCOPE. A git spawn there takes its `env:` from `inheritedEnv()`, never from a spread of `process.env`.
- **Mounts are faked, never made** (R35, spec §3.9).
  - Pins redefine `_ws_collect_mountinfo` (`MOUNTS_SEAM` with `realMounts`, from `wsCollectFixture.ts`).
  - No case mounts anything.
  - No session runs a privileged container.
- **Darwin** (R9). Every new mount ask passes through ONE guard, the first CODE line (after its header's `#` lines) of `_ws_removal_mounts_clear`.
  - Each Darwin pin sets `CCD_OS=darwin` and poisons `_ws_collect_mountinfo`. It then proves that the clean path reaches its existing Darwin removal.
  - On a Linux host, a pin that reaches `_plat_devino` or `rm -rfx` adds host-conditional shims (`process.platform === 'darwin' ? '' : SHIMS`). On Darwin, the shims are never added.
- **Rings.**
  - L0 holds declarations only: they go at the foot, plus the in-place edits the HARD BOUNDARY names.
  - L1 decides. L3 passes `measJson` and `truncated` raw. L4 wires and decides nothing.
- **No overloaded null.** For a collect row, `leaf` absent, `leaf` malformed and a truncated keyless row are three answers. A present value that is not a string is never revived as null (P3). The two places where the store's own encoding forces a fold are named, never hidden: a stored `"leaf":null` (the departure `present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy`) and a `meas` that is not an object (the residual `non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless`).
- **Wire.** It is additive. ccd's audit and verb JSON documents keep their shapes. `collect-readers.test.ts` moves only by `aside` (R20). `wsaudit.test.ts` stays green unedited.
- **Vocabulary.**
  - Nothing is added beyond `meas.leaf` with its two words and the probe word `aside`.
  - `ccd-refusal-scan`'s SANCTIONED stays 16.
  - No new `failed probe-unmeasured` or `refused state-changed` site is added anywhere in `ccd/ccd` (P6), so `archived-expiry-policy.test.ts`'s census holds unedited.
- **Single definition.**
  - One drop helper and one mount question (`_ws_collect_mounts_clear`, reused through one wrapper, never copied).
  - No third mountinfo reader: the sidecar's `CCD_MOUNTINFO` python reader is not reused.
  - One aside grammar per side, pinned in parity.
  - One aside path composer and one witness-body parser.
  - One leaf vocabulary, derived from its table.
- **Mutation-table discipline.**
  - Every guard ships with a case that goes red when the guard is deleted or mutated, measured before and after.
  - The three propagation pins are independent.
  - A comment is a request; a red suite is a mechanism.
- **Line neutrality.** The checks below are re-run after every such task, and no number in them is ever edited to go green.
  - `_lc_json` lies above `ccd/ccd:5818`, where the `|`-row pass sees an insert (`census-blind-below-line-5818`). Its edit keeps its line count, and leaves the line plan-a cites in it (`:4896`) untouched. Its python is one single-quoted bash string, so no apostrophe may be added.
  - `shared/api.ts` keeps every line above its foot.
  - `journalparse.ts` keeps every line above its frozen anchor.
  - The five citation passes: `(cd server && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/session-hook.test.ts -t 'CITATION DEBT|README HAS ITS OWN CENSUS|LOCATION INDEXES|ROW PASS|RANGE BOUND|backticked _identifier')`.
- **Every other `ccd/ccd` edit lies after line 19162, the corpus's highest `ccd/ccd` anchor (R43).** Only the stamp line and `_lc_json`'s in-place lines change at or before line 19162. Task 17 measures it.
- **The stamp, after every `ccd/ccd` edit:** `bash ccd/ccrc restamp ccd/ccd && bash -n ccd/ccd && node shared/mark.mjs --check ccd/ccd`, then `ownership.test.ts` and `mark-check.test.ts`.
- **vitest** runs in the foreground, from `server/`, as `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/<file>`, with a timeout of at least 600000 ms. Never use bare `npx vitest`.
  - A red in a CLAUDE.md load flake (the collector suites included) is re-run ALONE before it counts as a break.
  - Load-flake membership is measured, never assumed. A new file whose cases shell the real `/proc` walk joins CLAUDE.md's list in its own task's commit (R13). A walk counts whether it is `_ws_path_users`'s or the expiry ladder's (`_ws_expire_cwd_users`, through `_ws_expire_proc_root`; R45), so a case that runs a real ws-expire audit or verb without stubbing that seam walks `/proc`. `ccd-collect-race-spawn-late` (R30), `ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts` (Task 5), `ccd-tmproot-drop-propagation` (Task 7) and `ccd-collect-aside-settle` (Task 11) join it by this plan, the last three for their ws-expire cases. `ccd-removal-mounts` joins too if Task 4 Step 5 measures that it does (the ledger line `Task 4 Step 5: ccd-removal-mounts joined`).
- **The 300-byte cut.** Every reason a journal row carries passes `_ws_leaf_why_line`. New reasons put their decisive words first, before any path. Tests assert a fixed lead, or read the uncut global (`_WS_WDROP_WHY`, `_WS_MOUNTS_WHY`, `_WS_ASIDE_WHY`, `REAP_DETAIL`), never a clause after a fixture path.
- **New cases go in NEW files.** An existing file is edited only where the HARD BOUNDARY names it.
- **No `D-` token in a commit message, and no four-digit number range in a commit or in the as-built prose.** A departure is named by its slug, and the coordinator assigns its number.
- **Branch discipline.**
  - One commit per task, on this workspace's own branch. Never a feature branch.
  - Absorb `main` only with `git merge`, on a clause-16 trigger.
  - On the `ccd/ccd` line-2 conflict, take either side of THAT LINE only, then restamp.
  - Every task's commit message ends the same way: one blank line, then the commit attribution line the worker's own session is given (its system reminder, or the operator's instructions where those differ). No commit block in this plan writes it, so add it as the message's last line at commit time, after anything a block appends (Task 14's `printf` line included). If the session is given none, no commit carries one.
- **Cite the SPEC** ("path-identity spec §3.5"), never the contract. A backticked `_name` in a `ccd/ccd` comment must exist (the danglers scan).
- **Locate code by CONTENT.** The line numbers here are export hints. Task 0 re-grounds every anchor.
- **ws-expire** reaches steps 3, 4 and 6, `_ws_leaf_remove`, the drop helper, the aside settle and the reader through the shared tail. Those edits ride workspace-lifecycle's consent (R38). `_ws_expire_locked`, EXPIRE-V1 and the vocabulary come through byte-identical.
- **R89's closure.** `collect` joins no birth, generation, latest-event or seed read. `ws-collect-act.test.ts` and `child-reclaim-birth-removal.test.ts` stay green and untouched.
- **Commands are approval-free:** plain reads, git, grep, sed, awk, node, vitest, and `gh` reads, plus Task 17's push, PR and `workflow_dispatch`. Never `pkill` or `killall`; kill only a PID you recorded. Subagents never send mail, and never invoke the `ccrc-worker` skill.
- **The repository is public.** Nothing goes into code, tests, commits or the PR body that names a host, an absolute home path, a private project, an account or a lane. Use neutral stand-ins (`the fleet box`, `<projects-root>`, `demo-*` fixture ids).

## Rulings that amend the task text (binding; the coordinator, 2026-10-15)

The plan is built on a PROJECTION: `origin/main` at `a3cebde1b`, with #384, #397 and #410 merged in. W2 branches from `main` once those three land, and Task 0 re-grounds every anchor by content.

The operator's working rulings from the W0 merge stand: TR1 A, TR2 A, TR3 A, TR4 A, TR5 C, TR6 A, TR7 A, TR8 A, TR9 C, TR10 C, TR11 C, TR12 B, PG1 B and PG2 A. A slug marks each place where a ruling narrows, widens or spells out the spec. The as-built note names each such slug.

**The drop helper (TR3, TR4).**
- **R1 — Where no NOREPLACE move exists** (Darwin, or a Linux `mv` without `--no-copy`).
  - The helper re-reads the witness through `_ws_tmproot_witness_read`, compares all six parsed fields with its first read, runs `rm -f` on the live name and proves it absent.
  - The window from the re-read to the unlink is a stated residual, `tail-drop-not-noreplace-without-mv-no-copy`.
  - Where the move exists, the helper uses the collector's compare-and-drop (`_ws_collect_witness_cad`), and that window is closed.
  - The device and slot checks run on every platform, before either path.
  - Pins exist both ways: a Darwin pin for the fallback, and the Linux spy for the compare-and-drop.
- **R2 — Any standing slot of the id keeps the witness**, whether or not a record names it. The race-crash and race-spawn reshapes, and the extra collector round they cause, are accepted.
- **R3 — The helper proves the leaf absent again**, after its witness read and before the compare-and-drop, through one `_ws_reclaim_absent`. "Kept" therefore always means "not proven gone". The pins that assert today's window are rewritten in the same commit. Slug: `drop-helper-reproves-the-absence` (a widening beyond Figure 3).
- **R4 — An id no witness is named for answers rc 1**: kept, with nothing touched. The existing pins stay.
- **R5 — The tail records a kept witness as `unmeasured`**, for both kept answers, with the reason in `tmpwhy`. No new tail word is added.

- **R7 — The helper's contract.**
  - rc 0 means complete, with `_WS_WDROP` set to `dropped` or `absent`.
  - rc 1 means kept: a slot stands, a newer generation stands, or the id is not one a witness is named for.
  - rc 2 means unmeasured: the witness does not parse; the device answers 1 or 2; the quarantine cannot be listed; or the absence re-proof or the compare cannot decide.
  - The reason goes in `_WS_WDROP_WHY`, and `_WS_WIT_*` is shadowed with `local`.
  - `_ws_tmproot_remove` maps the helper's 1 and 2 to its own 2, never to 1, because its 1 means "the leaf was refused". Its stale header sentence ("a collector passes") is reworded.
  - A scan pin requires that no drop call in `ccd/ccd` is suppressed with `|| :`.

### Proposed by the frame (binding once the coordinator confirms them in the brief)

These settle the places where the rulings, the spec and the measured code meet, and the rulings do not name the shape. The brief confirms each, or carries a reversal.

- **P1 — One mount helper, with a resolve mode** (R9, R11).
  - `_ws_removal_mounts_clear DIR [resolve]`. Its FIRST CODE line (after its header's `#` lines) is the one Darwin guard. With `resolve`, it resolves DIR through `_ws_dir_physical`, which becomes its ninth caller: both of its census sentences ("its eight callers", twice) say nine.
  - The leaf and step 3 pass a path that is physical by construction (`rroot` came from `_ws_dir_physical`; `cpath` is proven physical by `_ws_reclaim_nested_proven` in the same iteration). Neither enters the directory, so a mode-000 leaf keeps today's answer.
  - Step 4 passes `resolve`, because `$workdir` may sit under a symlinked ancestor. A standing workdir that cannot be resolved therefore now fails `worktree-remove-failed` before `keep_of` (`step-4-unresolvable-workdir-fails-before-keep-of`, recorded under Task 5).
- **P2 — The learning audit's id gate** (R36's `collector-learning-audit-relies-on-the-population-gate`).
  - `CollectLearnAnswer` gains a DISTINCT arm, `{ kind: 'id-refused' }`, never `not-asked` with a reused why, because `watch.ts` clears every pair on a `not-asked`.
  - The arm forces one line in `watch.ts`'s `collectLearn` handler: `if (answer.kind === 'id-refused') return;`. This is the HARD BOUNDARY's one `watch.ts` line.
- **P3 — The reviver never folds a present value into null.**
  - `leaf` is revived by `presentAsText`: absent or JSON null gives `null`; a string gives itself, whatever its word; any other present value gives its JSON text.
  - A stored `"leaf":null` is therefore the store's own spelling of "not carried": `reviveMeas` writes every key, the store persists that revived object as `measJson`, and ccd's encoder never writes an empty or null meas value.
  - A forged `"leaf":null` reads as legacy and ends the item, as a forged `"removed"` would. Attribution, not authentication. This narrows spec §3.4's "fails closed for a present malformed value" for the one value the store itself writes, and is named as the substantive departure `present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy` (Task 13).
- **P4 — `childReclaimLeafKeptSentence` gains a REQUIRED fifth parameter**, `tmpFoundNothing: boolean`. Its three calls in `child-reclaim-leaf-kept-prose.test.ts` gain `, false` and nothing else, as R16's "TypeScript forces every literal" principle asks.
- **P5 — `lifecycle-wire.test.ts`'s three literals gain `leaf`** in the same commit as the member (Task 12). R16's member forces this.
- **P6 — No new census site.**
  - The C5 verb's unmeasured answers fold into existing sites:
    - an aside listing that fails before the lock joins the existing "records could not be listed" `probe-unmeasured` statement in `cmd_ws_collect`, with its own text chosen inside that one statement (the records arm's text byte-identical);
    - the settle's doubt under the lock sets `REAP_VERDICT=unmeasured` with its reason, so `_ws_collect_locked`'s existing `probe-unmeasured` statement prints it.
  - So `archived-expiry-policy.test.ts`'s site census holds unedited. A task that cannot keep it unedited STOPs.
- **P7 — The leaf-end row is a union.** A `create` row has no `leaf`; a `collect` row has a required `leaf: ChildReclaimLeafEndRead`. The existing `create` literals compile unchanged, and every `collect` literal is forced.
- **P8 — A leaf that stands again at the helper's re-proof answers rc 1 (kept).** It is a decided "not gone", and callers treat 1 and 2 alike. This is recorded under R3's slug.
- **P9 — The settle prints nothing.** It answers by rc and by `_WS_ASIDE_DID`/`_WS_ASIDE_WHY`. The verb prints a `ccd: warn:` line on `left` (and on rc 2 when the fork's answer outranks it). The tail prints one on `left` and on rc 2 (R26).
- **P10 — The witness body parser is extracted once.**
  - `_ws_tmproot_witness_parse PATH ID` holds today's reader body, path-parameterised.
  - `_ws_tmproot_witness_read ID` calls it, and its contract and every answer are unchanged (pinned by the existing reader table).
  - "A parseable aside" then means exactly "it would read sound as the witness after the restore".
  - `_ws_tmproot_witness_read` is not in R38's function list; its behaviour is unchanged. The brief confirms that the consent covers it, or the coordinator rules.
- **P11 — The audit names the aside path.** When the judged witness is an aside (`_WS_COLLECT_ASIDE` set), each of the THREE `witness-mismatch` details in `_ws_collect_eval` that speaks of the witness names the aside's path in its place: the no-birth-time detail ("the witness of $id records no birth time"), the link-or-not-a-directory detail ("…the directory its witness names") and the identity detail ("…its witness names"). The uncut `REAP_DETAIL` carries the path. No claim is made about the 300-byte cut: the identity detail leads with the leaf's path and two dev:ino values, so the aside path may fall past it in a journal row.
- **P12 — The kept-leaf clause.** Its words are R17's: "The collector found nothing at ~/.cc-tmp/<id> and dropped its witness; if ~/.cc-tmp is a mount, check that it is mounted." When the witness-only arm's compare kept a newer witness, the clause says "dropped its witness" of a witness it left. That is a stated residual, `absent-clause-names-a-drop-the-compare-kept`, and no extra key is added. When an item the list already holds has the id, the leaf item yields to it whole (today's merge), and the clause is not carried as a second clause, as the clips clause is. That makes two stated residuals, one per arm, each pinned as it stands in Task 13: `found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-collector-item` (a collector item holds the id) and `found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-reclaim-item` (a reclaim item holds it: terminal, failing, stuck, kept, or a kept-many member).

Each gains `foundNothing: false` and nothing else, as P4 and P5 ask.
- **P14 — Boundary entries the rulings imply but R40 does not name.** `ccd-child-tmproot-witness-drop.test.ts` and `ccd-child-tmproot-witness.test.ts` (R3, R6, R7: the pins that assert today's window and warn text are rewritten); `collectRaceFixture.ts` (R30's fence, R32's reshape); `ccd-review-335-pins.test.ts` (R31); `lifecycle-wire.test.ts` (P5); `child-reclaim-leaf-kept-prose.test.ts` (P4); `collect-attention.test.ts` (P13); `server/src/watch.ts` (P2); and the WS-AUDIT-COLLECT header's two in-place rewordings (Tasks 6 and 10), so the comment says what the code then does. The brief confirms each.

The helper calls it with `2>/dev/null` and composes its own reason from `_WS_CAD` and a look at the witness's name, so R6 holds with the reason intact. ## Review Focus (the five failure modes most likely to bite)

1. **A removal still crosses a mount.**
   - Input: a fake mountinfo line at or under each of: the clips leaf and the temp leaf (directly and through the real reclaim tail), a collector slot's leaf, a standing nested checkout, the child's workdir (also through a symlinked ancestor and a `//` spelling), and an archived worktree. Also an unreadable table, an empty table, a line that is not a mount, and a sibling `<dir>-x`. Task 4's case 4b builds the table line that is not a mount, and Task 5's C6 builds the `//` workdir through the real tail.
   - Expected:
     - the leaf answers unmeasured, and the modes inside the "mount" are untouched, because the first ask precedes the owner bits and normalise;
     - through the tail, the clips or temp leaf is kept `unmeasured` (`clipsKept`/`tmpRootKept`), with the leaf and its witness standing;
     - a worktree fails `worktree-remove-failed` before `keep_of`, with the breadcrumb and the tree kept;
     - the collector answers `failed quarantine-kept`, with its record and slot kept;
     - on Darwin, nothing is asked and the removals happen as today.
2. **A witness dies on an unproven absence, beside a slot, or over a newer generation.**
   - Input, at each of the three callers: a device mismatch; an unreadable device; a `~/.cc-tmp` deleted whole; a standing slot or record; an unlistable quarantine; a `tmproots/` that cannot be searched (its witness reads `-e` false); a leaf standing again; a witness replaced between the read and the drop (with and without a failed move-back). Each with and without `mv --no-copy`, and on simulated Darwin.
   - Expected: kept or unmeasured; `tmpRootKept` is `unmeasured` with the reason; the witness is byte-identical or is the newer one; nothing on stderr from the helper; no `|| :` on any drop.
3. **A kept-leaf item ends too early, or never.**
   - Input: `leaf=removed`; `leaf=absent`; no key in an uncut row; a cut row that kept `leaf`; a cut row without it; `leaf=7`; `leaf="gone"`; a `measJson` that does not parse; a last-resort line; a clips-only source with `absent`; monotone mixes in both orders; a stored `"leaf":null`; a `"meas":7` line.
   - Expected, in order: end; keep with the clause; end; decided by the word; keep; keep; keep; keep; decided by the word; no clause; any end wins whatever its place; end (the departure `present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy`); end (the residual `non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless`).
4. **C5 admits junk, or races.**
   - Input: one parseable aside; two asides; a malformed aside; an aside naming another id; an aside beside an equal witness, beside a newer witness, and beside a witness of a different body; an old-generation aside beside a new leaf; a writer racing the `link`; a crash between `link` and `rm`; a server name `.<id>.drop.x`; ambiguity beside a registry row; the pause standing.
   - Expected, in order: admit and restore; unmeasured `aside`, no lock; the same; the same; unlink; leave and warn; leave and warn; terminal `witness-mismatch` naming the aside; left, never clobbered; the next settle unlinks; not admitted; `registered`; nothing moves.
   - `ccd-ws-collect-order.test.ts`'s aside pin stays green.
5. **Something moves that a census or a sibling programme reads.**
   - Input: the whole diff.
   - Expected:
     - the five citation passes are green at `'ccd/ccd': 147`, with no number edited;
     - README's and plan-a's `shared/api.ts` anchors and plan-a's `journalparse.ts` anchor still resolve;
     - the `archived-expiry-policy` site census, `ccd-refusal-scan`, `ccd-child-reclaim-tail-contained`'s six, `macos-platform`, the registry glob/find census, `ccd-wsaudit-nonpoison` and `ccd-collect-header-prose` are all unchanged;
     - `collect-readers` moved by `aside` alone, `ccd-id-cap` by one row, and `id-argv-census` by R42's three edits (the docstring, the `collector-learn-gate` entry and its name in the `collectAudit` row);
     - ws-expire changes only by the consented refusals and kept words;
     - R89's reads are untouched;
     - the Linux-without-`--no-copy` box and Darwin behave as R1 rules.

## Execution order and dependencies

Task 0 → 1 → 2 → … → 17, strictly serial.
- Tasks 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 each edit and restamp `ccd/ccd`.
- Each task is one commit, and every commit leaves every suite it touches green.
- The TR12 fence (Task 3) is re-run after Tasks 6, 7, 8, 10 and 11.
- **Tasks 10 and 11 are one deployable unit.** Between their commits, a verb given the right token for an aside-only id judges the aside, runs the witness-only arm against an absent live name, writes `done` with witness `absent`, and leaves the aside, so the id would loop. The wave ships as one PR and no intermediate commit is ever deployed; Task 11's cases 1 to 3 are the pins that red if the settle is missing. No interim code is written.

## Interfaces (canonical)

Every name the tasks share. A later task uses exactly these names and contracts.

### `ccd/ccd` (the fleet box's executor; outside the server's rings)

**`_ws_collect_floor_s`** (Task 1). The contract is unchanged: rc 0 with the floor on stdout, or rc 2 with nothing printed and `_WS_FLOOR_WHY` set. One line changes, in place, and the capture's status is read, so a capture that fails answers that rc 2 rather than a silent 86400 (R28):
```bash
    [[ "$o" =~ ^0*([1-9][0-9]*)?$ ]] || { _WS_FLOOR_WHY="WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S could not be read by its capture, so the raised floor it asks for was never read"; return 2; }; o="${BASH_REMATCH[1]:-0}"
```

**`_ws_leaf_read_small FILE`** (Task 2).
- rc is unchanged: 0, 1 (not a regular file, or unreadable) or 2 (over 4096 bytes).
- It sets `_WS_SMALL`, as today, and the new global `_WS_SMALL_NUL`:
  - `inner`: a NUL stands before a byte that is not NUL, CR or LF;
  - `trailing`: every NUL is in the file's closing run of NUL, CR and LF bytes;
  - `''`: the file holds no NUL.
- Both globals are `''` on every return other than 0, and both are reset on entry.
- The NUL map is a second bounded read: `head -c 4096 | tr -c '\000\r\n' 'x' | tr '\000\r\n' 'Nrr'`, with a sentinel, then `[[ $m =~ N.*x ]]` gives `inner` and `[[ $m == *N* ]]` gives `trailing`.

**`_ws_leaf_checkout_one`'s back-link** (Task 2). Directly after `_ws_leaf_read_small "$adp/gitdir"` succeeds, and before `rec="$_WS_SMALL"`:
```bash
  [[ "$_WS_SMALL_NUL" != inner ]] \
    || { _WS_CHECKOUTS_WHY="$adp/gitdir holds a NUL byte inside the path it names — git never writes one, so it is not git's record of the tree at $d"; return 1; }
```

**`_ws_removal_mounts_clear DIR [resolve]`** (Task 4; RECLAIM region, directly above `_ws_leaf_remove`).
- rc 0: nothing is mounted at DIR or under it, or the box is Darwin (never asked, by design: path-identity spec §3.5).
- rc 2 (`_WS_MOUNTS_WHY`): a mount point stands at DIR or under it; or the kernel's table could not be read whole; or, with `resolve`, DIR could not be resolved.
- It never answers 1. Prints nothing.
- Its first CODE line, after the header's `#` lines, is the Darwin guard.
```bash
_ws_removal_mounts_clear() {   # dir [resolve] -> 0 nothing is mounted at dir or under it — on Darwin, never asked (spec
  #                                §3.5); 2 (_WS_MOUNTS_WHY) one is, the table could not be read whole, or (resolve) dir
  #                                could not be resolved. Never 1: every caller refuses both alike
  [[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || return 0
  local d="${1-}"
  if [[ -n "${2-}" ]]; then
    _ws_dir_physical "$d" \
      || { _WS_MOUNTS_WHY="$d cannot be resolved ($_WS_PHYS_WHY), so whether anything is mounted under it was never asked"; return 2; }
    d="$_WS_PHYS"
  fi
  [[ "$d" != //[!/]* ]] || d="${d#/}"   # Linux reads `//x` as `/x`, and the kernel's table never writes `//`
  _ws_collect_mounts_clear "$d" && return 0
  return 2
}
```

**`_ws_leaf_remove`'s two asks** (Task 4). Each is a two-line statement.
- Ask 1, directly after the st_dev compare's `|| { …ccd never removes a mount"; return 1; }` and before the owner-bits `find … chmod u+rwx`:
  `_ws_removal_mounts_clear "$leaf" || { _WS_LEAF_WHY="$_WS_MOUNTS_WHY — nothing under $leaf was removed"; return 2; }`
- Ask 2, directly before `if [[ "$CCD_OS" == darwin ]]; then err=$(rm -rfx …`: the same statement.

**Tail step 3 and step 4 asks** (Task 5). Each ask is a two-line statement, and none of its lines spells "git" or "worktree remove".
- Step 3 (standing arm), around the existing `keep_of` and forced-remove pairs:
  `_ws_removal_mounts_clear "$cpath" || { _ws_reclaim_fail "$id" "$lctx" worktree-remove-failed "$_WS_MOUNTS_WHY — the checkout at $cpath stands, and nothing further was deleted"; return 1; }`
  It goes directly before `_ws_reclaim_contained _ws_reclaim_keep_of "$main" "$id" tree "$cpath"`, and again directly before `wtout=$(… --force "$cpath" …`.
- Step 4 (inside `if [[ -d "$workdir" ]]; then`): `_ws_removal_mounts_clear "$workdir" resolve || { _ws_reclaim_fail … worktree-remove-failed "$_WS_MOUNTS_WHY — the tree at $workdir stands, and nothing further was deleted"; return 1; }`. It goes directly before the `keep_of` of `$workdir`, and again directly before the forced remove.

**`_ws_tmproot_witness_drop ID`** (Task 6; replaces today's body; RECLAIM region).
- rc 0 complete: `_WS_WDROP` is `dropped` (exactly the parsed generation was unlinked) or `absent` (no witness stood, PROVEN by `_ws_reclaim_absent`, never read off a failed test).
- rc 1 kept (`_WS_WDROP_WHY`): a quarantine slot of ID stands; a leaf stands again at `~/.cc-tmp/ID` (P8); a newer generation stands (or a generation this tail did not read could not be moved back from its compare-and-drop aside); or ID is no witness's name.
- rc 2 unmeasured (`_WS_WDROP_WHY`): no witness was read, but its absence could not be proven (a `tmproots/` this process cannot search reads `-e` false); the witness does not parse (a linked `tmproots/` included); the device answers 1 or 2; the quarantine cannot be listed; the absence re-proof answers 2; or the compare could not finish.
- It prints nothing (R6). It shadows with `local`: `_WS_WIT_DEV _WS_WIT_INO _WS_WIT_BTIME _WS_WIT_RUN _WS_WIT_UID _WS_WIT_AT _WS_CAD _WS_CAD_WHY` and `-a _WS_QSLOTS`.
- The order is fixed: id → read (rc 1 is `absent`, complete, only once `_ws_reclaim_absent "$w"` PROVES it; otherwise rc 2) → parse failure (rc 2) → `_ws_collect_root_dev "$dev"` → `_ws_collect_slots_of` → `_ws_reclaim_absent "$HOME/.cc-tmp/$id"` → either `_ws_collect_mv_ok` and then `_ws_collect_witness_cad … 2>/dev/null` with the first read's fields (P15), or the R1 fallback:
  - re-read;
  - if the witness is now absent, PROVEN by `_ws_reclaim_absent "$w"`: `absent`, rc 0 (not proven: rc 2);
  - if it no longer parses: rc 2;
  - if any of the six fields differs: rc 1;
  - otherwise `rm -f -- "$w"` and prove it absent: `dropped`, or rc 2.
- On the compare-and-drop path, `_WS_CAD=kept` is rc 1, and its reason is chosen by a look at the witness's name: `_ws_reclaim_absent "$w"` answering 0 means the move-back failed ("its witness was kept: a generation this tail did not read could not be moved back from its compare-and-drop aside, where it stands, so nothing stands at its name ($w)"); otherwise "its witness was kept: a newer generation stands at $w".
- Every reason begins "its witness was kept: " and names its cause before any path. A path, or a reused reason that leads with one (`_WS_ROOTDEV_WHY`, `_WS_QSLOTS_WHY`, `_WS_ABSENT_WHY`, `_WS_CAD_WHY`), comes after the cause, in parentheses (Task 6).

**`_ws_tmproot_remove ID [DEVINO]`** (Task 6).
- rc 0: the leaf was removed or PROVEN absent, AND the drop is complete.
- rc 1: the leaf was refused.
- rc 2 (`_WS_LEAF_WHY`): the leaf is unmeasured, or the drop answered 1 or 2. In the second case `_WS_LEAF_WHY="no leaf stands, but $_WS_WDROP_WHY"` (decisive words first, and true of both meanings of the leaf half's rc 0, removed or PROVEN absent; it is step 6's own lead; the path is already in the done row's `temp root <path> kept (…)` prefix).
- Its tail is `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop "$id" && return 0`, then that reason, then `return 2`.

**Step 6's two kept arms** (Task 7). `wdrc` joins the tail's locals line. Both arms' `0)` read:
```bash
         0) _ws_tmproot_witness_drop "$id"; wdrc=$?   # no leaf stands: its witness goes only on a COMPLETE drop
            (( wdrc == 0 )) || { tmpkept=unmeasured; tmpwhy=$(_ws_leaf_why_line "no leaf stands, but $_WS_WDROP_WHY"); } ;;
```

**C5 names** (Task 8):
```bash
_ws_tmproot_aside_path() { local id="${1-}" pid="${2-}"; printf '%s' "$REG/tmproots/.${id}.drop.${pid}"; }   # id pid -> an aside's path (a path, not a decision)
_ws_tmproot_witness_parse PATH ID   # -> 0 parsed (sets _WS_WIT_*) | 1 absent | 2 unreadable or malformed: today's reader body,
                                    #    path-parameterised: a linked parent, not a regular file, >512 bytes, no single LF,
                                    #    an id= that is not ID, or a bad run each answer 2; every field cleared first
_ws_tmproot_witness_read ID         # -> unchanged: `_ws_tmproot_id_ok "$id" || return 2`, then the parse of its witness file
_ws_collect_aside_id NAME           # -> 0 with _WS_ASIDE_ID = the id a `.<id>.drop.<pid>` name is for; 1 otherwise.
                                    #    `local LC_ALL=C re='^\.(.+)\.drop\.([0-9]+)$'` (ONE re='…' in the body), then
                                    #    `_ws_tmproot_id_ok` on the capture
_WS_ASIDES=(); _WS_ASIDES_WHY=''
_ws_collect_asides_of ID            # -> 0 with _WS_ASIDES = every path in $REG/tmproots whose name parses EXACTLY to ID
                                    #    (none when tmproots/ is PROVEN absent); 2 (_WS_ASIDES_WHY) when ID is no id an
                                    #    aside is named for, or tmproots/ is a link, not a directory, or cannot be listed.
                                    #    Two `_plat_mktemp` scratch files, removed. The listing is ONE line:
                                    #    find -P "$REG/tmproots" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*.drop.*' -print0
```
`_ws_collect_witness_cad`'s `aside="${w%/*}/.$id.drop.$BASHPID"` becomes `aside=$(_ws_tmproot_aside_path "$id" "$me")`, with `me="$BASHPID"` read on its `local` line (a `"$BASHPID"` inside the command substitution would be the subshell's pid).

**C5 admission** (Task 10; WS-AUDIT-COLLECT block, directly above `_ws_collect_witness_judge`):
```bash
_WS_COLLECT_ASIDE=''   # the aside a judge read as the witness; cleared by `_ws_collect_reset`
_ws_collect_aside_judge ID   # -> 0 the id's ONE aside parses as its witness (_WS_WIT_* set from it; _WS_COLLECT_ASIDE = its
                             #    path); 1 none stands (nothing set); 2 the answer is set: unmeasured `witness` (the asides
                             #    could not be listed) or unmeasured `aside` (two or more stand, or the one does not parse
                             #    as a witness of ID). Reads only; takes no lock; prints nothing
```
- The `aside` answer is spelled as a literal call, `_ws_collect_unmeasured aside "…"`, so `collect-readers.test.ts`'s `probesFromCcd` (which reads `_ws_collect_unmeasured <word>` literals) sees it.
- `_ws_collect_witness_judge` (Option X): on read rc 1 it calls the aside judge. 0 → `return 0`; 2 → `return 1` (the answer is set); 1 → today's `not-witnessed`, byte for byte.
- `_ws_collect_prelock`: `_ws_tmproot_witness_read "$id" && return 0` becomes the read, then (rc 1 only) the aside judge (0 → `return 0`; on any other answer, `_ws_collect_reset`, so no answer it set outlives the peek: `prelock-resets-a-pre-peek-aside-answer`, Task 10), then today's peek and judgement, unchanged. Ambiguity therefore answers only after the peek (R23). Its header's scratch-file count becomes "up to six" (the records listing's two, the pre-peek aside judge's two, and the witness judge's Option X two when the peek proves no row).
- `_ws_collect_audit_contained`'s population: after the records listing, while `! inpop`, `_ws_collect_asides_of`. rc 2 gives unmeasured `witness` and the document. A non-empty list sets `inpop=1`.
- `cmd_ws_collect`'s population: the `not-witnessed` refusal also requires no aside. An aside listing that fails, with no witness and no record, joins the existing records-listing `probe-unmeasured` statement with its own text (P6): "no lock was taken, and nothing was moved or removed: no witness stands for $id, and its compare-and-drop asides could not be listed ($_WS_ASIDES_WHY) — the witness's path is $wf". The records arm's text is byte-identical.
- `server/src/collectLane.ts`: `aside: 'per-leaf'`.

**`_ws_tmproot_aside_settle ID`** (Task 11; RECLAIM region, directly below `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop`).
- rc 0, with `_WS_ASIDE_DID` one of:
  - `none`: no aside stands;
  - `restored`: the sole parseable aside was linked to the absent witness name, proven the same dev:ino, then unlinked;
  - `unlinked`: every aside equals the standing witness (same dev:ino, or byte-equal), and each was unlinked;
  - `left`: at least one aside was left, and `_WS_ASIDE_WHY` names each and why.
- rc 2 (`_WS_ASIDE_WHY`): unmeasured. The asides could not be listed; the witness's absence could not be measured; with no witness, two or more asides stand or the one does not parse; `link` is unavailable or failed with no witness standing after; or a restored aside could not be unlinked.
- THE CALLER HOLDS `$REG/.reap-<id>.lock`. It prints nothing (P9), and shadows `_WS_WIT_*` and `_WS_ASIDES`.
- When the `link` fails because a witness now stands, or when the dev:ino proof fails, it runs the witness-stands arm once.

**`meas.leaf`** (Task 12). The emit lines change in place:
- `_ws_collect_witness_only`'s `_lc_done collect … meas.resumed "" meas.leaf absent \`;
- `_ws_collect_finish`'s `_lc_done collect … meas.resumed "$resumed" meas.leaf removed \`.

`_lc_json`, in place and line-neutral:
- the meas rung: `ev["meas"] = {"leaf": meas["leaf"]} if "leaf" in meas else None; ev["truncated"] = True`;
- the last resort's literal line: `"dec": {"surface": ev["dec"].get("surface", "none")}, "truncated": True, **({"meas": {"leaf": meas["leaf"]}} if "leaf" in meas else {})}`.

### `shared/api.ts` (L0; declarations only)

In place, line-neutral:
- The last member line of `LifecycleMeas` becomes two lines: the `clipsKept` member (unchanged), then
  `  /** A \`collect\` \`done\`'s leaf (path-identity spec §3.4): see \`COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS\`, at the foot. */ readonly leaf: string | null;`
  The `tmpRootKept` docstring is rewrapped from seven lines to six, with its words unchanged.
- `LIFECYCLE_MEAS_KEY_MAP`'s line `unremoved: true, childOf: true, wip: true, residueBytes: true, tmpRootKept: true, clipsKept: true,` gains ` leaf: true,` on the same line.

Appended at the foot, after the last foot block:
```ts
/** What a `collect` `done` journals of the leaf it acted on (path-identity spec §3.4, TR1 A): `removed` on
 *  `_ws_collect_finish`'s line (the slot's leaf proven gone after this collection removed it), `absent` on the
 *  witness-only arm's (no leaf stood at the witness's path). Spelled ONCE, as a total table's keys. Not the audit
 *  document's `collect.leaf` (`present`/`absent`), which is another wire. APPENDED at the foot, never inserted above:
 *  README and the frozen spec and plan corpus cite this file by line. */
export type CollectLeafEndWord = 'removed' | 'absent';
const COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE: Readonly<Record<CollectLeafEndWord, true>> = { removed: true, absent: true };
export const COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS: readonly CollectLeafEndWord[] = Object.keys(COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE) as CollectLeafEndWord[];
export function isCollectLeafEndWord(v: unknown): v is CollectLeafEndWord {
  return typeof v === 'string' && (COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS as readonly string[]).includes(v);
```

The end decision, in `childReclaimLeafKept` (it replaces today's `collected` and `tmp` lines; the id and clock filter stays in front):
```ts
const reads = after.flatMap((e) => (e.act === LEAF_END_COLLECT ? [e.leaf] : []));
const ends = (x: ChildReclaimLeafEndRead): boolean => (x.kind === 'word' && x.word === 'removed') || x.kind === 'keyless';
const collected = reads.some(ends);
const tmpRead = childReclaimMirrorLeaf(r, 'tmpRootKept');
const tmp = collected && tmpRead.kind !== 'none-or-unreported' ? 'collected' as const : tmpRead;
const foundNothing = !collected && tmpRead.kind !== 'none-or-unreported'
  && reads.some((x) => x.kind === 'word' && x.word === 'absent');
```

```bash
REG="$HOME/.cc-sessions"; T=$(cd -P -- "$HOME/.cc-tmp" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
echo "tmp-resolved=$([ -n "$T" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
TD=$(stat -c %d -- "$T" 2>/dev/null); RD=$(stat -c %d -- "$REG" 2>/dev/null); echo "tmp-dev-equals-reg-dev=$([ "$TD" = "$RD" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
echo "witnesses=$(ls -A -- "$REG/tmproots/" 2>/dev/null | grep -vc '^\.')"
echo "tmproots-dotnames=$(ls -A -- "$REG/tmproots/" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^\.')"
echo "asides=$(ls -A -- "$REG/tmproots/" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^\..+\.drop\.[0-9]+$')"
for f in "$REG"/tmproots/[!.]*; do [ -f "$f" ] && { head -c 4096 -- "$f"; echo; }; done | awk -v d="$TD" '
  /^v=1 id=[^ ]+ run=[^ ]* dev=[0-9]+ ino=[0-9]+ btime=([1-9][0-9]*|-) uid=[0-9]+ at=[0-9]+$/ { v1++; for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i ~ /^dev=/) { split($i,a,"="); if (a[2]==d) same++ } ; next }
  NF { bad++ } END { printf "witness-v1=%d witness-dev-match=%d witness-unparsed=%d\n", v1, same, bad }'
echo "records=$(ls -A -- "$REG/tmpquarantine/" 2>/dev/null | grep -vc '^\.')"
echo "quarantine-dir=$([ -d "$T/.ccd-quarantine" ] && echo 1 || echo 0) slots=$(ls -A -- "$T/.ccd-quarantine/" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^slot\.')"
awk -v t="$T" -v w="$HOME/worktrees" '{ mp=$5; if (mp==t) tm++; else if (index(mp, t"/")==1) undertmp++;
  if (mp==w) wm++; else if (index(mp, w"/")==1) underwt++ } END { printf "tmp-is-mount=%d mounts-under-tmp=%d worktrees-is-mount=%d mounts-under-worktrees=%d\n", tm, undertmp, wm, underwt }' /proc/self/mountinfo
for f in "$REG"/*.workdir; do [ -f "$f" ] && { head -c 4096 -- "$f"; echo; }; done | awk 'NR==FNR{ if (NF) wd[$0]=1; next } { for (p in wd) if ($5==p || index($5, p"/")==1) hit++ } END { print "mounts-at-or-under-a-workdir=" hit+0 }' - /proc/self/mountinfo
echo "mountinfo-lines=$(wc -l < /proc/self/mountinfo)"
J=$(cat "$REG"/.lifecycle/journal-*.ndjson 2>/dev/null | grep -F '"act":"collect","outcome":"done"')
echo "collect-done=$(printf '%s' "$J" | grep -c .) collect-done-truncated=$(printf '%s' "$J" | grep -c '"truncated":true') collect-done-witness-only=$(printf '%s' "$J" | grep -c 'no leaf stood at')"
git --version; bash --version | head -1; LC_ALL=C rm --version 2>/dev/null | head -1; python3 --version
echo "mv-no-copy=$(LC_ALL=C mv --help 2>/dev/null | grep -c -- --no-copy)"
```

Mount points are compared as encoded text, exactly as `_ws_collect_mounts_clear` does. The awk is approximate for a path holding a space.

**STOP rule** (the grounding report's set). Any of these STOPs the wave, reported as counts, never names:
- `mounts-under-tmp>0`, `mounts-at-or-under-a-workdir>0` or `mounts-under-worktrees>0`, beyond the binds themselves. W2's new asks would hold those trees: correct, but it changes live outcomes, and the coordinator sees it first.
- `asides>0`: C5 would restore live asides on first contact.
- `slots>0` or `records>0`: TR4 would hold those witnesses.
- `witness-dev-match < witness-v1`: TR3 would hold them.
- `witness-unparsed>0`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test `server/test/ccd-collect-floor-linear.test.ts`**

```ts
// path-identity W2, TR7: the collector's idle floor knob strips its leading zeros with ONE regex capture (path-identity
// spec §3.6). `_ws_collect_floor_s` used to strip them with a pattern expansion, `${o%%[!0]*}`, which is quadratic in
// the knob's length: measured 43.3 s at 131,000 zeros. The anchored capture `^0*([1-9][0-9]*)?$` has exactly one
// parse (its group must begin with a digit that is not 0), so its answer does not depend on how a libc orders POSIX
// subexpression matches, and it runs in linear time. It answers what the old strip answered, so
// `ccd-collect-idle-token.test.ts`'s padded rows stand unedited.
//
// A timing-free row cannot go red when the quadratic strip comes back, because both forms give the same answer. So the
// MECHANISM is the structure pin on `type _ws_collect_floor_s`; the 200,000-zero rows pin correctness at scale. Each
// knob is built INSIDE the shell (`printf -v`): written into the snippet or the env, it would be one argv or env string
// longer than 131072 bytes, which the kernel refuses before ccd runs.
//
// FIXTURE HOMES ONLY (`makePrHarness`). Every case runs on every platform. Each reads rc, stdout, `_WS_FLOOR_WHY` and
// stderr in the CURRENT shell, so the global it reads is the one this call set.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-collect-floor-linear-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

interface Floor { rc: string; out: string; why: string; err: string; len: string }
/** `_ws_collect_floor_s` asked in the CURRENT shell after `setup`: its rc, its stdout, `_WS_FLOOR_WHY`, its stderr, and
 *  the knob's length as the function saw it (the control that the knob arrived whole). */
const floor = (setup: string): Floor => {
  const [rc = '', out = '', why = '', err = '', len = ''] = h.sh(`${setup}`
    + ' _ws_collect_floor_s >"$HOME/fl.out" 2>"$HOME/fl.err"; rc=$?;'
    + ' printf \'%s\\x1f%s\\x1f%s\\x1f%s\\x1f%s\' "$rc" "$(cat -- "$HOME/fl.out")" "$_WS_FLOOR_WHY" "$(cat -- "$HOME/fl.err")"'
    + ' "${#WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S}"').split('\x1f');
  return { rc, out, why, err, len };
};

describe('_ws_collect_floor_s, TR7 (path-identity spec §3.6)', () => {
  it('a knob of 200,000 leading zeros reads its significant digits', () => {
    for (const [tail, want] of [['172800', '172800'], ['', '86400'], ['1111111111', '999999999']] as const) {
      const got = floor(`printf -v z '%0*d' 200000 0; WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S="\${z}${tail}";`);
      expect(got.len, `the knob reached the function whole: 200,000 zeros, then ${JSON.stringify(tail)}`)
        .toBe(String(200_000 + tail.length));
      expect({ rc: got.rc, out: got.out, why: got.why, err: got.err }, `200,000 zeros, then ${JSON.stringify(tail)}`)
        .toEqual({ rc: '0', out: want, why: '', err: '' });
    }
  });

  it('the strip is one capture, never a pattern expansion', () => {
    const body = h.sh('type _ws_collect_floor_s');
    expect(body, 'the CONTROL: `type` printed the function').toContain('WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S');
    expect(body).toContain('BASH_REMATCH[1]:-0');
    expect(body).toContain('^0*([1-9][0-9]*)?$');
    expect(body, 'the capture’s status is read: a capture that fails answers 2, never a silent 86400')
      .toMatch(/\^0\*\(\[1-9\]\[0-9\]\*\)\?\$ \]\] \|\| \{\s*_WS_FLOOR_WHY="WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S could not be read by its capture/);
    expect(body, 'the quadratic strip is gone').not.toMatch(/%%\[!0\]\*/);
  });

  it('a knob that is not a whole number still answers 2, and the anchored capture never sees it', () => {
    for (const k of ['0x10', '00 1']) {
      const got = floor(`WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S='${k}';`);
      expect({ rc: got.rc, out: got.out, err: got.err }, `knob ${JSON.stringify(k)}`).toEqual({ rc: '2', out: '', err: '' });
      expect(got.why, `knob ${JSON.stringify(k)}`).toContain('not a whole number');
    }
  });
});
```

```bash
    [[ "$o" =~ ^0*([1-9][0-9]*)?$ ]] || { _WS_FLOOR_WHY="WS_COLLECT_IDLE_FLOOR_S could not be read by its capture, so the raised floor it asks for was never read"; return 2; }; o="${BASH_REMATCH[1]:-0}"
```

- The `^[0-9]+$` validation directly above stays, so the capture matches whenever the regex engine runs. Its status is still read (R28, amended after review): a failed `=~` empties `BASH_REMATCH`, and `${BASH_REMATCH[1]:-0}` would then read 0, a silent 86400 that drops the raise. The function's contract says "a raise asked for unreadably is unmeasured, never folded to 24 h", so that arm answers 2, nothing printed, `_WS_FLOOR_WHY` set. Only a regex-engine failure (memory exhaustion on a long knob) reaches it, so no value row drives it: the structure pin holds it, and T1.5 measures that pin.
- `BASH_REMATCH` was already overwritten by that validation, so no caller loses anything it read across the call. `_ws_collect_floor_read` and `_ws_collect_floor_held` read only their own variables.
- The header comment ("Its leading zeros are stripped first … the clamp is asked of the LENGTH of what is left") stays as it is. It is still true.

**Model routing:** `opus`, effort `high`. `_ws_leaf_remove` reaches this code, so the task changes ws-expire's tail verdict for such a leaf from rc 0 or rc 2 to rc 1. That is a consent surface (R38).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test `server/test/ccd-leaf-nul-backlink.test.ts`**

```ts
// path-identity W2, TR8: a back-link with a NUL INSIDE the path it names is refused (path-identity spec §3.6).
// `_ws_leaf_read_small` reads each NUL as a newline, so a hand-made admin `gitdir` back-link whose NUL sat at the
// offset of a newline in the `.git` path read as that path, and `_ws_leaf_checkout_one` accepted the tree as the
// leaf's own. Git never writes a NUL. The reader now says where the NULs stood (`_WS_SMALL_NUL`: `inner`,
// `trailing` or ''), and a back-link with an inner one is refused, rc 1, before any compare. A trailing NUL stays a
// line end, and a NUL in the `.git` FILE stays unmeasured (rc 2), as before.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every leaf, admin directory and file is under the harness's HOME, written by
// hand; no git runs (git would never write these bytes), and ccd runs as SOURCED functions, never against the live
// HOME. The `${_WS_SMALL_NUL-}` reads are deliberate: before this wave the global does not exist and ccd runs under
// `set -u`, so a bare read would abort the snippet instead of answering. The source-time case pins the initialiser.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-leaf-nul-backlink-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const ID = 'demo-quiet-basin';
/** A path component holding one newline: a `.git` path under it holds one too. */
const NL = 'a\nb';
const rootOf = (): string => path.join(h.home, 'root');
const leafOf = (): string => path.join(rootOf(), ID);
/** The admin directory OUTSIDE the leaf that every tree here names. */
const admOf = (): string => path.join(h.home, 'adm', 'wt');

interface Answer { rc: string; why: string }
/** The checkout question's own answer: its rc and `_WS_CHECKOUTS_WHY`. */
const ask = (leaf: string): Answer => {
  const [rc = '', why = ''] = h.sh(`_ws_leaf_checkouts "${leaf}"; rc=$?;`
    + ' printf \'%s\\x1f%s\' "$rc" "$_WS_CHECKOUTS_WHY"').split('\x1f');
  return { rc, why };
};
/** The removal helper's answer: its rc and `_WS_LEAF_WHY`. */
const remove = (root: string, id: string): Answer => {
  const [rc = '', why = ''] = h.sh(`_ws_leaf_remove "${root}" "${id}"; rc=$?;`
    + ' printf \'%s\\x1f%s\' "$rc" "$_WS_LEAF_WHY"').split('\x1f');
  return { rc, why };
};
/** After a `_ws_leaf_read_small` call: its rc, `_WS_SMALL_NUL`, and `_WS_SMALL` with each newline shown as N. */
const SHOW = ' rc=$?; printf \'%s\\x1f%s\\x1f%s\' "$rc" "${_WS_SMALL_NUL-}" "${_WS_SMALL//$\'\\n\'/N}"';
const readOf = (f: string, pre = ''): string[] => h.sh(`${pre} _ws_leaf_read_small "${f}";${SHOW}`).split('\x1f');
/** `head` failing on its Nth call in this shell, after writing a partial line. The content read is the 1st call and
 *  the NUL map the 2nd, so a read that fails part-way is reached with no fault in the file system. Each call is
 *  logged to `$HOME/head-calls`: the pipeline runs it in a subshell, so a shell variable would not count it. */
const HEAD_FAILS_AT = (n: number): string => `FAIL_AT=${n}; head() { local k; echo x >> "$HOME/head-calls";`
  + ' k=$(wc -l < "$HOME/head-calls"); if (( k == FAIL_AT )); then printf partial; return 1; fi; command head "$@"; };';

/** A tree at `<leaf>/<sub>/wt` whose `.git` FILE names the admin directory outside the leaf, `<HOME>/adm/wt`, whose
 *  `gitdir` back-link is `backlink(f)`; `f` is the physical `.git` path the walk lists. Written by hand. Returns `f`. */
const linked = (sub: string, backlink: (f: string) => string): string => {
  const wt = path.join(leafOf(), sub, 'wt');
  fs.mkdirSync(wt, { recursive: true });
  fs.mkdirSync(admOf(), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, '.git'), `gitdir: ${admOf()}\n`);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, 'precious.txt'), 'work of the tree\n');
  const f = path.join(fs.realpathSync(leafOf()), sub, 'wt', '.git');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(admOf(), 'gitdir'), backlink(f));
  return f;
};
/** The refusal's reason, uncut, for the tree whose `.git` is `f`. */
const nulWhy = (f: string): string => `${admOf()}/gitdir holds a NUL byte inside the path it names — git never writes one,`
  + ` so it is not git's record of the tree at ${path.dirname(f)}`;

describe('_ws_leaf_read_small says where the NULs stood (path-identity spec §3.6)', () => {
  it.each([
    ['a line with no NUL', 'gitdir: /a\n', '', 'gitdir: /aN'],
    ['a trailing NUL', '/a\0', 'trailing', '/aN'],
    ['a newline, then a NUL', '/a\n\0', 'trailing', '/aNN'],
    ['a NUL, then CR LF', '/a\0\r\n', 'trailing', '/aN\rN'],
    ['a NUL inside the line', '/a\0b\n', 'inner', '/aNbN'],
    ['a leading NUL', '\0/a', 'inner', 'N/a'],
    ['NULs alone', '\0\0', 'trailing', 'NN'],
    ['an empty file', '', '', ''],
  ] as const)('the NUL map of %s', (_what, body, nul, small) => {
    const f = path.join(h.home, 'small');
    fs.writeFileSync(f, body);
    expect(readOf(f), 'rc, _WS_SMALL_NUL, and _WS_SMALL with each newline shown as N').toEqual(['0', nul, small]);
  }, 60_000);

  it.each([
    ['2, over 4096 bytes', 'big', '2'],
    ['1, a directory', 'dir', '1'],
    ['1, no such file', 'gone', '1'],
  ] as const)('a read that answers %s after an inner NUL leaves both globals empty', (_what, second, rc) => {
    const inner = path.join(h.home, 'inner');
    fs.writeFileSync(inner, '/a\0b\n');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'big'), 'a'.repeat(5000));
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'dir'));
    const out = h.sh(`_ws_leaf_read_small "${inner}"; a="\${_WS_SMALL_NUL-}"; _ws_leaf_read_small "${path.join(h.home, second)}"; rc=$?;`
      + ' printf \'%s|%s|%s|%s\' "$a" "$rc" "${_WS_SMALL_NUL-}" "$_WS_SMALL"');
    expect(out, 'the CONTROL (the first read said inner), then no stale value on the second').toBe(`inner|${rc}||`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('_WS_SMALL_NUL is defined once ccd is sourced, so a reader under `set -u` never meets an unbound name', () => {
    expect(h.sh('printf \'[%s]\' "$_WS_SMALL_NUL"')).toBe('[]');
  }, 60_000);

  it.each([
    ['the content read', 1],
    ['the NUL map', 2],
  ] as const)('a read that fails part-way answers 1 with both globals empty: %s', (_what, n) => {
    const f = path.join(h.home, 'small');
    fs.writeFileSync(f, '/a\0b\n');
    expect(readOf(f, HEAD_FAILS_AT(n)), 'rc 1, and no partial bytes left in _WS_SMALL').toEqual(['1', '', '']);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'head-calls'), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).length,
      'the CONTROL: the shim ran up to its failing call').toBe(n);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('a back-link with a NUL inside the path it names is refused (TR8)', () => {
  it('CONTROL: a literal back-link of a `.git` path holding a newline is the leaf’s own', () => {
    const f = linked(NL, (g) => `${g}\n`);
    expect(f.split('\n').length - 1, 'the CONTROL: the `.git` path holds exactly one newline').toBe(1);
    const a = ask(leafOf());
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
  }, 60_000);

  it('a NUL at the offset of the path’s newline — accepted before this wave — is refused', () => {
    const f = linked(NL, (g) => `${g.replace('\n', '\0')}\n`);
    expect(f.split('\n').length - 1, 'the CONTROL: the `.git` path holds exactly one newline').toBe(1);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(admOf(), 'gitdir'), 'utf8').replace('\0', '\n'),
      'the CONTROL: read with its NUL as a newline, the back-link IS the `.git` path').toBe(`${f}\n`);
    const a = ask(leafOf());
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.why).toBe(nulWhy(f));
  }, 60_000);

  it('a NUL elsewhere, in a path holding a newline, is refused — no longer unmeasured', () => {
    const f = linked(NL, (g) => `${g.replace('/wt/.git', '/w\0t/.git')}\n`);
    const a = ask(leafOf());
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.why).toBe(nulWhy(f));
  }, 60_000);

  it('a NUL elsewhere, in a path holding none, is refused for the NUL', () => {
    const f = linked('x', (g) => `${g.replace('/wt/.git', '/w\0t/.git')}\n`);
    const a = ask(leafOf());
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.why).toBe(nulWhy(f));
  }, 60_000);

  it.each([
    ['a NUL', (g: string) => `${g}\0`, '0', ''],
    ['a newline, then a NUL', (g: string) => `${g}\n\0`, '0', ''],
    ['a NUL, then CR LF', (g: string) => `${g}\0\r\n`, '1', 'which git records as'],
  ] as const)('a trailing NUL stays a line end: %s', (_what, backlink, rc, whyHas) => {
    linked('x', backlink);
    const a = ask(leafOf());
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe(rc);
    expect(a.why, 'never refused for the NUL').not.toContain('holds a NUL byte');
    expect(a.why, 'the CR is never stripped at the back-link: the compare refuses it').toContain(whyHas);
  }, 60_000);

  it('a `.git` FILE with an inner NUL stays unmeasured: the new flag is the back-link’s alone', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x', '.git'), 'gitdir: /x\0/y\n');
    const a = ask(leafOf());
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`${leafOf()}/x/.git is not one 'gitdir: <path>' line — git cannot tell what it names, so neither can ccd`);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('_ws_leaf_remove keeps a leaf whose tree has such a back-link (the tail reaches it)', () => {
  it('a leaf holding a tree whose back-link has a NUL inside its path is refused, and every file stands', () => {
    const f = linked(NL, (g) => `${g.replace('\n', '\0')}\n`);
    const r = remove(rootOf(), ID);
    expect(r.rc, r.why).toBe('1');
    expect(r.why).toBe(`${nulWhy(f)} — nothing under ${leafOf()} was removed`);
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(leafOf(), NL, 'wt', 'precious.txt')), 'the tree’s work stands').toBe(true);
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(leafOf(), NL, 'wt', '.git'))).toBe(true);

    linked(NL, (g) => `${g}\0`);
```

**3a. The global and the reader, replaced whole.** Hint `:31570-31598`.

Before:
```bash
_WS_SMALL=''
_ws_leaf_read_small() {   # file -> 0 with _WS_SMALL = its bytes, each NUL read as a newline; 1 when it is
  #                            not a regular file or cannot be read; 2 when it holds more than 4096 bytes
  # A FILE READ AS A FILE, bounded: `-f` first (a FIFO would block), the size
  # before the bytes, and the read is the group's redirection (an unopenable file
  # answers 1). A NUL becomes a newline, never dropped. What an INNER one means
  # is each caller's: in the `.git` file it splits the line, unmeasured; in an
  # admin directory's `gitdir` back-link it leaves a newline in the text that is
  # compared with the `.git` path, so the tree is refused when that path holds no
  # newline, accepted when the NUL sits at the offset of a newline the path does
  # hold (a hand-crafted file: git writes no NUL), and unmeasured otherwise
  # (the corner is the path-identity programme's). A TRAILING one is a line
  # end each caller strips, so `gitdir: A\0` and `gitdir: A\n\0` both read as
  # A. Git reads the second as `A\n` and fails; ccd answers measured, safely:
  # an A inside the leaf passes before any back-link is read (removing the leaf
  # removes all of it), and outside the leaf only a tree git back-links passes
  # (`_ws_leaf_checkout_one` says which back-links count).
  local f="$1" sz
  _WS_SMALL=''
  [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 1
  { sz=$(LC_ALL=C wc -c < "$f"); } 2>/dev/null || return 1
  sz="${sz//[!0-9]/}"
  [[ -n "$sz" ]] || return 1
  (( 10#$sz <= 4096 )) || return 2
  { _WS_SMALL=$( { LC_ALL=C head -c 4096 | LC_ALL=C tr '\000' '\n'; } < "$f" && printf x); } 2>/dev/null || return 1
  [[ "$_WS_SMALL" == *x ]] || { _WS_SMALL=''; return 1; }
  _WS_SMALL="${_WS_SMALL%x}"
  return 0
}
```
After:
```bash
_WS_SMALL=''; _WS_SMALL_NUL=''
_ws_leaf_read_small() {   # file -> 0 with _WS_SMALL = its bytes, each NUL read as a newline, and _WS_SMALL_NUL
  #                            = `inner` (a NUL stands before a byte that is not NUL, CR or LF), `trailing` (every
  #                            NUL is in the file's closing run of NUL, CR and LF bytes) or '' (it holds none); 1
  #                            when it is not a regular file or cannot be read; 2 when it holds more than 4096
  #                            bytes. On 1 and 2, _WS_SMALL and _WS_SMALL_NUL are both ''
  # A FILE READ AS A FILE, bounded: `-f` first (a FIFO would block), the size
  # before the bytes, and the read is the group's redirection (an unopenable file
  # answers 1). A NUL becomes a newline, never dropped, and where the NULs stood
  # is reported beside the bytes (path-identity spec §3.6). What an INNER one
  # means is each caller's: in the `.git` file it splits the line, unmeasured;
  # in an admin directory's `gitdir` back-link it is refused
  # (`_ws_leaf_checkout_one`): git never writes one, and read as a newline it
  # would let a hand-made back-link read as a `.git` path holding a newline at
  # its offset. A TRAILING one is a line end each caller strips, so
  # `gitdir: A\0` and `gitdir: A\n\0` both read as A. Git reads the second as
  # `A\n` and fails; ccd answers measured, safely: an A inside the leaf passes
  # before any back-link is read (removing the leaf removes all of it), and
  # outside the leaf only a tree git back-links passes (`_ws_leaf_checkout_one`
  # says which back-links count).
  # THE NUL MAP is the same bounded read again, each NUL read as N, each CR or
  # LF as r and every other byte as x, so where the NULs stood is a question
  # about a string the shell can hold (it holds no NUL): an N before an x is an
  # inner NUL. A regex, never a two-star glob, so 4096 bytes match in linear
  # time; its `=~` overwrites BASH_REMATCH, which no caller reads across this
  # call. It is a SECOND read: a writer between the two can only make the map
  # say inner (refused, safely), or miss a NUL the first read already turned
  # into a newline, and that back-link is then compared exactly as before.
  # A read that fails part-way leaves both globals '' (the contract above).
  local f="$1" sz m
  _WS_SMALL=''; _WS_SMALL_NUL=''
  [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 1
  { sz=$(LC_ALL=C wc -c < "$f"); } 2>/dev/null || return 1
  sz="${sz//[!0-9]/}"
  [[ -n "$sz" ]] || return 1
  (( 10#$sz <= 4096 )) || return 2
  { _WS_SMALL=$( { LC_ALL=C head -c 4096 | LC_ALL=C tr '\000' '\n'; } < "$f" && printf x); } 2>/dev/null || { _WS_SMALL=''; return 1; }
  [[ "$_WS_SMALL" == *x ]] || { _WS_SMALL=''; return 1; }
  _WS_SMALL="${_WS_SMALL%x}"
  { m=$( { LC_ALL=C head -c 4096 | LC_ALL=C tr -c '\000\r\n' 'x' | LC_ALL=C tr '\000\r\n' 'Nrr'; } < "$f" && printf .); } 2>/dev/null \
    || { _WS_SMALL=''; return 1; }
  [[ "$m" == *. ]] || { _WS_SMALL=''; return 1; }
  m="${m%.}"
  if [[ "$m" =~ N.*x ]]; then _WS_SMALL_NUL=inner
  elif [[ "$m" == *N* ]]; then _WS_SMALL_NUL=trailing; fi
  return 0
}
```
