- [ ] **Step 1: Write the fence, `server/test/ccd-collect-race-spawn-late.test.ts`**

```ts
// path-identity W2 (TR12 B; path-identity spec §3.9): six LATE recycled-spawn boundaries of the collector, forced
// through the real verb. `ccd-collect-race-spawn.test.ts` forces a spawn on the recycled slug before the move and at
// `moved`, `proven` and `removed`. Review 369's C1 built thirteen later boundaries through the verb and measured each
// safe, and none was pinned. This file pins six of them, one for each guard that alone keeps the new child whole:
//   a fresh collection's `emptied`: the compare-and-drop, fed the record's fields;
//   its `witnessed`: the temp-file reap, which waits for a free slug;
//   its `dropped`: the next audit's registry rung;
//   the putback's `restoring`: the restore's NOREPLACE rename, behind a doubt that is not the registry;
//   the witness-only arm's `witnessed`: the reap again, on the arm that makes no record;
//   a resume past `removed`, at its `emptied`: the compare-and-drop, on a path with no step 5 and no registry ask.
// At each one, a real `_child_tmpdir` hands the slug to a new child. Each case asserts what stands on disk afterwards:
// the new child's leaf and its witness, never touched.
// THESE ARE FENCES, NOT RED-FIRST TESTS. C1 measured every one of these paths safe on the code this file was written
// against, so no case was red before a fix: there is no fix here. Each case is proven by a mutation that deletes an
// EXISTING guard of ccd and is measured red (the path-identity W2 plan's table for this file). The compare-and-drop's
// own row is measured once the reclaim tail's generation-exact witness drop stands. The file is re-run after every
// later W2 change to the witness drop or to the compare-and-drop aside.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`collectRaceFixture.ts`, `makePrHarness`). Linux only, and only where `mv --no-copy` exists
// (child-workspace reclamation spec §5.10): anywhere else the collector moves nothing, so a case would measure
// nothing. Every audit and verb stubs the in-use probe (`COLLECT_STUBS`), so no case walks /proc. No case asserts
// `meas.leaf`: its own pins own that key.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { eventsOf } from './lifecycleHelpers.js';
import {
  COL_ID, DEAD_RUN, G2_RUN, LINUX, NO_COPY, collectAudit, collectVerb, crashAt, crashedAt, devinoOf, docOf, g2Departs,
  g2Row, g2Spawn, gapAt, gapErrorsOf, gapsOf, lastVerdict, leafOf, orphanLeaf, quarantineOf, recordsOf, regOf, settle,
  shownRounds, slotsOf, tokenOf, verdictOf, witnessField, witnessOf,
} from './collectRaceFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-collect-spawn-late-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

/** A recycled-slug spawn, whole: `ws-add`'s registry half, then `_child_tmpdir` and the new child's first scratch file. */
const SPAWN = `${g2Row()} && ${g2Spawn()}`;
/** The witness writer's dead temp file of this id: the exact shape `_ws_collect_reap_temps` removes while the slug
 *  reads free, planted two hours old (`ccd-ws-collect-order.test.ts`'s `plant()`). */
const AGED_TEMP = `.${COL_ID}.4242.17.tmp`;
const agedTempOf = (): string => path.join(regOf(h), 'tmproots', AGED_TEMP);
const plantAgedTemp = (): void => {
  const old = Date.now() / 1000 - 7200;
  fs.writeFileSync(agedTempOf(), 'x');
  fs.utimesSync(agedTempOf(), old, old);
};
/** The in-use probe answers "in use" once `$HOME/in-use` exists, and "nobody" before. It is placed AFTER
 *  `COLLECT_STUBS` (which `collectVerb` puts first), so it wins over their `NOBODY`. It walks no /proc. */
const INUSE_AFTER_FLAG = '_ws_path_users() { if [[ -e "$HOME/in-use" ]]; then _WS_PATH_USERS_PIDS=4242;'
  + ' _WS_PATH_USERS_WHY="process 4242 has its working directory at $1"; return 1; fi;'
  + " _WS_PATH_USERS_PIDS=''; _WS_PATH_USERS_WHY=''; return 0; };";
/** The compare-and-drop asides of this id (`.<id>.drop.<pid>`) in `tmproots/`: none may be left behind. */
const asidesOf = (): string[] => {
  const d = path.join(regOf(h), 'tmproots');
  return fs.existsSync(d) ? fs.readdirSync(d).filter((n) => n.startsWith(`.${COL_ID}.drop.`)) : [];
};
/** The new child's leaf and its witness stand, untouched: the leaf `_child_tmpdir` handed it, its scratch, and a
 *  witness for its run that names that leaf's inode. */
const newChildStands = (): void => {
  const leaf = leafOf(h);
  expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'g2-dir'), 'utf8'), 'the CONTROL: the spawn was handed the id-derived leaf')
    .toBe(leaf);
  expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(leaf, 'g2.txt'), 'utf8'), 'the new child\'s scratch stands').toBe('g2 scratch\n');
  expect(witnessField(h, 'run'), 'the new child\'s witness stands').toBe(G2_RUN);
  expect(witnessField(h, 'ino'), 'naming the new child\'s leaf').toBe(String(fs.lstatSync(leaf, { bigint: true }).ino));
};
/** The next audit refuses `registered` and offers no token: the new child holds the slug. */
const nextAuditRegistered = (what: string): void => {
  const d = docOf(collectAudit(h).stdout);
  expect(d['verdict'], `${what}: ${JSON.stringify(d)}`).toBe('registered');
  expect(d['token'], `${what}: no token while a child holds the slug`).toBeUndefined();
};
/** The detail of the last collect `done` row. Its decisive words lead it, before any path, so it holds under the
 *  300-byte cut whatever this HOME's length. */
const lastDoneDetail = (): string =>
  String(eventsOf(h.home, 'collect').filter((e) => e['outcome'] === 'done').at(-1)?.['detail']);

describe.skipIf(!LINUX || !NO_COPY)('six late recycled-spawn boundaries, forced through the real verb (TR12 B): the new child\'s leaf and witness always stand', () => {
  it('late-1 fresh emptied: the compare-and-drop, fed the record\'s fields, keeps the spawn\'s witness', () => {
    orphanLeaf(h);
    const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h), COL_ID, gapAt({ emptied: SPAWN }));
    expect(gapErrorsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the spawn ran').toEqual([]);
    expect(gapsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: at `emptied`, after the slot was rmdir\'d').toContain('emptied');
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout), r.stdout).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, resumed: false, witness: 'kept' });
    newChildStands();
    expect(slotsOf(h), 'the slot went').toEqual([]);
    expect(recordsOf(h), 'and the record, last').toEqual([]);
    expect(asidesOf(), 'the new witness was moved back: no aside is left').toEqual([]);
    nextAuditRegistered('the next audit sees the new child\'s row');
  }, 120_000);

  it('late-2 fresh witnessed: the temp-file reap holds while the slug is taken, and the spawn\'s witness survives the record drop', () => {
    orphanLeaf(h);
    plantAgedTemp();
    const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h), COL_ID, gapAt({ witnessed: SPAWN }));
    expect(gapErrorsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the spawn ran').toEqual([]);
    expect(gapsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: at `witnessed`').toContain('witnessed');
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout), r.stdout).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, resumed: false, witness: 'dropped' });
    newChildStands();
    expect(fs.existsSync(agedTempOf()), 'the reap held: the slug was taken when it ran').toBe(true);
    expect(lastDoneDetail()).toMatch(/^witness dropped; 0 stale witness temp file\(s\) removed; /);
    expect(slotsOf(h), 'the slot went').toEqual([]);
    expect(recordsOf(h), 'and the record, last').toEqual([]);
    nextAuditRegistered('the next audit sees the new child\'s row');
  }, 120_000);

  it('late-3 fresh dropped: the next audits refuse registered and license nothing until the child leaves', () => {
    const o = orphanLeaf(h);
    const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h), COL_ID, gapAt({ dropped: SPAWN }));
    expect(gapErrorsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the spawn ran').toEqual([]);
    expect(gapsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: at `dropped`').toContain('dropped');
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout), r.stdout).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, resumed: false, witness: 'dropped' });
    newChildStands();
    expect(slotsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
    expect(recordsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
    const g2 = devinoOf(o.leaf);
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) nextAuditRegistered(`audit ${i + 1} while the new child holds the slug`);
    expect(devinoOf(o.leaf), 'the audits touched nothing').toBe(g2);
    // It leaves, as its own reclaim leaves it, and the next passes find nothing to collect.
    g2Departs(h);
    const rounds = settle(h);
    console.info(`late-3 settle rounds: ${rounds.length} ${JSON.stringify(rounds.map((x) => verdictOf(x)))}`);
    expect(lastVerdict(rounds), shownRounds(rounds)).toBe('not-witnessed');
    expect(devinoOf(o.leaf), 'nothing stands at the id').toBeNull();
    expect(slotsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
    expect(recordsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
  }, 240_000);

  it('late-4 putback restoring: NOREPLACE alone keeps the new child\'s empty leaf, and the old one stays in its slot', () => {
    const o = orphanLeaf(h);
    const pre = `${gapAt({ moved: 'touch "$HOME/in-use"', restoring: `${g2Row()} && ${g2Spawn(COL_ID, '')}` })}`
      + ` ${INUSE_AFTER_FLAG}`;
    const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h), COL_ID, pre);
    expect(gapErrorsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the spawn ran').toEqual([]);
    expect(gapsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: step 5 refused in-use, and the putback reached its seam').toContain('restoring');
    expect(gapsOf(h), 'step 6 never ran').not.toContain('proven');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'g2-dir'), 'utf8'), 'the CONTROL: the spawn was handed the id-derived leaf')
      .toBe(o.leaf);
    const g2 = devinoOf(o.leaf);
    expect(g2, 'the new child was handed a NEW inode at the id').not.toBeNull();
    expect(g2).not.toBe(o.devino);
    expect(fs.readdirSync(o.leaf), 'untouched, and still EMPTY: a restore that replaced it would have filled it').toEqual([]);
    expect(witnessField(h, 'run'), 'the new child\'s witness stands').toBe(G2_RUN);
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    const d = docOf(r.stdout);
    expect(d['refused'], r.stdout).toBe('quarantine-kept');
    expect(String(d['detail']))
      .toMatch(/^kept in its slot with the quarantine record \S+, listed for the operator, and nothing was removed: /);
    const slots = slotsOf(h);
    expect(slots, 'one slot is kept').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(recordsOf(h), 'named by its record').toEqual([slots[0]!.slice('slot.'.length)]);
    const kept = path.join(quarantineOf(h), slots[0]!, 'leaf');
    expect(devinoOf(kept), 'the old leaf is kept in its slot').toBe(o.devino);
    // The doubt clears and the new child leaves: the record resumes, and only the record's inode goes.
    fs.rmSync(path.join(h.home, 'in-use'));
    g2Departs(h);
    const rounds = settle(h);
    console.info(`late-4 settle rounds: ${rounds.length} ${JSON.stringify(rounds.map((x) => verdictOf(x)))}`);
    expect(lastVerdict(rounds), shownRounds(rounds)).toBe('not-witnessed');
    expect(devinoOf(kept), 'the kept leaf went once nothing held the slug').toBeNull();
    expect(slotsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
    expect(recordsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
  }, 240_000);

  it('late-5 witness-only witnessed: the spawn\'s leaf and witness stand, the reap holds, and no quarantine is ever made', () => {
    const o = orphanLeaf(h);
    fs.rmSync(o.leaf, { recursive: true });
    plantAgedTemp();
    const t = tokenOf(h);
    const r = collectVerb(h, t, COL_ID, gapAt({ witnessed: SPAWN }));
    expect(gapErrorsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the spawn ran').toEqual([]);
    expect(gapsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the witness-only arm: no record, no slot, no move')
      .toEqual(['locked', 'consented', 'witnessed']);
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout), r.stdout).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, record: null, resumed: false, witness: 'dropped' });
    newChildStands();
    expect(fs.existsSync(agedTempOf()), 'the reap held: the slug was taken when it ran').toBe(true);
    expect(lastDoneDetail()).toMatch(/^witness dropped; 0 stale witness temp file\(s\) removed; no leaf stood at /);
    expect(fs.existsSync(quarantineOf(h)), 'no quarantine was ever made: nothing moved').toBe(false);
    expect(recordsOf(h)).toEqual([]);
    nextAuditRegistered('the next audit sees the new child\'s row');
  }, 120_000);

  it('late-6 resume past removed, at emptied: no step 5 and no registry ask, so the compare-and-drop alone keeps the new witness', () => {
    const o = orphanLeaf(h);
    const k = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h), COL_ID, crashAt('removed'));
    expect(crashedAt(h), 'the CONTROL: the kill fired at `removed`').toBe('removed');
    expect(docOf(k.stdout)['collected'], 'a killed verb reports nothing').toBeUndefined();
    const recs = recordsOf(h);
    expect(recs, 'the CONTROL: one record stands').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(slotsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: its slot stands').toEqual([`slot.${recs[0]!}`]);
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(quarantineOf(h), `slot.${recs[0]!}`, 'leaf')), 'the CONTROL: the slot\'s leaf was removed')
      .toBe(false);
    expect(devinoOf(o.leaf), 'the CONTROL: nothing stands at the id').toBeNull();
    expect(witnessField(h, 'run'), 'the CONTROL: the witness is still the dead run\'s').toBe(DEAD_RUN);
    const before = gapsOf(h).length;
    const t = tokenOf(h);
    const r = collectVerb(h, t, COL_ID, gapAt({ emptied: SPAWN }));
    expect(gapErrorsOf(h), 'the CONTROL: the spawn ran').toEqual([]);
    const resumed = gapsOf(h).slice(before);
    expect(resumed, 'the resume entered the order at the slot\'s rmdir').toEqual(['locked', 'consented', 'emptied', 'witnessed', 'dropped']);
    expect(resumed, 'no move after the crash').not.toContain('moved');
    expect(resumed, 'and no step 5').not.toContain('proven');
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout), r.stdout).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, resumed: true, witness: 'kept' });
    newChildStands();
    expect(slotsOf(h), 'the slot went').toEqual([]);
    expect(recordsOf(h), 'and the record, last').toEqual([]);
    expect(asidesOf(), 'no aside is left').toEqual([]);
  }, 120_000);
});
```

```ts
// and none walks the real /proc: every verb, audit and evaluation call stubs the in-use probe (`NOBODY`, `PROBE_STUB`).
// Darwin has no table: its pins POISON the seam and prove the clean path never reads it, on both hosts; a Linux host
// forcing `CCD_OS=darwin` shims the two BSD spellings it cannot run (`DARWIN_SHIMS`).
//
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every root, leaf, table, registry row and slot derives from `h.home`, and every
// verb runs as a SOURCED function, never through the installed launcher and never against the live HOME. A case that
// narrows a directory's mode restores it in `finally`.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { eventsOf, measOf } from './lifecycleHelpers.js';
import { CHILD_ID, childReclaimVerb, evalOf, makeChild } from './childReclaimFixture.js';
import { NOBODY, NO_COPY } from './collectRaceFixture.js';
import {
  MOUNTS_SEAM, PROBE_STUB, collectToken, collectVerb, docOf, gapAt, gaps, makeOrphan, quarantineOf, realMounts,
  records, slots,
} from './wsCollectFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-removal-mounts-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';
const DARWIN_HOST = process.platform === 'darwin';
const ROOT_USER = process.getuid?.() === 0;
const ID = 'demo-quiet-basin';

/** A path as the kernel's table writes it: space, tab, newline and backslash as \040, \011, \012 and \134. */
const encoded = (p: string): string =>
  p.replace(/\\/g, '\\134').replace(/ /g, '\\040').replace(/\t/g, '\\011').replace(/\n/g, '\\012');
/** One line of the kernel's table, naming a mount point at `p` (a PHYSICAL path). */
const MOUNT_LINE = (p: string): string => `9999 1 0:99 / ${encoded(p)} rw,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw`;
const at = (n: string): string => path.join(h.home, n);
/** The table `MOUNTS_SEAM` names. */
const tableOf = (): string => at('mountinfo');
/** The kernel's own table copied under the fixture HOME, then one line at each of `ps`. */
const fakeTable = (...ps: string[]): void => {
  realMounts(h);
  for (const p of ps) fs.appendFileSync(tableOf(), `${MOUNT_LINE(p)}\n`);
};
/** The seam POISONED: any read of the table leaves `$HOME/mi-called`, and the table it names does not exist. */
const POISON = '_ws_collect_mountinfo() { echo x >> "$HOME/mi-called"; printf "%s" "$HOME/no-such-table"; };';
/** Forced Darwin on a LINUX host (measured: GNU `stat -f '%d:%i'` and GNU `rm -rfx` both fail): the device read takes
 *  GNU's spelling, and `rm -rfx` is logged to `$HOME/rm-calls` and run as `rm -rf`; every other `rm` passes through
 *  unlogged. On a Darwin host the real BSD spellings run, and nothing is shimmed. */
const DARWIN_SHIMS = DARWIN_HOST ? '' : '_plat_devino() { stat -c \'%d:%i\' "$@"; };'
  + ' rm() { if [[ "${1-}" == -rfx ]]; then printf \'%s\\n\' "$*" >> "$HOME/rm-calls"; shift;'
  + ' command rm -rf "$@"; else command rm "$@"; fi; };';
/** `_ws_dir_physical`, wrapped: every directory it is asked to resolve is logged to `$HOME/phys-called`. */
const PHYS_SPY = 'eval "_t_phys_real()$(declare -f _ws_dir_physical | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_dir_physical() { printf \'%s\\n\' "$1" >> "$HOME/phys-called"; _t_phys_real "$@"; };';
const linesAt = (n: string): string[] =>
  (fs.existsSync(at(n)) ? fs.readFileSync(at(n), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : []);
const modeOf = (p: string): string => (fs.statSync(p).mode & 0o777).toString(8);
/** A fresh directory under the fixture HOME, returned in its PHYSICAL spelling. */
const dirAt = (n: string): string => { fs.mkdirSync(at(n), { recursive: true }); return fs.realpathSync(at(n)); };
/** `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`'s own reason for a mount point `mp` at or under `dir`. */
const MOUNTED = (mp: string, dir: string): string =>
  `something is mounted at ${encoded(mp)}, at or under ${dir} — ccd never removes across a mount`;

/** The helper, asked in the current shell: `[rc=N] <its reason>`. */
const ask = (d: string, opts: { resolve?: boolean; pre?: string } = {}): string =>
  h.run(`${opts.pre ?? ''} _ws_removal_mounts_clear '${d}'${opts.resolve ? ' resolve' : ''};`
    + ' echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_MOUNTS_WHY"').stdout;

const rootOf = (): string => at('root');
const leafOf = (): string => path.join(rootOf(), ID);
/** The leaf as `_ws_leaf_remove` composes it: the root resolved physically, then the id. */
const physLeaf = (): string => path.join(fs.realpathSync(rootOf()), ID);
/** `_ws_leaf_remove "$HOME/root" <ID>`, asked in the current shell: `[rc=N] <its raw, uncut reason>`. */
const removeLeaf = (pre = ''): string =>
  h.run(`${pre} _ws_leaf_remove "$HOME/root" ${ID}; echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_LEAF_WHY"`).stdout;
/** What `_ws_leaf_remove` answers when the mount question answers 2 with `why`. */
const LEAF_KEPT = (why: string, leaf: string): string => `[rc=2] ${why} — nothing under ${leaf} was removed`;

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('_ws_removal_mounts_clear — the one mount question, 0 or 2 and never 1 (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  it('case 1: a mount AT the directory answers 2', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    fakeTable(d);
    expect(ask(d, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM })).toBe(`[rc=2] ${MOUNTED(d, d)}`);
  });

  it('case 2: a mount UNDER the directory answers 2', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    fakeTable(`${d}/x`);
    expect(ask(d, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM })).toBe(`[rc=2] ${MOUNTED(`${d}/x`, d)}`);
  });

  it('case 3: a mount at a SIBLING (`<d>-x`) is not under it: 0', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    fakeTable(`${d}-x`);
    expect(ask(d, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM })).toBe('[rc=0]');
  });

  it('case 4: a table that cannot be read answers 2', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    const pre = '_ws_collect_mountinfo() { printf \'%s\' "$HOME/no-such"; };';
    expect(ask(d, { pre }))
      .toBe(`[rc=2] ${at('no-such')} could not be read, so whether anything is mounted under ${d} was never asked`);
  });

  it('case 4b: a table that holds a line that is not a mount answers 2', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    fakeTable();
    fs.appendFileSync(tableOf(), 'not a mount line\n');
    expect(ask(d, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM }))
      .toBe(`[rc=2] ${tableOf()} holds a line that is not a mount, so the table was never read whole`);
  });

  it('case 5: a table that lists no mount answers 2', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    fs.writeFileSync(tableOf(), '');
    expect(ask(d, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM })).toBe(`[rc=2] ${tableOf()} listed no mount at all, so the table was never read`);
  });

  it('case 6: a `//` spelling is collapsed to `/` and asked — never missed, never refused', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    fakeTable(`${d}/x`);
    // THE CONTROL: the collector's question asked of the `//` spelling directly MISSES the mount (the table never
    // writes `//`), so the collapse is what makes the answer right.
    expect(h.run(`${MOUNTS_SEAM} _ws_collect_mounts_clear '/${d}'; echo "[rc=$?]"`).stdout).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(ask(`/${d}`, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM })).toBe(`[rc=2] ${MOUNTED(`${d}/x`, d)}`);
  });

  it('case 7: `resolve` asks the PHYSICAL path of a directory under a symbolic link; without it the text is asked', () => {
    const d = dirAt('real/d');
    fs.symlinkSync(at('real'), at('alias'));
    const logical = path.join(at('alias'), 'd');
    fakeTable(`${d}/x`);
    expect(ask(logical, { resolve: true, pre: MOUNTS_SEAM })).toBe(`[rc=2] ${MOUNTED(`${d}/x`, d)}`);
    expect(ask(logical, { pre: MOUNTS_SEAM }), 'without resolve the logical spelling is compared as text').toBe('[rc=0]');
  });

  it('case 8: `resolve` of a directory that cannot be entered answers 2, and the table is never asked', () => {
    const n = at('nowhere');
    expect(ask(n, { resolve: true, pre: MOUNTS_SEAM }))
      .toBe(`[rc=2] ${n} cannot be resolved (${n} cannot be entered), so whether anything is mounted under it was never asked`);
  });

  it('case 9: the CONTROL — the kernel’s own table, untouched, has no mount under a fixture directory: 0', () => {
    expect(ask(dirAt('d'))).toBe('[rc=0]');
  });
});

describe('on Darwin nothing is asked: the helper’s one guard, and the leaf’s clean removal (both hosts; path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  it('case 10: forced Darwin, the seam poisoned and the resolution spied — 0, and neither was reached', () => {
    const d = dirAt('d');
    expect(ask(d, { resolve: true, pre: `CCD_OS=darwin; ${POISON} ${PHYS_SPY}` })).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(linesAt('mi-called'), 'the table was never read').toEqual([]);
    expect(linesAt('phys-called'), 'nothing was resolved').toEqual([]);
    // THE CONTROL: the same poison and spy on the Linux arm are reached, and the poison answers 2.
    expect(ask(d, { resolve: true, pre: `CCD_OS=linux; ${POISON} ${PHYS_SPY}` }))
      .toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] \S+\/no-such-table could not be read, so whether anything is mounted under /);
    expect(linesAt('mi-called')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(linesAt('phys-called')).toEqual([d]);
  });

  it('D1: forced Darwin, a clean directory leaf — removed by its Darwin removal, and the table never read', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x', 'f'), 'scratch\n');
    const leaf = physLeaf();
    expect(removeLeaf(`CCD_OS=darwin; ${POISON} ${DARWIN_SHIMS}`)).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(fs.existsSync(leafOf()), 'the leaf is gone').toBe(false);
    expect(linesAt('mi-called'), 'the table was never read').toEqual([]);
    if (!DARWIN_HOST) expect(linesAt('rm-calls'), 'the Darwin removal itself ran').toEqual([`-rfx -- ${leaf}`]);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('_ws_leaf_remove asks it twice: after the device compare, and before rm (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  it('L1: a mount under the leaf answers 2 before the permission pass — a mode-0500 directory inside it keeps its mode', () => {
    const locked = path.join(leafOf(), 'mnt', 'locked');
    fs.mkdirSync(locked, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(locked, 'f'), 'inside the mount\n');
    fs.chmodSync(locked, 0o500);
    const leaf = physLeaf();
    fakeTable(`${leaf}/mnt`);
    let out: string; let mode: string;
    try { out = removeLeaf(MOUNTS_SEAM); mode = fs.existsSync(locked) ? modeOf(locked) : 'gone'; }
    finally { if (fs.existsSync(locked)) fs.chmodSync(locked, 0o755); }
    expect(out).toBe(LEAF_KEPT(MOUNTED(`${leaf}/mnt`, leaf), leaf));
    expect(mode, 'the permission pass never ran inside the mount').toBe('500');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(locked, 'f'), 'utf8'), 'everything stands').toBe('inside the mount\n');
  }, 60_000);

  it('L1b: a mount AT the leaf answers 2 before the leaf’s own owner bits are set', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'), { recursive: true });
    const leaf = physLeaf();
    fakeTable(leaf);
    fs.chmodSync(leafOf(), 0o500);
    let out: string; let mode: string;
    try { out = removeLeaf(MOUNTS_SEAM); mode = fs.existsSync(leafOf()) ? modeOf(leafOf()) : 'gone'; }
    finally { if (fs.existsSync(leafOf())) fs.chmodSync(leafOf(), 0o755); }
    expect(out).toBe(LEAF_KEPT(MOUNTED(leaf, leaf), leaf));
    expect(mode, 'the leaf’s own mode, untouched: ask 1 precedes the owner bits').toBe('500');
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x')), 'everything stands').toBe(true);
  }, 60_000);

  it('L2: a mount made while the permission pass runs is seen by the second ask, directly before rm', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'mnt'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'mnt', 'f'), 'inside the mount\n');
    const leaf = physLeaf();
    fakeTable();
    const pre = `${MOUNTS_SEAM} eval "_t_norm_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_normalise | tail -n +2)";`
      + ` _ws_reclaim_normalise() { if [[ "$1" == */${ID} ]]; then`
      + ' printf \'%s\\n\' "9999 1 0:99 / $1/mnt rw,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw" >> "$HOME/mountinfo"; fi;'
      + ' _t_norm_real "$@"; };';
    expect(removeLeaf(pre)).toBe(LEAF_KEPT(MOUNTED(`${leaf}/mnt`, leaf), leaf));
    expect(fs.readFileSync(tableOf(), 'utf8'), 'the CONTROL: the line was added inside the pass, after ask 1')
      .toContain(`/ ${leaf}/mnt rw,relatime`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'mnt', 'f'), 'utf8'), 'everything stands').toBe('inside the mount\n');
  }, 60_000);

  it('L3: a table that cannot be read answers 2, and nothing is removed', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'), { recursive: true });
    const leaf = physLeaf();
    const pre = '_ws_collect_mountinfo() { printf \'%s\' "$HOME/no-such-table"; };';
    expect(removeLeaf(pre)).toBe(LEAF_KEPT(
      `${at('no-such-table')} could not be read, so whether anything is mounted under ${leaf} was never asked`, leaf));
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'))).toBe(true);
  }, 60_000);

  it('L4: the CONTROL — a mount at a sibling of the leaf is not under it: removed, and proven gone', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'), { recursive: true });
    fakeTable(`${physLeaf()}-x`);
    expect(removeLeaf(MOUNTS_SEAM)).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(fs.existsSync(leafOf())).toBe(false);
  }, 60_000);

  it('L5: a root that resolves to a `//` spelling is collapsed and asked: a mount under the real spelling answers 2', () => {
    const real = dirAt('rootreal');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(real, ID, 'x'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(real, ID, 'x', 'f'), 'inside the mount\n');
    fs.symlinkSync(`/${real}`, rootOf());
    expect(h.sh('_ws_dir_physical "$HOME/root"; printf \'%s\' "$_WS_PHYS"'),
      'the CONTROL: bash keeps the link target’s leading `//`').toBe(`/${real}`);
    fakeTable(`${real}/${ID}/x`);
    expect(removeLeaf(MOUNTS_SEAM))
      .toBe(LEAF_KEPT(MOUNTED(`${real}/${ID}/x`, `${real}/${ID}`), `/${real}/${ID}`));
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(real, ID, 'x', 'f'), 'utf8'), 'everything stands').toBe('inside the mount\n');
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(ROOT_USER)('L6: a mode-000 leaf with no mount is removed as before — the question never enters the leaf', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(leafOf(), 'x'), { recursive: true });
    fakeTable();
    fs.chmodSync(leafOf(), 0o000);
    let out: string;
    try { out = removeLeaf(MOUNTS_SEAM); } finally { if (fs.existsSync(leafOf())) fs.chmodSync(leafOf(), 0o755); }
    expect(out).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(fs.existsSync(leafOf())).toBe(false);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('the tail’s two leaves, through the real reclaim verb: kept `unmeasured`, the act complete (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  const done = (): Record<string, unknown> => eventsOf(h.home, 'reclaim').find((e) => e['outcome'] === 'done')!;

  it('TL1: a mount under the temp root — kept `unmeasured`, the leaf and its witness standing, byte for byte', () => {
    makeChild(h);

    expect(measOf(done())['tmpRootKept']).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(String(done()['detail'])).toContain(`temp root ${tmp} kept (unmeasured): something is mounted at `);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'scratch.txt'), 'utf8'), 'the leaf stands').toBe('scratch\n');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(wit, 'utf8'), 'its witness stands, byte for byte').toBe(before);
  }, 90_000);

  it('TL2: a mount under the clips leaf — kept `unmeasured`, the clips leaf standing', () => {
    makeChild(h);

    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);

    expect(measOf(done())['clipsKept']).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(String(done()['detail'])).toContain(`clips ${clips} kept (unmeasured): something is mounted at `);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(clips, 'shot.png'), 'utf8'), 'the clips leaf stands').toBe('png');

describe.skipIf(!LINUX || !NO_COPY)('the collector’s window: a mount made after its step 5 asked (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  it('K1: step 6 answers failed quarantine-kept — the record and the slot kept, the leaf whole in its slot', () => {
    makeOrphan(h);

    realMounts(h);
    const mountAtProven = gapAt('proven',
      'printf "9999 1 0:99 / %s/leaf/mnt rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw\\n" "$3" >> "$HOME/mountinfo"');
    const r = collectVerb(h, token, { pre: `${MOUNTS_SEAM} ${PROBE_STUB} ${mountAtProven}` });
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(1);

    expect(doc['failed']).toBe('quarantine-kept');
    expect(String(doc['detail'])).toMatch(
      /^the quarantine record \S+ is kept, and nothing further was removed: something is mounted at /);
    expect(gaps(h), 'step 5 passed').toContain('proven');
    expect(gaps(h), 'and nothing was removed').not.toContain('removed');
    expect(records(h), 'its record is kept').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(slots(h), 'its slot is kept').toHaveLength(1);
    const sleaf = path.join(quarantineOf(h), slots(h)[0]!, 'leaf');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(sleaf, 'scratch.txt'), 'utf8'), 'scratch.txt is intact').toBe('scratch\n');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(sleaf, 'cdk.out', 'manifest.json'), 'utf8')).toBe('{}');
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('the source: one helper, one Darwin guard, and the leaf’s two asks in their places (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
  /** `name`'s definition, from its head line to its closing brace at column 0, or '' when it is not defined. */
  const bodyOf = (name: string): string => {
    const a = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
    const b = a > -1 ? src.indexOf('\n}\n', a + 1) : -1;
    return b > a ? src.slice(a + 1, b) : '';
  };
  /** Its lines of code: every whole-line comment dropped. */
  const codeOf = (name: string): string[] => bodyOf(name).split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l));
  const GUARD = '[[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || return 0';

  it('src-guard: the helper’s first line of code is the ONE Darwin guard, spelled once in ccd', () => {
    const code = codeOf('_ws_removal_mounts_clear');
    expect(code[0], 'the helper is defined').toMatch(/^_ws_removal_mounts_clear\(\) \{/);
    expect(code[1]?.trim(), 'its first line of code is the guard').toBe(GUARD);
    expect(src.split(GUARD).length - 1, 'the guard is spelled once').toBe(1);
  });

  it('src-reuse: the helper asks the collector’s question and reads no table of its own', () => {
    const code = codeOf('_ws_removal_mounts_clear').join('\n');
    expect(code).toContain('_ws_collect_mounts_clear "$d" && return 0');
    expect(code, 'no second reader of the table').not.toMatch(/mountinfo|exec \{|\bread -r\b/);
  });

  it('src-order: _ws_leaf_remove asks it twice — directly after the device compare, and directly before rm', () => {
    const code = codeOf('_ws_leaf_remove');
    const at = (needle: string): number => code.findIndex((l) => l.includes(needle));
    const asks = code.flatMap((l, i) => (/^\s*_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$leaf" \\$/.test(l) ? [i] : []));
    expect(asks, 'two asks, neither in resolve mode').toHaveLength(2);
    const dev = at('ccd never removes a mount"; return 1; }');
    const bits = at('find -P "$leaf" -maxdepth 0');
    const rm = at('then err=$(rm -rfx -- "$leaf"');
    expect([dev, bits, rm].every((i) => i > -1), 'the anchors were found').toBe(true);
    expect(asks[0], 'ask 1 directly follows the device compare').toBe(dev + 1);
    expect(asks[0]! + 2, 'and directly precedes the owner bits').toBe(bits);
    expect(asks[1]! + 2, 'ask 2 directly precedes rm').toBe(rm);
    for (const i of asks) {
      expect(code[i + 1]?.trim(), 'each maps the answer to 2, the reason first')
        .toBe('|| { _WS_LEAF_WHY="$_WS_MOUNTS_WHY — nothing under $leaf was removed"; return 2; }');
    }
  });
});
```

**3a. The helper**, directly above `_ws_leaf_remove`. The block from `# ONE QUESTION` to the guard is all `#` lines, so the guard stays the first line of code.

Before:
```bash

  [[ -z "$why" ]] || return 2
  return 0
}
_ws_leaf_remove() {   # root id [expect-devino [alias accepted]] -> 0 removed, or absent — PROVEN by `_ws_reclaim_absent`;
```
After:
```bash
  _WS_CHECKOUTS_WHY="$why"
  [[ -z "$why" ]] || return 2
  return 0
}
_ws_removal_mounts_clear() {   # dir [resolve] -> 0 nothing is mounted at dir or under it — on Darwin, never asked (spec
  #                                §3.5); 2 (_WS_MOUNTS_WHY) one is, the table could not be read whole, or (resolve) dir
  #                                could not be resolved. Never 1: every caller refuses both alike
  # ONE QUESTION, ONE DEFINITION, ONE GUARD (path-identity spec §3.5). A
  # removal that could cross a mount asks it before it acts. The device
  # compare in `_ws_leaf_remove` and `rm --one-file-system` see only another
  # device, so a bind mount of the leaf's own file system was crossed, and a
  # same-uid process can make a FUSE mount in ccd's namespace. This is the
  # collector's own question, `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`, reused and never
  # copied: the kernel's table, read through its one seam
  # (`_ws_collect_mountinfo`), with a mount point at or under the path
  # compared as encoded text.
  # - THE GUARD is the first line of code below, and the only one: Darwin has
  #   no such table, so nothing is asked there and the caller's removal runs
  #   as before. "Not asked" and "clear" both answer 0, and both mean
  #   "proceed".
  # - THE PATH is the one the removal acts on, spelled physically, because the
  #   table writes mount points physically. `_ws_leaf_remove` hands its leaf,
  #   physical by construction (a physical root, an id with no `/`, and no
  #   link), so nothing here enters it: resolved, a mode-000 leaf could not be
  #   entered, and would be kept for ever. A caller whose path may stand under
  #   a symbolic link passes `resolve`, and the path is resolved first
  #   (`_ws_dir_physical`); a path that cannot be resolved is never asked, and
  #   answers 2. Bash's `pwd -P` keeps a link target's leading `//`, which
  #   Linux reads as `/` and the table never writes, so it is collapsed,
  #   never refused.
  # - THE ANSWER is 0 or 2, never 1. The question's own 1 (a mount stands) and
  #   2 (the table was not read whole) are folded HERE, so no caller can split
  #   them or read either as a refusal: each keeps what it would have removed.
  [[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || return 0
  local d="${1-}"
  if [[ -n "${2-}" ]]; then
    _ws_dir_physical "$d" \
      || { _WS_MOUNTS_WHY="$d cannot be resolved ($_WS_PHYS_WHY), so whether anything is mounted under it was never asked"; return 2; }
    d="$_WS_PHYS"
  fi
  [[ "$d" != //[!/]* ]] || d="${d#/}"   # Linux reads `//x` as `/x`, and the kernel's table never writes `//`
  _ws_collect_mounts_clear "$d" && return 0
  return 2
}
_ws_leaf_remove() {   # root id [expect-devino [alias accepted]] -> 0 removed, or absent — PROVEN by `_ws_reclaim_absent`;
```

```bash
  #   for a mount made after its step 5 asked). The leaf is handed over

```

```bash
fix(ccd): the leaf removal asks the mount question before its owner bits and again before rm

The leaf removal compared st_dev alone, and rm --one-file-system
measures st_dev too, so a bind mount of the leaf's own file system was
crossed, and the permission pass's find -xdev chmod changed modes in
the bind's source before any later check could refuse
(path-identity spec §3.5).

One helper, _ws_removal_mounts_clear, now asks the collector's mount
question, _ws_collect_mounts_clear, reused rather than copied. Its
first line of code is the one Darwin guard: Darwin has no mount table,
so nothing is asked there and the removal runs as before. It answers 0
or 2, never 1, so a mount and an unreadable table are folded in one
place. With resolve it resolves the path first, and a // physical
spelling collapses to /.

_ws_leaf_remove asks it directly after its device compare, before the
owner bits, the checkout question and the permission pass
(leaf-mount-ask-before-the-owner-bits), and again directly before rm.
Either answer is unmeasured, with nothing removed. The reclaim and
expiry tail's step 6 therefore keeps a clips leaf or a temp root with
a mount under it as unmeasured, its witness standing, and the
collector's step 6 answers failed quarantine-kept for a mount made
after its step 5 asked, keeping its record and slot.
EOF
```

### Task 5: Every standing forced worktree removal asks the mount question first (TR5 C, the worktree half)

**Model routing:** `opus`, effort `xhigh`. This is SAFETY and the shared tail (step 3 and step 4, consent R38). Git's forced recursive delete has no device test (judgement; `git-mount-crossing-unmeasured`), and a FUSE daemon survives the pane kill under `KillMode=process`.

**Why:** spec §3.5, R10 and P1. The asks go before `keep_of` and again before `--force`, at each standing nested checkout and at the child's own worktree. They fail `worktree-remove-failed` and leave the breadcrumb and the tree. The vanished arms get no ask, and no whole-child ask is added (R12).

**The 300-byte cut, read narrowly here.** Global Constraints says every reason a journal row carries passes `_ws_leaf_why_line`. That line governs the kept-leaf and collect reasons this wave adds. The tail's four new reasons go to `_ws_reclaim_fail` raw, as §Interfaces spells the statement, and as every existing tail failure does (the `pin-failed` reasons beside them, and git's own output at the same sites). `_ws_reclaim_fail` writes the one string to both the journal row and the document, so the two cannot drift, and the cases assert only a reason's leading text. A mount point holding a control byte the kernel's table does not encode (it encodes only space, tab, newline and backslash) therefore reaches the row raw, escaped by the journal's JSON encoder. The worker records this reading under `w2-task-5-plan-text` (Step 8). Whether every tail failure reason should be cut is the coordinator's to rule, never this task's to widen.

```ts
// path-identity W2, Task 5 (path-identity spec §3.5; TR5 C, the worktree half). The reclaim and expiry tail asks the
// mount question before every STANDING forced worktree removal. Nothing measured says git's forced recursive delete
// stops at a mount, and a FUSE daemon outlives the pane kill, so a mount inside a tree the tail removes could be
// emptied through. Each standing nested checkout (step 3) and the child's own tree (step 4) is asked
// `_ws_removal_mounts_clear` directly before its `_ws_reclaim_keep_of` and again directly before its forced removal.
// Step 4 asks with `resolve`: the record's spelling may run through a symlinked ancestor, and the kernel's table names
// the physical mount point. Either answer fails `worktree-remove-failed`, with the breadcrumb and the tree standing.
// The vanished arms ask nothing, and on Darwin the helper's one guard answers before any table is read.
// MOUNTS ARE FAKED, NEVER MADE: `_ws_collect_mountinfo` is pointed at `$HOME/mountinfo` (`MOUNTS_SEAM`), a copy of this
// process's own table (`realMounts`) with lines appended. Nothing here mounts anything.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): both verbs run as SOURCED functions with the unit and pane calls recorded
// (`CHILD_STUBS`, `EXP_STUBS`, which `childReclaimVerb` and `expireVerb` prepend), the temp root's in-use probe
// answering "nobody", and every path derived from `h.home`. The cases that read a table run on Linux only; the Darwin
// pins and the source pins run on every host.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { eventsOf } from './lifecycleHelpers.js';
import { CHILD_BRANCH, CHILD_ID, childReclaimVerb, evalOf, makeChild, type Child } from './childReclaimFixture.js';
import { verbHelpers } from './childReclaimVerbHelpers.js';
import { EXP_BRANCH, EXP_ID, expireToken, expireVerb, makeArchived } from './wsExpireFixture.js';
import { MOUNTS_SEAM, realMounts } from './wsCollectFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-reclaim-tail-mounts-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });
const { interrupted, resumeToken, failedPairAgrees } = verbHelpers(() => h);

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';
type Run = { code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string };
type Doc = { failed?: string; detail?: string; reclaimed?: string; expired?: string };
const docOf = (r: Run): Doc => JSON.parse(r.stdout) as Doc;

/** A mount point as the kernel's table writes it: space, tab, newline and backslash encoded. */
const encoded = (p: string): string =>
  p.replace(/\\/g, '\\134').replace(/ /g, '\\040').replace(/\t/g, '\\011').replace(/\n/g, '\\012');
/** One line of a mount table naming `p` (physical) as a mount point: Task 4's shape. */
const MOUNT_LINE = (p: string): string => `9999 1 0:99 / ${encoded(p)} rw,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw`;
/** Appends a mount at `p` to the faked table now. */
const mountAt = (p: string): void => { fs.appendFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'mountinfo'), `${MOUNT_LINE(p)}\n`); };
/** Arms `KEEP_LOG`: once `_ws_reclaim_keep_of` answers 0 for the path spelled `spelling`, a mount at `p` appears. */
const mountOnceKept = (spelling: string, p: string): void => {
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'mount-when'), spelling);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'mount-later'), `${MOUNT_LINE(p)}\n`);
};
const linesIn = (name: string): string[] => {
  const p = path.join(h.home, name);
  return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
};

/** The temp root's in-use probe answering "nobody", so the tail's wait never runs the real walk of /proc. */
const NOBODY = '_ws_path_users() { _WS_PATH_USERS_PIDS=""; _WS_PATH_USERS_WHY=""; return 0; };';
/** Task 4's poison: any read of the mount table is recorded in `$HOME/mi-called`, and the table cannot be read. */
const POISON = '_ws_collect_mountinfo() { echo x >> "$HOME/mi-called"; printf "%s" "$HOME/no-such-table"; };';
/** `_ws_reclaim_keep_of`, wrapped: logs its `$4` (the path or branch it keeps for) to `$HOME/keep-calls`, runs the
 *  real one, and, once that answered 0 for the spelling in `$HOME/mount-when`, appends `$HOME/mount-later` to the
 *  faked table: a mount that appears between the two asks. */
const KEEP_LOG = 'eval "_t_keep_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_keep_of | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_reclaim_keep_of() { local r; printf \'%s\\n\' "$4" >> "$HOME/keep-calls"; _t_keep_real "$@"; r=$?;'
  + ' if (( r == 0 )) && [[ -f "$HOME/mount-when" ]] && [[ "$4" == "$(cat "$HOME/mount-when")" ]]; then'
  + ' cat "$HOME/mount-later" >> "$HOME/mountinfo"; fi; return "$r"; };';
/** `_ws_removal_mounts_clear`, wrapped: logs `<dir>|<mode>` to `$HOME/ask-calls`, then asks the real one. */
const ASK_LOG = 'eval "_t_ask_real()$(declare -f _ws_removal_mounts_clear | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_removal_mounts_clear() { printf \'%s|%s\\n\' "$1" "${2-}" >> "$HOME/ask-calls"; _t_ask_real "$@"; };';
/** `_ws_dir_physical` failing for the mount helper's `resolve` only: every other caller asks the real one. */
const PHYS_FAILS_AT_THE_ASK = 'eval "_t_phys_real()$(declare -f _ws_dir_physical | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_dir_physical() { if [[ "${FUNCNAME[1]-}" == _ws_removal_mounts_clear ]]; then'
  + ' _WS_PHYS=""; _WS_PHYS_WHY="stub: $1 could not be entered"; return 1; fi; _t_phys_real "$@"; };';
const LINUX_PRE = `${MOUNTS_SEAM} ${NOBODY} ${KEEP_LOG}`;
const DARWIN_PRE = `CCD_OS=darwin; ${POISON} ${ASK_LOG}`;

/** How many times the helper was asked of `spelling` in `mode` ('' or 'resolve'). */
const asked = (spelling: string, mode = ''): number =>
  linesIn('ask-calls').filter((l) => l === `${spelling}|${mode}`).length;
const reclaimToken = (): string => {
  const a = evalOf(h);
  expect(a.token, `the CONTROL: the ladder passes — ${a.verdict}: ${a.detail}`).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return a.token;
};
const workdirOf = (id: string): string => {
  const w = h.reg(id, 'workdir');
  expect(w, 'the CONTROL: the registry row names a workdir').not.toBeNull();
  return w!;
};
/** A standing nested checkout of the child's own repository, holding a file of its own. */
const nested = (c: Child): string => {
  const inner = path.join(c.wt, 'inner');
  h.git(c.main, 'worktree', 'add', '-b', 'ws/nested', inner);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(inner, 'f'), 'nested work\n');
  return inner;
};
/** The fleet's layout, made BEFORE the child: `$HOME/worktrees` a link to `$HOME/wtreal`. */
const linkedRoot = (): void => {
  const real = path.join(h.home, 'wtreal');
  fs.mkdirSync(real);
  fs.symlinkSync(real, path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'));
};
/** Exit 1 and `worktree-remove-failed`: the document a mount answer leaves. */
const mountFailed = (r: Run): Doc => {
  expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(1);
  const o = docOf(r);
  expect(o.failed).toBe('worktree-remove-failed');
  return o;
};
/** The CONTROL, after a Darwin subject: the poison records a read, so its absence there means none was made. */
const poisonIsLive = (): void => {
  expect(h.sh(`${POISON} _ws_collect_mounts_clear "$HOME"; printf '[rc=%s]' "$?"`)).toBe('[rc=2]');
  expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(h.home, 'mi-called')), 'the poison records a read').toBe(true);
};

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('the tail asks the mount question before every standing forced worktree removal (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  it('N1: a mount under a standing nested checkout fails worktree-remove-failed before its keep_of; the checkout and its branch stand', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);

    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(inner, 'f'), 'utf8'), 'the nested checkout stands').toBe('nested work\n');
    expect(h.git(c.main, 'branch', '--list', 'ws/nested'), 'its branch stands').toContain('ws/nested');

    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(c.wt, 'f1.txt')), 'the tree stands').toBe(true);
    expect(linesIn('keep-calls').filter((l) => l === wd), 'keep_of was never asked of the tree').toEqual([]);
    failedPairAgrees(r);
  }, 120_000);

  it('C6: a tree whose worktrees root resolves to a `//` spelling is asked by its collapsed physical spelling', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    // The hardening suite's layout: `$HOME/worktrees` moved to `$HOME/wtreal`, then linked back as `/` + its path.
    fs.renameSync(path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'), path.join(h.home, 'wtreal'));
    fs.symlinkSync(`/${path.join(h.home, 'wtreal')}`, path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'));
    const wd = workdirOf(CHILD_ID);
    const real = fs.realpathSync(c.wt);
    expect(h.sh(`_ws_dir_physical '${wd}'; printf '%s' "$_WS_PHYS"`),
      'the CONTROL: bash keeps the link target’s leading `//`').toBe(`/${real}`);
    const tok = reclaimToken();
    realMounts(h);
    mountAt(path.join(real, 'sub'));
    const r = childReclaimVerb(h, tok, { pre: `${LINUX_PRE} ${ASK_LOG}` });
    const o = mountFailed(r);
    expect(o.detail).toMatch(/^something is mounted at /);
    expect(h.reg(CHILD_ID, 'reaping')).toBe('reclaim:worktree');
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(real, 'f1.txt')), 'the tree stands').toBe(true);
    expect(asked(wd, 'resolve'), 'the tree was asked once, resolved, and failed there').toBe(1);
    expect(linesIn('keep-calls').filter((l) => l === wd), 'keep_of was never asked of the tree').toEqual([]);
    failedPairAgrees(r);
  }, 120_000);

  it('E1: ws-expire, through the same tail, fails worktree-remove-failed and keeps the archived tree', () => {
    const a = makeArchived(h);
    const wd = workdirOf(EXP_ID);
    const tok = expireToken(h);
    expect(tok, 'the CONTROL: the expiry ladder passes').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
    realMounts(h);
    mountAt(path.join(fs.realpathSync(a.wt), 'sub'));
    const r = expireVerb(h, tok, { pre: LINUX_PRE });
    const o = mountFailed(r);
    expect(o.detail).toMatch(/^something is mounted at /);
    expect(h.reg(EXP_ID, 'reaping'), 'the breadcrumb stays at the step that failed').toBe('expire:worktree');
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(a.wt, 'f1.txt')), 'the archived tree stands').toBe(true);
    expect(h.git(a.main, 'branch', '--list', EXP_BRANCH), 'its branch stands').toContain(EXP_BRANCH);
    expect(linesIn('keep-calls').filter((l) => l === wd), 'keep_of was never asked of the tree').toEqual([]);
    const row = eventsOf(h.home, 'expire').filter((e) => e['outcome'] === 'failed').pop();
    expect(row?.['refusal'], 'the journal names the failure the document names').toBe('worktree-remove-failed');
    expect(row?.['detail'], 'the journal and the document carry one detail').toBe(o.detail);
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('the asks, read from the source (path-identity spec §3.5)', () => {
  /** `_ws_reclaim_tail`'s code: whole-line comments dropped, continuations joined (the six-calls census's own reading),
   *  so each two-line statement is one line. */
  const tailCode = (): string[] => {
    const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
    const tail = src.slice(src.indexOf('\n_ws_reclaim_tail() {'), src.indexOf('\ncmd_ws_reclaim() {'));
    expect(tail.length, 'the CONTROL: the tail was found').toBeGreaterThan(1000);
    return tail.split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l)).join('\n').replace(/\s*\\\n\s*/g, ' ').split('\n');
  };
  const SITES = /_ws_removal_mounts_clear|_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(cpath|workdir)"(?! 1)|worktree remove --force/;
  const label = (l: string): string => {
    let m = /_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$(\w+)"( resolve)?/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `mounts ${m[1]}${m[2] ?? ''}`;
    m = /_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(\w+)"/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `keep ${m[1]}`;
    m = /worktree remove --force "\$(\w+)"/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `remove ${m[1]}`;
    return `unlabelled: ${l.trim()}`;
  };

  it('in order: before keep_of and again before the forced removal, at the nested checkout and then at the tree, the tree resolved', () => {
    expect(tailCode().filter((l) => SITES.test(l)).map(label)).toEqual([
      'mounts cpath', 'keep cpath', 'mounts cpath', 'remove cpath',
      'mounts workdir resolve', 'keep workdir', 'mounts workdir resolve', 'remove workdir',
    ]);
  });

  it('each ask stands directly before a keep_of or the forced removal of its own path, so no vanished arm holds one', () => {
    const code = tailCode();
    const at = code.flatMap((l, i) => (/_ws_removal_mounts_clear /.test(l) ? [i] : []));
    expect(at.length, 'four asks in the tail').toBe(4);
    for (const i of at) {
      const p = /_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$(cpath|workdir)"/.exec(code[i]!)?.[1] ?? '?';
      const next = code.slice(i + 1).find((l) => l.trim() !== '') ?? '';
      const keep = `_ws_reclaim_keep_of "$main" "$id" tree "$${p}" ||`;
      const rm = `worktree remove --force "$${p}" 2>&1)`;
      expect(next.includes(keep) || next.includes(rm), `after ${code[i]!.trim().slice(0, 60)}: ${next.trim()}`).toBe(true);
    }
    // No ask spells git, so the tail's six destructive git calls stay six (`ccd-child-reclaim-tail-contained`).
    expect(code.filter((l) => /_ws_removal_mounts_clear /.test(l) && /\bgit\b/.test(l)), 'an ask that spells git').toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// path-identity W2 (TR3 A, TR4 A): the reclaim tail's witness drop is generation-exact (path-identity spec §3.2 and
// §3.3, Figure 3). Before this wave `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop` was a plain unlink of the live name: a tail that ran
// while `~/.cc-tmp` was unmounted read the leaf as gone and dropped its witness, and beside a quarantine slot of the id
// it orphaned that slot's witness. Now it reads and parses the witness, asks the device the witness records, lists the
// quarantine slots of the id, proves the leaf absent again, and unlinks only the generation it read: through the
// collector's compare-and-drop where `mv --no-copy` exists, and by a second read and a six-field compare elsewhere. It
// answers complete (0), kept (1) or unmeasured (2), with its reason in `_WS_WDROP_WHY`, and prints nothing.
// `_ws_tmproot_remove` reports a drop that is not complete as its own 2, never 1.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every witness, leaf and slot lives under the harness's HOME, and ccd runs as
// sourced functions, never against the live HOME. Nothing is mounted: the device question is driven by a rewritten
// `dev=` field and by `~/.cc-tmp` removed whole. The compare-and-drop rows need Linux with `mv --no-copy`; every other
// row runs on both platforms, Darwin simulated on a Linux host.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { LINUX, NO_COPY } from './collectRaceFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-tmproot-drop-exact-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const ID = 'demo-quiet-mesa';
const wdir = (): string => path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'tmproots');
const witness = (id: string = ID): string => path.join(wdir(), id);
const root = (): string => path.join(h.home, '.cc-tmp');
const leaf = (id: string = ID): string => path.join(root(), id);
const quarantine = (): string => path.join(root(), '.ccd-quarantine');
const esc = (s: string): string => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
const linesOf = (name: string): string[] => {
  const p = path.join(h.home, name);
  return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
};
/** What stands at `p`, for an untouched check: a directory's sorted names, or a file's bytes. */
const standing = (p: string): string =>
  (fs.lstatSync(p).isDirectory() ? `dir:${fs.readdirSync(p).sort().join(',')}` : fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8'));

/** The drop, and its answer on one line: `[rc=<n>] <_WS_WDROP>|<_WS_WDROP_WHY>`. */
const DROP = (id: string): string => `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop ${id}; echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_WDROP|$_WS_WDROP_WHY"`;
/** `pre`, then `DROP(id)`. Everything written to stderr after ccd is sourced goes to `$HOME/drop-stderr`, so a row can
 *  assert that the drop printed nothing. */
const drop = (id: string = ID, pre = ''): { out: string; err: string } => {
  const r = h.run(`exec 2>"$HOME/drop-stderr"; ${pre} ${DROP(id)}`);
  const ef = path.join(h.home, 'drop-stderr');
  const err = fs.existsSync(ef) ? fs.readFileSync(ef, 'utf8') : '';
  expect(r.code, `the CONTROL: the snippet ran to its answer: ${r.stdout} ${err}`).toBe(0);
  return { out: r.stdout, err };
};

/** A leaf and the witness the REAL writer writes for it, for run 7. Returns the witness's bytes. */
const plant = (id: string = ID): string => {
  fs.mkdirSync(leaf(id), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(leaf(id), 'scratch'), 'the leaf’s own');
  h.sh(`_ws_tmproot_witness_write ${id} '${leaf(id)}' 7`);
  expect(fs.existsSync(witness(id)), 'the CONTROL: the real writer wrote the witness').toBe(true);
  return fs.readFileSync(witness(id), 'utf8');
};
/** `plant`, then the leaf removed: the drop's ordinary input, a witness whose leaf is gone. */
const orphaned = (id: string = ID): string => {
  const bytes = plant(id);
  fs.rmSync(leaf(id), { recursive: true, force: true });
  return bytes;
};

/** `mv` and `rm`, each logged to `$HOME/mv-calls` or `$HOME/rm-calls` and then run (`ccd-ws-collect-order.test.ts`'s
 *  spy shape). */
const MV_SPY = 'mv() { printf \'%s\\n\' "$*" >> "$HOME/mv-calls"; command mv "$@"; };';
const RM_SPY = 'rm() { printf \'%s\\n\' "$*" >> "$HOME/rm-calls"; command rm "$@"; };';
/** Simulated Darwin. On a Linux host `_plat_devino`'s Darwin arm runs BSD `stat -f`, which GNU `stat` refuses, so the
 *  Linux arm stands in for it; on a Darwin host nothing is added. */
const DARWIN = `CCD_OS=darwin; ${process.platform === 'darwin' ? '' : "_plat_devino() { stat -c '%d:%i' \"$@\"; };"}`;
/** `_ws_reclaim_absent`, wrapped: when the drop asks it of the leaf — its absence proven again, the last ask before it
 *  drops — a recycled spawn's writer first replaces the witness (`sed` into a dot-leading temp file, then `mv -f` over
 *  the live name, as `_ws_tmproot_witness_write` does), and the real function then answers. Every other ask is the
 *  real one. The swap is logged to `$HOME/race-ran`. */
const RACE_AT_REPROVE = (sed: string): string =>
  'eval "_t_absent_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_absent | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_reclaim_absent() { if [[ "${FUNCNAME[1]}" == _ws_tmproot_witness_drop && "$1" == "$HOME/.cc-tmp/' + ID + '" ]]; then'
  + ' sed -e "' + sed + '" "$REG/tmproots/' + ID + '" > "$REG/tmproots/.' + ID + '.race.tmp"'
  + ' && command mv -f -- "$REG/tmproots/.' + ID + '.race.tmp" "$REG/tmproots/' + ID + '"'
  + ' && echo raced >> "$HOME/race-ran"; fi;'
  + ' _t_absent_real "$@"; };';
/** The real `_ws_collect_mv`, refused when its destination is the witness's own name: the compare-and-drop's move
 *  back fails, and what it moved aside stays at its aside. Each refusal is logged to `$HOME/move-back-refused`. */
const MOVE_BACK_FAILS =
  'eval "_t_mv_real()$(declare -f _ws_collect_mv | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_collect_mv() { if [[ "$2" == "$REG/tmproots/' + ID + '" ]]; then echo "$1" >> "$HOME/move-back-refused"; return 1; fi;'
  + ' _t_mv_real "$@"; };';
/** Search permission is never asked of root, so a `tmproots/` made unsearchable is no fixture there. */

/** `_ws_reclaim_absent`, wrapped as `RACE_AT_REPROVE` wraps it: when the drop proves the leaf's absence again,
 *  `tmproots/` is first made unsearchable (mode 0600), so the second read finds no witness off a failed test while the
 *  witness stands. Logged to `$HOME/lock-ran`. Every other ask is the real one. */
const LOCK_AT_REPROVE =
  'eval "_t_absent_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_absent | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_reclaim_absent() { if [[ "${FUNCNAME[1]}" == _ws_tmproot_witness_drop && "$1" == "$HOME/.cc-tmp/' + ID + '" ]]; then'
  + ' chmod 0600 "$REG/tmproots" && echo locked >> "$HOME/lock-ran"; fi;'
  + ' _t_absent_real "$@"; };';
/** `fn`, with `tmproots/`'s mode as it stood before restored after it whatever it answered, so the harness can remove
 *  the fixture. */
const restoringMode = <T>(fn: () => T): T => {
  const mode = fs.statSync(wdir()).mode & 0o7777;
  try { return fn(); } finally { fs.chmodSync(wdir(), mode); }
};

describe('the source: the drop prints nothing, and reuses the collector’s compare-and-drop', () => {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
  /** `name`'s body, from its head line to its first closing brace at column 0, or '' when it is not defined. */
  const bodyOf = (name: string): string => {
    const a = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
    const b = a > -1 ? src.indexOf('\n}\n', a) : -1;
    return b > a ? src.slice(a, b) : '';
  };

  it('one call of _ws_collect_witness_cad with its stderr dropped, no move of its own, no echo or printf', () => {
    const code = bodyOf('_ws_tmproot_witness_drop').split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l)).join('\n');
    expect(code.length, 'the drop could not be sliced').toBeGreaterThan(600);
    expect((code.match(/_ws_collect_witness_cad\b[^\n]*2>\/dev\/null/g) ?? []).length, 'one call, its stderr dropped').toBe(1);
    expect(code, 'it moves nothing itself: the compare-and-drop is the collector’s, never a copy').not.toMatch(/\b(?:_ws_collect_mv|mv)\s/);
    expect(code, 'it prints nothing').not.toMatch(/\b(?:printf|echo)\b/);
  });
});
```

```ts
// asks the device the witness records and the quarantine slots of the id, proves
// the leaf absent again, and unlinks only the generation it read (a compare-and-
```

```ts
/** Simulated Darwin on a Linux host: `_plat_devino`'s Darwin arm runs BSD `stat -f`, which GNU `stat` refuses, so the

const DEVINO_SHIM = process.platform === 'darwin' ? '' : "_plat_devino() { stat -c '%d:%i' \"$@\"; };";
```

```ts
describe('_ws_tmproot_witness_drop — the witness half, alone (spec §5.2; path-identity spec §3.2 and §3.3)', () => {
  const ID = 'demo-quiet-mesa';
  /** A leaf and the witness the REAL writer writes for it. */
  const plant = (): string => {
    fs.mkdirSync(leaf(ID), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(leaf(ID), 'scratch'), 'the leaf’s own');
    h.sh(`_ws_tmproot_witness_write ${ID} '${leaf(ID)}' 7`);
    expect(fs.existsSync(witness(ID)), 'the CONTROL: the witness was written').toBe(true);
    return fs.readFileSync(witness(ID), 'utf8');
  };
  /** The drop, its stderr merged IN FRONT of its answer: anything it printed comes before `[rc=`. */
  const drop = (id: string): { code: number; out: string } => {
    const r = h.run(`exec 2>&1; _ws_tmproot_witness_drop '${id}'; echo "[rc=$?] \${_WS_WDROP-}|\${_WS_WDROP_WHY-}"`);
    return { code: r.code, out: r.stdout + r.stderr };
  };

  it('a leaf that STANDS keeps its witness: the drop proves the absence again, answers kept, and touches nothing', () => {
    const bytes = plant();
    expect(drop(ID).out).toMatch(/^\[rc=1\] \|its witness was kept: a leaf stands at /);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(witness(ID), 'utf8'), 'the witness stays, byte for byte').toBe(bytes);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(leaf(ID), 'scratch'), 'utf8'), 'the leaf stands').toBe('the leaf’s own');
  });

  it('the leaf gone: the drop removes the witness and nothing else — tmproots/ stays', () => {
    plant();
    fs.rmSync(leaf(ID), { recursive: true, force: true });
    expect(drop(ID).out).toBe('[rc=0] dropped|');
    expect(fs.existsSync(witness(ID))).toBe(false);
    expect(fs.statSync(wdir()).isDirectory()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('a LINKED tmproots/ is never followed: unmeasured (rc 2), nothing printed, and the file it reaches stands', () => {
    const bytes = plant();
    fs.rmSync(leaf(ID), { recursive: true, force: true });
    const elsewhere = path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere');
    fs.renameSync(wdir(), elsewhere);
    fs.symlinkSync(elsewhere, wdir());
    const r = drop(ID);
    expect(r.out, 'nothing printed before the answer').toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] \|its witness was kept: /);
    expect(r.out).not.toContain('ccd: warn');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(elsewhere, ID), 'utf8'), 'the link’s target is untouched').toBe(bytes);
  });

  it.each([['.demo-quiet-mesa.4242.17.tmp'], ['.x']])('an id no witness is named for (%j) is refused, rc 1, its reason in _WS_WDROP_WHY and nothing printed — a planted file of that name stands', (id) => {
    fs.mkdirSync(wdir(), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(witness(id), 'a writer’s in-flight temp file');
    const r = drop(id);
    expect(r.out).toMatch(/^\[rc=1\] \|its witness was kept: /);
    expect(r.out).toContain(`'${id}' is not an id a witness is named for`);
    expect(r.out).not.toContain('ccd: warn');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(witness(id), 'utf8')).toBe('a writer’s in-flight temp file');
  });

  it('a directory at the witness name is no witness ccd wrote: unmeasured (rc 2), nothing printed, and it stands', () => {
    plant();
    fs.rmSync(leaf(ID), { recursive: true, force: true });
    fs.rmSync(witness(ID));
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(witness(ID), 'inside'), { recursive: true });
    const r = drop(ID);
    expect(r.out).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] \|its witness was kept: /);
    expect(r.out).not.toContain('ccd: warn');
    expect(fs.statSync(witness(ID)).isDirectory()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**4c. `_ws_tmproot_remove` and `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop`.** Replace the whole range Step 0 (o) measured with the block below. The range runs from the line `# THE TEMP ROOT'S REMOVAL (spec §5.6 and §5.2): the ONE removal helper on` through the `}` that closes `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop`, directly above `_ws_leaf_why_line() {`. That is 57 lines at the export, hints `:31945` to `:32001`, and holds both headers and both functions.
```bash
# THE TEMP ROOT'S REMOVAL (spec §5.6 and §5.2): the ONE removal helper on
# the temp root, then — on its rc 0 only, the leaf removed or PROVEN
# absent — the leaf's witness (`_ws_tmproot_witness_drop`). Remove, prove,
# THEN drop the witness: a crash between the last two leaves a witness with
# no leaf, which is nothing to do and is cleaned by the next call; the
# reverse order could leave a leaf with no witness, which no collector may
# ever take. A refusal or an unmeasured answer leaves the witness beside the
# leaf it still describes.
# THE ANSWER IS THE LEAF'S AND THE DROP'S (path-identity spec §3.2). A drop
# that keeps the witness (its 1) or could not measure (its 2) makes this
# helper answer 2, `_WS_LEAF_WHY` reading "no leaf stands, but " and the
# drop's reason (step (6)'s own lead, true whether the leaf half removed the
# leaf or PROVED it absent), so the tail records the temp root `unmeasured`
# with that reason. Never 1: this helper's 1 means the leaf was refused, and
# no leaf stands here.
# The tail passes NO dev:ino (the row and the marker prove identity there,
# and the check-to-rm window is `_ws_leaf_remove`'s own stated residual).
# The optional second argument hands an expected dev:ino through to
# `_ws_leaf_remove`; no caller in ccd passes one: the collector removes its
# slot's leaf through `_ws_leaf_remove` itself, and drops a witness by its
# own compare-and-drop (`_ws_collect_witness_cad`).
# An id no witness is named for (`_ws_tmproot_id_ok`: anything dot-leading,
# `.`, `..` and the writer's own `.<id>.*.tmp` names among them) is refused
# FIRST, rc 1 with `_WS_LEAF_WHY`, and nothing is asked or touched: a
# collector walking `tmproots/` must never turn a writer's temp file into a
# leaf to remove. The writer refuses the same ids, so such a leaf was never
# witnessed either; the tail keeps and records it, a leak and never a loss.
# WHO DROPS A WITNESS (spec §5.2): this helper, after its own rc 0; and the
# tail's step (6), on its in-use and unmeasured arms, ONLY when
# `_ws_reclaim_absent` PROVES no leaf stands (spec §5.6) — the witness of a
# leaf that is gone is nothing to keep, and after the row's purge nothing
# would ask about that id again. Those arms call the drop alone, never this
# helper: its leaf half would remove, unprobed, a leaf re-created after the
# absence was proven. Either way the drop decides, by its own proofs,
# whether the witness dies.
_ws_tmproot_remove() {   # id [expect-devino] -> 0 the leaf removed or PROVEN absent, and its witness drop complete | 1 the leaf refused | 2 unmeasured: the leaf, or a drop that kept the witness (_WS_LEAF_WHY)
  local id="${1-}" rc=0
  _ws_tmproot_id_ok "$id" || { _WS_LEAF_WHY="'$id' is not an id a witness is named for, so nothing was touched"; return 1; }
  if [[ -n "${2-}" ]]; then
    _ws_leaf_remove "$HOME/.cc-tmp" "$id" "$2"; rc=$?
  else
    _ws_leaf_remove "$HOME/.cc-tmp" "$id"; rc=$?
  fi
  (( rc == 0 )) || return "$rc"
  _ws_tmproot_witness_drop "$id" && return 0
  _WS_LEAF_WHY="no leaf stands, but $_WS_WDROP_WHY"
  return 2
}
# THE WITNESS'S DEATH (path-identity spec §3.2 and §3.3, Figure 3): the
# witness of `<id>` is dropped only on a PROVEN absence of its leaf, on the
# device the witness records, beside no quarantine slot of the id, and only
# in the generation this call read. Its callers are `_ws_tmproot_remove`,
# after its leaf half answers 0, and the reclaim tail's step (6) on its kept
# arms, once `_ws_reclaim_absent` has proven no leaf stands; both run under
# the id's reap lock.
# THREE ANSWERS, and every reason in `_WS_WDROP_WHY` begins "its witness was
# kept: " and names its cause before any path, which follows in parentheses:
#   0 complete — `_WS_WDROP` is `dropped` (exactly the generation read was
#     unlinked) or `absent` (no witness stood, at the read or at the compare,
#     PROVEN by `_ws_reclaim_absent`: never read off a failed test, because a
#     `tmproots/` this process cannot search reads `-e` false);
#   1 kept — a quarantine slot of the id stands, whether or not a record names
#     it; a leaf stands at `~/.cc-tmp/<id>` again; a newer generation stands
#     (or one this call did not read is stranded at a compare-and-drop aside);
#     or the id is no witness's name, and nothing is touched;
#   2 unmeasured — no witness was read, but its absence could not be proven;
#     the witness does not parse (a `tmproots/` that is a link included: never
#     followed); the physical `~/.cc-tmp` is on another device
#     or its device cannot be read; the quarantine cannot be listed; the
#     leaf's absence cannot be proven again; or the compare could not finish.
# THE ORDER IS FIXED: the read, the device the witness records
# (`_ws_collect_root_dev`), the slots (`_ws_collect_slots_of`), the leaf's
# absence proven again (`_ws_reclaim_absent`), then the drop. The device
# comes BEFORE the slots: with `~/.cc-tmp` deleted whole, or its volume
# missing and its mount point standing empty, every slot under it reads
# absent, and "no slot" would license the drop. The absence is proven again
# HERE because the caller's proof came before this read: a leaf re-created
# between the two keeps its witness, so "kept" always means "not proven gone".
# TWO WAYS TO DROP. Where `mv` makes a NOREPLACE rename (`_ws_collect_mv_ok`),
# the collector's own compare-and-drop, `_ws_collect_witness_cad`, is called
# with the fields of THIS read: moved aside, compared, unlinked there only if
# equal, and moved back otherwise — no window. Where it does not (Darwin, or
# an `mv` without `--no-copy`), the witness is read a second time, all six
# fields are compared with the first read, and only an equal one is unlinked
# and proven gone. The window from that second read to the unlink is a stated
# residual (`tail-drop-not-noreplace-without-mv-no-copy`): a writer that lands
# in it loses the witness of a leaf that is not gone, which leaks that leaf
# (nothing collects what no witness names) and never loses it.
# IT PRINTS NOTHING: the reason reaches the journal through the caller's row.
# The compare-and-drop warns once on stderr when it cannot move what it moved
# aside back; that call's stderr is dropped here, and the kept reason is
# chosen by a look at the witness's name instead — nothing there means the
# move back failed and the generation it moved aside stands at its aside;
# otherwise a newer generation stands at the name.
_WS_WDROP=''; _WS_WDROP_WHY=''
_ws_tmproot_witness_drop() {   # id -> 0 complete (_WS_WDROP dropped or absent); 1 kept; 2 unmeasured (both with _WS_WDROP_WHY)
  local id="${1-}" w leaf rc run dev ino bt uid at
  local _WS_WIT_DEV='' _WS_WIT_INO='' _WS_WIT_BTIME='' _WS_WIT_RUN='' _WS_WIT_UID='' _WS_WIT_AT='' _WS_CAD='' _WS_CAD_WHY=''
  local -a _WS_QSLOTS=()
  _WS_WDROP=''; _WS_WDROP_WHY=''
  _ws_tmproot_id_ok "$id" || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: '$id' is not an id a witness is named for, so no witness was touched"; return 1; }
  w=$(_ws_tmproot_witness_file "$id"); leaf="$HOME/.cc-tmp/$id"
  _ws_tmproot_witness_read "$id"; rc=$?
  (( rc != 1 )) || { _ws_reclaim_absent "$w" && { _WS_WDROP=absent; return 0; }   # no witness stands, PROVEN: nothing to drop
    _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: no witness was read at its name, and its absence could not be proven (${_WS_ABSENT_WHY:-something stands at $w})"; return 2; }
  (( rc == 0 )) || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: it cannot be read as ccd writes it, so the generation it names was never read ($w; a link at ${w%/*} is never followed)"; return 2; }
  run="$_WS_WIT_RUN"; dev="$_WS_WIT_DEV"; ino="$_WS_WIT_INO"; bt="$_WS_WIT_BTIME"; uid="$_WS_WIT_UID"; at="$_WS_WIT_AT"
  _ws_collect_root_dev "$dev" "the witness of $id" || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: the physical ~/.cc-tmp was not proven on the device the witness records ($_WS_ROOTDEV_WHY)"; return 2; }
  _ws_collect_slots_of "$id" || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: the quarantine slots of the id could not be listed ($_WS_QSLOTS_WHY)"; return 2; }
  (( ${#_WS_QSLOTS[@]} == 0 )) || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: the quarantine slot ${_WS_QSLOTS[0]##*/} of $id stands, so the collector lists it"; return 1; }
  _ws_reclaim_absent "$leaf"; rc=$?   # the absence, proven again here
  (( rc != 1 )) || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: a leaf stands at $leaf again, so the leaf it names is not proven gone"; return 1; }
  (( rc == 0 )) || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: the absence of the leaf could not be proven again ($_WS_ABSENT_WHY)"; return 2; }
  if _ws_collect_mv_ok; then   # a NOREPLACE rename exists: the collector's compare-and-drop, with this read's fields
    _ws_collect_witness_cad "$id" "$dev" "$ino" "$bt" "$run" "$at" 2>/dev/null \
      || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: the compare-and-drop could not finish, so it was never compared and dropped ($_WS_CAD_WHY)"; return 2; }
    case "$_WS_CAD" in dropped|absent) _WS_WDROP="$_WS_CAD"; return 0 ;; esac
    _ws_reclaim_absent "$w" && { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: a generation this tail did not read could not be moved back from its compare-and-drop aside, where it stands, so nothing stands at its name ($w)"; return 1; }
    _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: a newer generation stands at $w"; return 1
  fi
  # NO NOREPLACE RENAME: a second read, six fields compared, then the unlink.
  _ws_tmproot_witness_read "$id"; rc=$?
  (( rc != 1 )) || { _ws_reclaim_absent "$w" && { _WS_WDROP=absent; return 0; }   # it went since the first read, PROVEN
    _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: on a second read no witness was read at its name, and its absence could not be proven (${_WS_ABSENT_WHY:-something stands at $w})"; return 2; }
  (( rc == 0 )) || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: on a second read it cannot be read as ccd writes it, so it was never dropped ($w)"; return 2; }
  [[ "$_WS_WIT_RUN" == "$run" && "$_WS_WIT_DEV" == "$dev" && "$_WS_WIT_INO" == "$ino" && "$_WS_WIT_BTIME" == "$bt" && "$_WS_WIT_UID" == "$uid" && "$_WS_WIT_AT" == "$at" ]] \
    || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: a newer generation stands at $w"; return 1; }
  rm -f -- "$w" 2>/dev/null || :
  _ws_reclaim_absent "$w" || { _WS_WDROP_WHY="its witness was kept: its unlink could not be proven ($w${_WS_ABSENT_WHY:+: $_WS_ABSENT_WHY})"; return 2; }
  _WS_WDROP=dropped; return 0
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped file outside the tree and writes the one-mutation helper:

```bash
S="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/path-identity-w2-task6"; mkdir -p "$S" && cp ccd/ccd "$S/ccd.task6" && cat > "$S/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused unless every anchor matches exactly once.
//   node mut.mjs FILE sub OLD NEW          replace the ONE occurrence of OLD with NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE del NEEDLE...        delete each ONE line holding NEEDLE
//   node mut.mjs FILE range START END NEW  replace the ONE line holding START, through the first line from there that
//                                          holds END, with the single line NEW
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, mode, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const lines = src.split('\n');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const one = (needle) => {
  const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(needle) ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(needle)} is on ${at.length} lines, not one`);
  return at[0];
};
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a;
  const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'del') {
  const drop = new Set(a.map(one));
  out = lines.filter((_, i) => !drop.has(i)).join('\n');
} else if (mode === 'range') {
  const [start, end, n] = a;
  const s = one(start);
  const e = lines.findIndex((l, i) => i >= s && l.includes(end));
  if (e < 0) fail(`no ${JSON.stringify(end)} at or after line ${s + 1}`);
  out = [...lines.slice(0, s), n, ...lines.slice(e + 1)].join('\n');
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```

Then each row is ONE Bash call, run from the workspace root in the foreground with a timeout of at least 600000 ms. The call applies the mutation, runs the named cases, and restores the file whatever vitest answered. No mutation is restamped, because no suite these rows run reads the stamp. Every red below was drafted, not measured, so record the measured text in the ledger. A case listed as red that stays green is a STOP, reported by its row number.

```bash
_ws_tmproot_witness_drop now reads and parses the witness, asks the
device the witness records, lists the quarantine slots of the id, proves
the leaf absent again, and only then drops exactly the generation it
read. Where mv has --no-copy it calls the collector's compare-and-drop
with the fields of its own read. Elsewhere (Darwin, or an mv without

is a stated residual (tail-drop-not-noreplace-without-mv-no-copy).

nothing: the compare-and-drop's one warning is silenced at its call and
carried as the reason (kept-witness-reason-in-the-row-not-on-stderr).
Proving the absence again is drop-helper-reproves-the-absence: a leaf
that stands again keeps its witness.

_ws_tmproot_remove reports a drop that is not complete as its own 2,
"no leaf stands, but" and the drop's reason, never 1: its leaf half's 0
means removed or proven absent, so that lead is true of both. ws-expire
reaches both through the shared tail. Step 6's two kept arms take the
drop's answer in the next commit.

The race-crash suite's tail-drop-ignores-a-recordless-slot residual is
closed: a later tail's drop keeps the witness beside the record's slot,
and those cases converge one collector round later.
```
