```ts
describe('the settle alone: its answers, and it prints nothing (path-identity spec §3.6)', () => {
  const ID = 'demo-quiet-mesa';
  const w = (): string => path.join(tmproots(), ID);
  /** One settle, sourced, its stderr folded into its stdout: what it prints is only the echo of its answer. */
  const SETTLE = (id: string, pre = ''): string =>
    `exec 2>&1; ${pre} _ws_tmproot_aside_settle '${id}'; echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_ASIDE_DID|$_WS_ASIDE_WHY"`;

  it('#18a: no tmproots/ at all: none, and nothing else is printed', () => {
    expect(fs.existsSync(tmproots()), 'the CONTROL: no tmproots/').toBe(false);
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID)).stdout).toBe('[rc=0] none|');
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18b: a sole aside and no witness: restored — the witness IS the aside’s inode (a link, never a copy)', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    fs.renameSync(w(), aside);
    const ino = inoAt(aside);
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID)).stdout).toBe('[rc=0] restored|');
    expect(inoAt(w()), 'the restored witness is the aside’s own inode').toBe(ino);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(w(), 'utf8')).toBe(body);
    expect(fs.existsSync(aside)).toBe(false);
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18c: an aside that is the witness (one inode, two names — a restore’s crash state): unlinked', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    fs.linkSync(w(), aside);
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID)).stdout).toBe('[rc=0] unlinked|');
    expect(fs.existsSync(aside)).toBe(false);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(w(), 'utf8')).toBe(body);
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18d: an aside of another generation beside the witness: left, named, and only the answer is printed', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    const older = body.replace(' run=7 ', ' run=8 ');
    fs.writeFileSync(aside, older);
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID)).stdout).toBe(`[rc=0] left|a compare-and-drop aside of ${ID} was left beside its witness,`
      + ` never restored over it: ${aside} (not the witness that stands at ${w()})`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(aside, 'utf8')).toBe(older);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(w(), 'utf8')).toBe(body);
  }, 30_000);

  it.each(['.demo-quiet-mesa.drop.1', '-x', '..'])('#18e: an id no witness is named for (%s): unmeasured, and nothing is looked at', (id) => {
    plantWitness(ID);
    fs.writeFileSync(asideOf(ID), 'x');
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(id)).stdout).toBe(`[rc=2] |'${id}' is not an id a witness is named for, so no aside of it was looked at`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(asideOf(ID), 'utf8')).toBe('x');
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18f: an aside that is the witness’s own inode, beside a witness that does not read as one: unlinked', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(tmproots(), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(w(), 'x');
    fs.linkSync(w(), asideOf(ID));
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID)).stdout).toBe('[rc=0] unlinked|');
    expect(fs.existsSync(asideOf(ID))).toBe(false);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(w(), 'utf8'), 'the witness stands as it was').toBe('x');
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18g: restored but not unlinked (the state a death between link and rm leaves): unmeasured, one inode under two names; the next settle unlinks the aside', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    fs.renameSync(w(), aside);
    const RM_FAILS = 'rm() { if [[ "$*" == *"/tmproots/."*".drop."* ]]; then return 1; fi; command rm "$@"; };';
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID, RM_FAILS)).stdout).toBe(`[rc=2] |the compare-and-drop aside of ${ID} was restored as its`
      + ` witness, but it could not be unlinked after, so one witness stands under two names until the next settle: ${aside}`);
    expect(inoAt(aside), 'one inode under two names').toBe(inoAt(w()));
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID)).stdout, 'the next settle reads it as the witness itself').toBe('[rc=0] unlinked|');
    expect(fs.existsSync(aside)).toBe(false);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(w(), 'utf8')).toBe(body);
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18h: the asides cannot be listed: unmeasured, and an aside it never listed is never read as none', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    fs.renameSync(w(), aside);
    const UNLISTED = '_ws_collect_asides_of() { _WS_ASIDES_WHY=stub; return 2; };';
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID, UNLISTED)).stdout)
      .toBe(`[rc=2] |the compare-and-drop asides of ${ID} could not be listed (stub), so none was settled`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(aside, 'utf8'), 'the aside stands as it was').toBe(body);
    expect(fs.existsSync(w()), 'nothing was restored').toBe(false);
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18i: whether a witness stands cannot be asked: unmeasured, and the one aside is untouched', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    fs.renameSync(w(), aside);
    // `_ws_reclaim_absent` cannot ask about the witness's own name (rc 2, `stub`); every other path is the real ask.
    const WITNESS_UNASKED = 'eval "_t_absent_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_absent | tail -n +2)";'
      + ` _ws_reclaim_absent() { if [[ "$1" == */tmproots/${ID} ]]; then _WS_ABSENT_WHY=stub; return 2; fi; _t_absent_real "$@"; };`;
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID, WITNESS_UNASKED)).stdout)
      .toBe(`[rc=2] |whether a witness of ${ID} stands could not be asked (stub), so no aside of it was settled`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(aside, 'utf8'), 'the aside stands as it was').toBe(body);
    expect(fs.existsSync(w()), 'nothing was restored').toBe(false);
  }, 30_000);

  it('#18j: a link that fails with no witness standing after: unmeasured, and the one aside is untouched', () => {
    const body = plantWitness(ID);
    const aside = asideOf(ID);
    fs.renameSync(w(), aside);
    const LINK_FAILS = 'link() { return 1; };';
    expect(h.run(SETTLE(ID, LINK_FAILS)).stdout).toBe(`[rc=2] |the compare-and-drop aside of ${ID} was not restored,`
      + ` and no witness is proven to stand at ${w()} after: ${aside}`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(aside, 'utf8'), 'the aside stands as it was').toBe(body);
    expect(fs.existsSync(w()), 'nothing was restored').toBe(false);
  }, 30_000);
});
```

Before:
```bash
_ws_leaf_why_line() {   # text -> ONE short line a journal row can carry: printable ASCII only (every
```
After:
```bash
# THE COMPARE-AND-DROP ASIDE, SETTLED (path-identity spec §3.6, TR6 A). The
# collector's compare-and-drop (`_ws_collect_witness_cad`), which the tail's
# drop reuses, moves a witness aside to `.<id>.drop.<pid>`
# (`_ws_tmproot_aside_path`) by one NOREPLACE rename, reads it there, then
# unlinks it or moves it back. A SIGKILL between the rename and the unlink, or
# a move back that fails, leaves that aside and no witness: no collector could
# finish the id, and no tail would drop it. This settles every aside of one id
# under the reap lock THE CALLER HOLDS (`$REG/.reap-<id>.lock`): ws-collect
# after its pause and before its evaluation, the reclaim and expiry tail before
# its step (6).
# - NO WITNESS STANDS: a SOLE aside that reads as the id's witness
#   (`_ws_tmproot_witness_parse`, the reader's own rules) is RESTORED by `link`,
#   then a dev:ino proof, then `rm` of the aside; never by a rename. `link` is
#   portable (the tail runs on Darwin, where `_ws_collect_mv` refuses), and it
#   refuses a name that exists, so a witness a spawn wrote meanwhile (its
#   writer takes no lock) is never replaced. Two or more asides, or one that
#   does not read as the witness, are never chosen between: unmeasured.
# - THE CRASH STATE IS SAFE: a death between the `link` and the `rm` leaves
#   one inode under two names, an aside EQUAL to the witness, which the next
#   settle unlinks.
# - A WITNESS STANDS (from the start, or a writer's that won the name, or one
#   that replaced the name after the link, which the dev:ino proof catches):
#   an aside that IS it (one inode) or reads as it field for field (the
#   grammar is canonical, so that is byte for byte) is redundant and goes; any
#   other is LEFT and named, never restored over the witness and never
#   unlinked, since it may be the generation a collector acted on.
# It PRINTS NOTHING: it answers by rc and by _WS_ASIDE_DID and _WS_ASIDE_WHY,
# and each caller says what a person reads. It never sets REAP_*.
_WS_ASIDE_DID=''; _WS_ASIDE_WHY=''
_ws_tmproot_aside_settle() {   # id -> 0 with _WS_ASIDE_DID = none | restored | unlinked | left (_WS_ASIDE_WHY names
  #                                each aside left, and why); 2 unmeasured (_WS_ASIDE_WHY). The CALLER HOLDS the lock
  local LC_ALL=C id="${1-}" w a rc wdi adi wf eq left=''
  local _WS_WIT_DEV _WS_WIT_INO _WS_WIT_BTIME _WS_WIT_RUN _WS_WIT_UID _WS_WIT_AT
  local -a _WS_ASIDES=()
  _WS_ASIDE_DID=''; _WS_ASIDE_WHY=''
  _ws_tmproot_id_ok "$id" \
    || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="'$id' is not an id a witness is named for, so no aside of it was looked at"; return 2; }
  _ws_collect_asides_of "$id" >/dev/null \
    || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="the compare-and-drop asides of $id could not be listed ($_WS_ASIDES_WHY), so none was settled"; return 2; }
  (( ${#_WS_ASIDES[@]} )) || { _WS_ASIDE_DID=none; return 0; }
  w=$(_ws_tmproot_witness_file "$id")
  _ws_reclaim_absent "$w"; rc=$?
  (( rc != 2 )) \
    || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="whether a witness of $id stands could not be asked ($_WS_ABSENT_WHY), so no aside of it was settled"; return 2; }
  if (( rc == 0 )); then
    (( ${#_WS_ASIDES[@]} == 1 )) \
      || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="${#_WS_ASIDES[@]} compare-and-drop asides of $id stand and no witness does, so which is its witness is never chosen: ${_WS_ASIDES[*]}"; return 2; }
    a="${_WS_ASIDES[0]}"
    _ws_tmproot_witness_parse "$a" "$id" \
      || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="the one compare-and-drop aside of $id does not read as its witness, so it is never restored: $a"; return 2; }
    if link "$a" "$w" 2>/dev/null; then
      adi=$(_plat_devino "$a" 2>/dev/null) || adi=''
      wdi=$(_plat_devino "$w" 2>/dev/null) || wdi=''
      if [[ "$adi" =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ && "$adi" == "$wdi" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$a" 2>/dev/null || :
        _ws_reclaim_absent "$a" \
          || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="the compare-and-drop aside of $id was restored as its witness, but it could not be unlinked after, so one witness stands under two names until the next settle: $a"; return 2; }
        _WS_ASIDE_DID=restored; return 0
      fi
    fi
    # THE RESTORE DID NOT TAKE: `link` refused a name a writer took first, or
    # the name was replaced after the link. What stands there now is asked
    # once more, and the witness-stands arm below runs ONCE.
    _ws_reclaim_absent "$w"; rc=$?
    (( rc == 1 )) \
      || { _WS_ASIDE_WHY="the compare-and-drop aside of $id was not restored, and no witness is proven to stand at $w after${_WS_ABSENT_WHY:+ ($_WS_ABSENT_WHY)}: $a"; return 2; }
  fi
  wdi=$(_plat_devino "$w" 2>/dev/null) || wdi=''
  [[ "$wdi" =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || wdi=''
  wf=''
  if _ws_tmproot_witness_parse "$w" "$id"; then
    wf="$_WS_WIT_RUN $_WS_WIT_DEV $_WS_WIT_INO $_WS_WIT_BTIME $_WS_WIT_UID $_WS_WIT_AT"
  fi
  for a in "${_WS_ASIDES[@]}"; do
    adi=$(_plat_devino "$a" 2>/dev/null) || adi=''
    eq=0
    if [[ -n "$wdi" && "$adi" == "$wdi" ]]; then
      eq=1
    elif [[ -n "$wf" ]] && _ws_tmproot_witness_parse "$a" "$id" \
         && [[ "$_WS_WIT_RUN $_WS_WIT_DEV $_WS_WIT_INO $_WS_WIT_BTIME $_WS_WIT_UID $_WS_WIT_AT" == "$wf" ]]; then
      eq=1
    fi
    if (( eq )); then
      rm -f -- "$a" 2>/dev/null || :
      _ws_reclaim_absent "$a" && continue
      left+="${left:+; }$a (the witness itself, but it could not be unlinked)"
    else
      left+="${left:+; }$a (not the witness that stands at $w)"
    fi
  done
  [[ -n "$left" ]] || { _WS_ASIDE_DID=unlinked; return 0; }
  _WS_ASIDE_DID=left
  _WS_ASIDE_WHY="a compare-and-drop aside of $id was left beside its witness, never restored over it: $left"
  return 0
}
```

```bash
  # COMPARE-AND-DROP (spec §5.10): the collector's, and since path-identity W2
```

First copy the restamped file, and write the one-anchor replacer, outside the tree:

```bash
S="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/path-identity-w2-task11"; mkdir -p "$S" && cp ccd/ccd "$S/ccd.task11" && cat > "$S/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// node mut.mjs <file> <old> <new>: replaces the ONE occurrence of <old>; exits 3, writing nothing, when <old> is not
// there exactly once.
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [f, a, b] = process.argv.slice(2);
const s = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
const n = s.split(a).length - 1;
if (n !== 1) { console.error(`anchor found ${n} times: ${a}`); process.exit(3); }
fs.writeFileSync(f, s.replace(a, () => b));
EOF
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Commit**

```bash
git add ccd/ccd server/test/ccd-collect-aside-settle.test.ts CLAUDE.md
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(ccd): an orphaned compare-and-drop aside is restored under the reap lock, in the verb and the tail

A SIGKILL inside the collector's compare-and-drop, or a move back that
fails, leaves the witness at .<id>.drop.<pid> and nothing under its own
name (path-identity spec §3.6). _ws_tmproot_aside_settle settles every
aside of one id under the reap lock its caller holds, and prints
nothing.

With no witness standing, a sole aside that reads as the id's witness
is restored by link, then a dev:ino proof, then rm of the aside. It is
never renamed, so a witness a spawn wrote meanwhile is never replaced.
A death between the link and the rm leaves one inode under two names,
which the next settle unlinks (aside-restore-by-link-not-rename). Two
or more asides, or one that does not read as the witness, are never
chosen between: unmeasured. Beside a standing witness, an aside that is
it (one inode, or the same fields) is unlinked, and any other is left
and named.

ws-collect settles after its pause and before its evaluation, so the
fork reads the restored witness and the audit's token matches. Its
doubt applies only where the evaluation would act; a refusal the fork
gives keeps its place, and the doubt is warned. The reclaim and expiry
tail settles before step (6), so the drop takes a restored witness with
its leaf. Its doubt only warns and never sets tmpRootKept
(tail-aside-warns-without-keeping).

The compare-and-drop's move-back warning no longer claims that a newer
witness stands when none does, or that no reader takes the aside. Its
header no longer calls _ws_tmproot_witness_drop the tail's plain
unlink, since that drop now reuses the compare-and-drop
(cad-header-calls-the-tail-drop-a-plain-unlink, closed here).

The new file's ws-expire case walks the real /proc through the expiry
ladder, so CLAUDE.md lists the file as a load flake.
EOF
```

- together: `archived-expiry-policy`, `ccd-refusal-scan`, `macos-platform` and `ccd-child-tmproot-witness` (the glob and find census).

**Deviation slots** (bare slugs):
- `aside-restore-by-link-not-rename` (R21);
- `tail-aside-warns-without-keeping` (R26);
- `cad-header-calls-the-tail-drop-a-plain-unlink` (R41: closed here, by 3f);

**Drafter's corrections:**
1. **"Byte-equal" is decided by `_ws_tmproot_witness_parse`, field for field, not by `_ws_leaf_read_small`.** The witness grammar is canonical, so equal fields are equal bytes. A body that does not parse is never "equal": a link, a non-regular file, or a malformed body. This needs no new guard and no read of Task 2's `_WS_SMALL_NUL`, so `_ws_leaf_read_small` leaves the consumed list. An aside that shares the witness's inode is still unlinked when the witness does not parse (#18f, T11.5b).
2. **There is no `command -v link` guard.** A missing `link` fails the link (rc 127), the name is asked again, and the settle answers rc 2. That is the contract's "link is unavailable or failed with no witness standing after", and it avoids a guard that no case could red. The rc 2 itself is pinned by #18j (a `link` that fails) and T11.25.
3. **The settle refuses an id `_ws_tmproot_id_ok` rejects (rc 2)** before it looks at anything (#18e, T11.16). Its callers already validate the id.
4. **The verb's `left` warning prints right after the settle, and its rc-2 warning prints after the fork.** Only after the fork is it known whether the fork's answer outranks the doubt. The doubt is weighed before the token compare, where the frame puts it ("after the fork's no verdict line").
5. **R41: the header's first sentence, which calls `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop` the tail's plain unlink, is reworded in place, and the slug `cad-header-calls-the-tail-drop-a-plain-unlink` closes with this commit.** That sentence has been false since Task 6 (P15). It sits in the paragraph whose dot-leading clause R27 deletes, so 3f edits that one paragraph where it stands and moves nothing else.
6. **Platforms.** The tail's cases (#13 to #15, #17) run on Linux without requiring `--no-copy`, because Task 6's fallback drops there. #16 and #18 run on both hosts. The collector's cases are Linux with `--no-copy`, as framed.
7. **Planted asides use pids 9999999 and 9999998**, above every kernel's pid ceiling. The frame's 4242 and 5 could, rarely, equal the `$BASHPID` that a compare-and-drop under test composes.
8. **Stderr is captured to a file.** `h.run` hands back stderr only on a non-zero exit, so every stderr assertion sends it to `$HOME/verb-err` (`extra`), or folds it with `exec 2>&1` (#18).
9. **Case 8's state is built by a crash at `moved`.** That leaves a record, a slot and a witness. The witness is then turned into two asides, and the resume token is the audit's own. The frame named no recipe.
10. **Case 11 is its own `it`** (the frame folds it into case 3), so that T11.2 has a red. T11.2 does not red case 3: settled after the fork, case 3 ends in the same state.
11. **Cases added:**
    - #4b, a writer that wins at the settle's own parse. Case 4's writer lives inside `link`, so a restore that does not call `link` could clobber without case 4 seeing it by bytes.
    - #6's byte-copy row, and #7's symlink row.
    - #12b, the warning's other arm.
    - #18a to #18g, direct calls: the answers, "prints nothing", the id guard, the inode arm beside an unparseable witness, and the crash state between `link` and `rm`, which the next settle unlinks (Review Focus 4).
    - #18h to #18j, direct calls, one for each unmeasured guard no other case reaches: the asides cannot be listed, a witness's absence cannot be asked, and a `link` that fails with no witness after. Without them, deleting any of the three leaves the file green (the Global Constraints' mutation discipline).
12. **Mutation rows added:** T11.5b, T11.5c, T11.13b, and T11.14 to T11.25. Each pins a guard or a warning this task introduces.
13. **Gates added:** `ccd-collect-aside-admission`, `ccd-collect-aside-grammar`, `ccd-tmproot-drop-propagation`, `ccd-wsaudit-nonpoison`, `wsaudit`, `ccd-collect-header-prose`, `ccd-child-reclaim-tail-contained`, `collect-readers`, `ccd-id-cap`, the danglers pass and the typecheck.
14. **The export cannot show Tasks 6 to 10.** Their names, the drop helper, the lister and the aside judge, are taken from §Interfaces, and Step 0 measures each of them before any edit. Line hints are export lines and move with those tasks' inserts.
15. **R45: #17 walks `/proc` through the expiry ladder.** The draft said no case walks `/proc`, which holds for the in-use probe only. #17's expiry audit and verb run `_ws_expire_cwd_users` unstubbed, so the file joins CLAUDE.md's load-flake list in this commit (Step 7a), its header says so, and Step 5 records the walk.

**Model routing:** `opus`, effort `high`. `ccd-lifecycle-contain` goes red as soon as ccd writes `meas.leaf` without L0 declaring it. So the emit, the encoder, L0, the reviver and the count all go in one commit.

```ts
// path-identity W2 (spec 2026-10-12 §3.4, TR1 A): a `collect` `done` journals the leaf it ended on. The witness-only
// arm's `done` and a real removal's `done` carried the same keys, so a reader could not tell a collection that removed
// a leaf from one that found nothing there. `meas.leaf` tells them apart: `removed` on `_ws_collect_finish`'s line (the
// slot's leaf proven gone after this collection removed it), `absent` on `_ws_collect_witness_only`'s (no leaf stood at
// the witness's path). The encoder's meas rung keeps `leaf` when it drops every other meas field, and so does its
// last-resort line, so a collect line cut twice still says which it was; a line that passed no `leaf` is cut as before.
// The reviver carries `leaf` and never folds a PRESENT value into null. The words are L0's (`COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS`),
// and ccd writes exactly those, both directions.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makeCcdHarness`, `makePrHarness`): every path derives from `h.home`, and ccd runs as SOURCED
// functions, never through the installed launcher and never against the live HOME. The encoder, census and reviver
// cases run everywhere. The verb cases run on Linux where `mv --no-copy` exists (`collectRaceFixture.ts`), and every
// audit and verb there carries that fixture's `COLLECT_STUBS`, so no case walks the real /proc.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS, LIFECYCLE_MEAS_KEYS, isCollectLeafEndWord } from '../../shared/api.js';
import { parseJournalLine, reviveMeas } from '../src/coord/journalparse.js';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD, makeCcdHarness, type CcdHarness } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { NO_TMUX, eventsOf, readJournal } from './lifecycleHelpers.js';
import {
  COL_ID, LINUX, NO_COPY, collectVerb, crashAt, crashedAt, docOf, leafOf, orphanLeaf, recordsOf, tokenOf,
} from './collectRaceFixture.js';

/** The last `collect` `done` line in a fixture HOME's journal. */
const lastDone = (home: string): Record<string, unknown> => {
  const done = eventsOf(home, 'collect').filter((e) => e['outcome'] === 'done');
  expect(done.length, 'the CONTROL: a collect done line was journaled').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  return done[done.length - 1]!;
};

describe.skipIf(!LINUX || !NO_COPY)('a collect done journals the leaf it ended on (path-identity spec §3.4): the verb', () => {
  let h: PrHarness;
  beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-collect-leaf-meas-'); });
  afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

  it('case 1: a collection that removes the leaf journals meas.leaf removed, and no resumed', () => {
    orphanLeaf(h);
    const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h));
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout)).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, resumed: false, witness: 'dropped' });
    expect(fs.existsSync(leafOf(h)), 'the CONTROL: the leaf went').toBe(false);
    const done = lastDone(h.home);
    expect(done['verb']).toBe('ws-collect');
    expect(done['meas'], 'a fresh collection passes an empty resumed, which the encoder omits').toEqual({ leaf: 'removed' });
  }, 60_000);

  it('case 2: the witness-only arm journals meas exactly { leaf: absent }', () => {
    orphanLeaf(h);
    fs.rmSync(leafOf(h), { recursive: true });
    const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h));
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r.stdout), 'the CONTROL: the witness-only arm answered')
      .toEqual({ collected: COL_ID, record: null, resumed: false, witness: 'dropped' });
    expect(lastDone(h.home)['meas']).toEqual({ leaf: 'absent' });
  }, 60_000);

  for (const point of ['moved', 'removed', 'emptied', 'witnessed'] as const) {
    it(`case 3: killed at ${point}, the resume journals meas.leaf removed beside the record it finished`, () => {
      orphanLeaf(h);
      collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h), COL_ID, crashAt(point));
      expect(crashedAt(h), 'the CONTROL: the kill fired where it was aimed').toBe(point);
      const recs = recordsOf(h);
      expect(recs, 'the CONTROL: the record stands, for the resume to finish from').toHaveLength(1);
      const r = collectVerb(h, tokenOf(h));
      expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
      expect(docOf(r.stdout)).toMatchObject({ collected: COL_ID, record: recs[0], resumed: true });
      expect(lastDone(h.home)['meas']).toEqual({ resumed: recs[0], leaf: 'removed' });
    }, 90_000);
  }
});

describe('the encoder keeps leaf through its truncation ladder (path-identity spec §3.4)', () => {
  let h: CcdHarness;
  beforeEach(() => { h = makeCcdHarness('ccrc-collect-leaf-enc-'); });
  afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });
  const R = 'r'.repeat(2100);
  const D = 'd'.repeat(4000);
  /** The one line `snippet` journaled. */
  const only = (snippet: string): Record<string, unknown> => {
    h.sh(`${NO_TMUX} ${snippet}`);
    const all = readJournal(h.home);
    expect(all, 'the CONTROL: exactly one line was written').toHaveLength(1);
    return all[0]!;
  };

  it('case 4: the meas rung drops every meas field but leaf, and keeps detail', () => {
    const e = only(`_lc_emit collect done demo-quiet-basin "" verb ws-collect meas.resumed '${R}' meas.leaf removed detail short`);
    expect(e['truncated'], 'the line was cut').toBe(true);
    expect(e['meas'], 'the meas rung kept leaf alone').toEqual({ leaf: 'removed' });
    expect(e['detail'], 'the meas rung fired, not the last resort').toBe('short');
    expect(Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(e), 'utf8')).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2048);
    const row = parseJournalLine(JSON.stringify(e));
    expect([row.truncated, row.meas?.leaf, row.meas?.resumed], 'the mirror reads the cut line decided')
      .toEqual([true, 'removed', null]);
  });

  it('case 5: the last-resort line keeps leaf, and nothing else of meas', () => {
    const e = only(`_lc_emit collect done demo-quiet-basin "" verb ws-collect meas.resumed '${R}' meas.leaf absent detail '${D}'`);
    expect(e['truncated']).toBe(true);
    expect(e['detail'], 'the last resort fired: it keeps no detail').toBeUndefined();
    expect(e['meas'], 'the last resort keeps leaf').toEqual({ leaf: 'absent' });
    expect(Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(e), 'utf8')).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2048);
    expect(parseJournalLine(JSON.stringify(e)).meas?.leaf).toBe('absent');
  });

  it('case 5b: a last-resort line that passed no leaf writes no meas key, as before', () => {
    const e = only(`_lc_emit collect done demo-quiet-basin "" verb ws-collect detail '${D}'`);
    expect(e['truncated']).toBe(true);
    expect(e['detail']).toBeUndefined();
    expect(Object.keys(e), 'the last resort of a leafless line is the joinable minimum it always was').not.toContain('meas');
  });

  it('case 6: a cut line that passed no leaf writes meas null at the meas rung, never {}', () => {
    // `childReclaimMirrorLeaf`'s truncated arm reads `meas === null` on a cut reclaim line; a `{}` there would read the
    // cut line as "nothing kept", and drop a kept-leaf item in silence.
    const e = only(`_lc_emit reclaim done demo-x "" verb ws-reclaim meas.workdir '${'w'.repeat(2100)}'`);
    expect(e['truncated']).toBe(true);
    expect(e['meas']).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('the leaf words ccd writes are L0s, both directions (path-identity spec §3.4)', () => {
  it('case 7: every meas.leaf word in ccd is in COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS, and every one of them is written', () => {
    const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
    const written = [...src.matchAll(/\bmeas\.leaf\s+([a-z-]+)/g)].map((m) => m[1]!);
    expect(written, 'the two `_lc_done collect` lines, each naming one word').toHaveLength(2);
    expect(COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS, 'the CONTROL: L0 declares two words').toHaveLength(2);
    expect([...new Set(written)].sort()).toEqual([...COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS].sort());
    for (const w of written) expect(isCollectLeafEndWord(w), w).toBe(true);
  });

  it('case 7b: isCollectLeafEndWord admits the two words and nothing else, the audit document’s present included', () => {
    for (const w of COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS) expect(isCollectLeafEndWord(w), w).toBe(true);
    for (const v of ['present', 'gone', '', 'REMOVED', 'toString', 7, null, undefined, {}]) {
      expect(isCollectLeafEndWord(v), String(v)).toBe(false);
    }
  });
});

describe('the reviver carries leaf, and never folds a present value into null (path-identity spec §3.4)', () => {
  it.each<readonly [string, Record<string, unknown>, string | null]>([
    ['absent key', {}, null],
    ['JSON null', { leaf: null }, null],
    ['removed', { leaf: 'removed' }, 'removed'],
    ['absent', { leaf: 'absent' }, 'absent'],
    ['a word ccd never writes', { leaf: 'gone' }, 'gone'],
    ['the empty string', { leaf: '' }, ''],
    ['a number', { leaf: 7 }, '7'],
    ['an object', { leaf: {} }, '{}'],
    ['a boolean', { leaf: true }, 'true'],
  ])('case 8: %s', (_what, meas, want) => {
    const once = reviveMeas(meas);
    expect(once!.leaf).toBe(want);
    // The store keeps `JSON.stringify` of the REVIVED object and revives it again on every read: one definition, both
    // directions, and a stored `"leaf":null` must read back as the key it was, not carried.
    expect(reviveMeas(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(once)))).toEqual(once);
  });

  it('case 8: a collect done line carries its leaf through parseJournalLine, and a line without one reads null', () => {
    const lineWith = (meas: unknown): string => JSON.stringify({
      v: 1, uid: '1790000000000000000.1.1', atNs: '1790000000000000000', at: 1_790_000_000_000, act: 'collect',
      outcome: 'done', id: 'demo-quiet-basin', dec: { surface: 'none' }, meas,
    });
    expect(parseJournalLine(lineWith({ leaf: 'absent' })).meas?.leaf).toBe('absent');
    expect(parseJournalLine(lineWith({ resumed: 'x' })).meas?.leaf).toBeNull();
    expect(parseJournalLine(lineWith(null)).meas).toBeNull();
  });

  it('case 9: the revived key list is the derived L0 list, and it holds leaf', () => {
    expect(LIFECYCLE_MEAS_KEYS).toContain('leaf');
    expect(Object.keys(reviveMeas({})!).sort()).toEqual([...LIFECYCLE_MEAS_KEYS].sort());
  });
});
```

```ts

/** What a `collect` `done` journals of the leaf it acted on (path-identity spec §3.4, TR1 A): `removed` on
 *  `_ws_collect_finish`'s line (the slot's leaf proven gone after this collection removed it), `absent` on the
 *  witness-only arm's (no leaf stood at the witness's path). Spelled ONCE, as a total table's keys. Not the audit
 *  document's `collect.leaf` (`present`/`absent`), which is another wire. APPENDED at the foot, never inserted above:
 *  README and the frozen spec and plan corpus cite this file by line. */
export type CollectLeafEndWord = 'removed' | 'absent';
const COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE: Readonly<Record<CollectLeafEndWord, true>> = { removed: true, absent: true };
export const COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS: readonly CollectLeafEndWord[] = Object.keys(COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE) as CollectLeafEndWord[];
export function isCollectLeafEndWord(v: unknown): v is CollectLeafEndWord {
  return typeof v === 'string' && (COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS as readonly string[]).includes(v);
}
```

The foot. Append after `parseJournalLine`'s closing `}` (the file's last line), with one blank line before it. It is a hoisted declaration, so `reviveMeas` above may call it:
```ts

/** `meas.leaf`'s reviver (path-identity spec §3.4). Absent, or a JSON null, is `null`: the key was not carried. A JSON
 *  null is the store's own spelling of that, since `reviveMeas` writes every key and the store keeps that object. A
 *  string is itself, whatever its word. Any other PRESENT value is its JSON text, so a present value is never read as
 *  absent. Declared at the foot, below every line the frozen plan corpus cites. */
function presentAsText(o: Obj, k: string): string | null {
  const v = o[k];
  if (v === undefined || v === null) return null;
  return typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v);
}
```

First, write the mutation script and snapshot the three source files, outside the tree:

```bash
S="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/path-identity-w2-task12"; mkdir -p "$S" && cat > "$S/mut.cjs" <<'EOF'
// path-identity W2 Task 12: one mutation row at a time, run from the workspace root. `snap` copies the three source
// files here; `<row>` applies that row's exact edits, each refusing unless its old text occurs exactly once;
// `restore` copies the three back.
'use strict';
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const FILES = { ccd: 'ccd/ccd', api: 'shared/api.ts', jp: 'server/src/coord/journalparse.ts' };
const RUNG = 'ev["meas"] = {"leaf": meas["leaf"]} if "leaf" in meas else None; ev["truncated"] = True';
const ROWS = {
  'T12.1': [['ccd', 'meas.resumed "$resumed" meas.leaf removed', 'meas.resumed "$resumed"']],
  'T12.2': [['ccd', 'meas.resumed "" meas.leaf absent', 'meas.resumed ""']],
  'T12.3': [['ccd', 'meas.resumed "$resumed" meas.leaf removed', 'meas.resumed "$resumed" meas.leaf absent'],
            ['ccd', 'meas.resumed "" meas.leaf absent', 'meas.resumed "" meas.leaf removed']],
  'T12.4': [['ccd', RUNG, 'ev["meas"] = None; ev["truncated"] = True']],
  'T12.5': [['ccd', RUNG, 'ev["meas"] = meas or None; ev["truncated"] = True']],
  'T12.6': [['ccd', ', "truncated": True, **({"meas": {"leaf": meas["leaf"]}} if "leaf" in meas else {})}', ', "truncated": True}']],
  'T12.7': [['ccd', 'if "leaf" in meas else None; ev["truncated"] = True', 'if "leaf" in meas else {}; ev["truncated"] = True']],
  'T12.8': [['ccd', 'a row rather than a silence.', "a row rather than a silence's."]],
  'T12.9': [['jp', "leaf: presentAsText(o, 'leaf'),", "leaf: s(o, 'leaf'),"]],
  'T12.10': [['jp', "return typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v);",
              "return typeof v === 'string' ? (v === 'removed' || v === 'absent' ? v : null) : JSON.stringify(v);"]],
  'T12.11': [['api', ' */ readonly leaf: string | null;', ' */'], ['api', 'clipsKept: true, leaf: true,', 'clipsKept: true,']],
  'T12.12': [['ccd', 'if "leaf" in meas else {})}', 'if "leaf" in meas else {"meas": None})}']],
  'T12.13': [['jp', 'if (v === undefined || v === null) return null;', 'if (v === undefined) return null;']],
};
const cmd = process.argv[2];
if (cmd === 'snap' || cmd === 'restore') {
  for (const [k, f] of Object.entries(FILES)) {
    if (cmd === 'snap') fs.copyFileSync(f, path.join(__dirname, k)); else fs.copyFileSync(path.join(__dirname, k), f);
  }
  process.exit(0);
}
const row = ROWS[cmd];
if (!row) { console.error(`no row ${cmd}`); process.exit(2); }
for (const [k, a, b] of row) {
  const f = FILES[k];
  const s = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
  const n = s.split(a).length - 1;
  if (n !== 1) { console.error(`${cmd}: ${f} holds ${n} copies of: ${a}`); process.exit(2); }
  fs.writeFileSync(f, s.replace(a, () => b));
}
EOF
node "$S/mut.cjs" snap && ls "$S"
```

### Task 13: A kept-leaf item ends only on a removal, and an absence keeps it with a clause (TR1 A, TR2 A; R16, R17, R18; `leaf-end-acts-spelled-twice`)

**Model routing:** `opus`, effort `xhigh`. A misread here does one of two things. It ends a line whose leaf still stands, or it brings back, on the day of the deploy, three lines that were correctly ended.

**Why:** spec §3.4.
- The store passes `measJson` and `truncated` raw. L1 reads them into four kinds (R16).
- The decision is monotone:
  - any row that ends the half ends it, whatever its place;
  - otherwise, any `absent` adds the clause;
  - otherwise, the item stands.
- An item that ended on `absent` never joins the collapse (R17).
- An appended block pins the vocabulary once (R18).
- The two end acts are spelled once (R36).
- The store's own encoding forces two folds, and each is named:
  - A stored `"leaf":null` reads as keyless. This is the departure `present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy` (P3).
  - A `meas` that is not an object is stored as NULL and reads as keyless. This is the residual `non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless`. ccd's encoder never writes such a `meas`.

```ts
// path-identity W2 (spec 2026-10-12 §3.4): the kept-leaf end, from ccd's encoder to L1's decision. A `collect` `done`
// line cut to fit at the encoder's meas rung keeps `meas.leaf`; the parser, the store and L1's reader carry it; and the
// decision reads it exactly as it reads an uncut line, which is the spec's "still drives the same decision": `removed`
// ends the temp-root half, `absent` keeps the line with the found-nothing clause. One residual is pinned as it stands:
// a `meas` that is not a JSON object is stored as no `meas` at all, reads as an older ccd's keyless line, and ends the
// half (`non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless`; ccd's encoder never writes one, so that line is built by hand).
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makeCcdHarness`): `_lc_emit` writes into the harness HOME's journal, never the live one. No
// collector runs, so no case walks `/proc`.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { LC_LINE_MAX } from '../../shared/api.js';
import { openCoordDb } from '../src/coord/db.js';
import { CoordStore } from '../src/coord/store.js';
import { parseJournalLine } from '../src/coord/journalparse.js';
import {
  childReclaimLeafFoundNothing, childReclaimLeafKept, childReclaimLeafKeptSince, type ChildReclaimLeafKept,
} from '../src/childReclaimSweep.js';
import { makeCcdHarness, type CcdHarness } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { NO_TMUX, generationsOf, lcDir } from './lifecycleHelpers.js';
import { mkTmp } from './tmpHelpers.js';

const ID = 'demo-quiet-basin';
const GEN = '1790000000000000000';
const store = (): CoordStore =>
  new CoordStore(openCoordDb(path.join(mkTmp('ccrc-leaf-end-chain-'), '.ccrc', 'coord.db')));
/** Every journal line in the harness HOME, RAW and in generation order: the bytes the server's sweep parses. */
const rawLines = (h: CcdHarness): string[] => generationsOf(h.home)
  .flatMap((f) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(lcDir(h.home), f), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean));
/** Parse each raw line as the sweep does, and ingest them in order. */
const ingest = (s: CoordStore, lines: readonly string[]): void => {
  const rows = lines.map((l) => parseJournalLine(l));
  s.ingestJournal({ gen: GEN, rows, cursor: 100 * rows.length, size: 100 * rows.length, at: 9 });
};
/** L1's decision over the store's two reads, as `watch.ts` composes it. */
const decide = (s: CoordStore): ChildReclaimLeafKept[] => {
  const nowMs = Date.now();
  return childReclaimLeafKept({
    rows: s.lifecycleReclaimRowsSince(childReclaimLeafKeptSince(nowMs)), ends: s.lifecycleLeafEndsFor([ID]), nowMs });
};
/** The source: a reclaim `done` that kept the temp root. */
const SOURCE = `${NO_TMUX} _lc_emit reclaim done ${ID} "" verb ws-reclaim meas.childOf 41 meas.tmpRootKept in-use`;
/** A collect `done` carrying `meas.leaf <word>`. CUT: a 2100-byte `resumed` pushes the line past the cap, so the meas
 *  rung fires and the short `detail` survives. Uncut: a short `resumed`. */
const COLLECT = (word: string, cut: boolean): string => `${NO_TMUX} _lc_emit collect done ${ID} "" verb ws-collect `
  + `meas.resumed '${cut ? 'r'.repeat(2100) : 'rec-1'}' meas.leaf ${word} detail short`;

describe('the kept-leaf end, from the encoder to the decision (path-identity spec §3.4)', () => {
  let h: CcdHarness;
  beforeEach(() => { h = makeCcdHarness('ccrc-leaf-end-chain-'); });
  afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

  it.each([
    ['removed', true], ['absent', true], ['removed', false], ['absent', false],
  ] as const)('meas.leaf %s, cut %s: the line carries the word, and the decision reads it', (word, cut) => {
    h.sh(SOURCE);
    h.sh(COLLECT(word, cut));
    const lines = rawLines(h).filter((l) => (JSON.parse(l) as Record<string, unknown>)['id'] === ID);
    expect(lines.map((l) => (JSON.parse(l) as Record<string, unknown>)['act'])).toEqual(['reclaim', 'collect']);
    const done = JSON.parse(lines[1]!) as Record<string, unknown>;

      expect(done['truncated'], 'the line was cut to fit').toBe(true);
      expect(done['meas'], 'the meas rung kept the leaf, and the leaf alone').toEqual({ leaf: word });
      expect(done['detail'], 'the meas rung fired, not the last resort').toBe('short');
      expect(Buffer.byteLength(lines[1]!)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(LC_LINE_MAX);
    } else {
      expect(done['truncated'], 'CONTROL: the line was not cut').toBeUndefined();
      expect(done['meas']).toEqual({ resumed: 'rec-1', leaf: word });
    }
    const s = store();
    ingest(s, lines);
    const got = decide(s);
    if (word === 'removed') {
      expect(got, 'a removal ends the temp-root half, and no clips directory was kept').toEqual([]);
    } else {
      expect(got.map((k) => [k.item.sessionId, k.foundNothing])).toEqual([[ID, true]]);
      expect(got[0]!.item.sentence).toContain(childReclaimLeafFoundNothing(ID));
    }
  }, 60_000);
});
```

**6b. The end row and its reader** (hint :1557). This replaces the interface.

Before:
```ts
/** A row that may END a kept-leaf item (`CoordStore.lifecycleLeafEndsFor`): a `done` `create` or `collect`
 *  of the id, with the mirror's id and ccd's nullable clock. */
export interface ChildReclaimLeafEndRow {
  readonly id: number;
  readonly act: Extract<LifecycleAct, 'create' | 'collect'>;
  readonly at: number | null;
}
```
After:
```ts
/** What one later `collect` `done` line says of the temp-root leaf (path-identity spec §3.4), read off the line as
 *  the mirror holds it. FOUR answers, never folded:
 *  - `word`: ccd's `meas.leaf`, a word of L0's `COLLECT_LEAF_END_WORDS` (`removed`: this collection removed the leaf;
 *    `absent`: no leaf stood at the witness's path);
 *  - `keyless`: an UNCUT line with no `leaf`, which only an older ccd writes, or the store's own `"leaf":null` (its
 *    revived `meas` spells every key, so a line that carried none is stored with a null one);
 *  - `truncated-keyless`: a line cut to fit with no `leaf`, so what it said of the leaf is not known;
 *  - `malformed`: `leaf` present and no word of ccd's, or a `meas` text that is not a JSON object. */
export type ChildReclaimLeafEndRead =
  | { readonly kind: 'word'; readonly word: CollectLeafEndWord }
  | { readonly kind: 'keyless' }
  | { readonly kind: 'truncated-keyless' }
  | { readonly kind: 'malformed' };

/** THE ONE READER of a `collect` `done`'s leaf (path-identity spec §3.4). It reads the stored `measJson` and the cut
 *  flag RAW, because a revived null cannot say whether the line was cut. A null text, or a JSON `null`, is no `meas`
 *  at all. A present `leaf` that is no word of ccd's is never read as absent. Pure and total. */
export function childReclaimLeafEndRead(measJson: string | null, truncated: boolean): ChildReclaimLeafEndRead {
  const keyless: ChildReclaimLeafEndRead = truncated ? { kind: 'truncated-keyless' } : { kind: 'keyless' };
  if (measJson === null) return keyless;
  let meas: unknown;
  try { meas = JSON.parse(measJson); } catch { return { kind: 'malformed' }; }
  if (meas === null) return keyless;
  if (typeof meas !== 'object' || Array.isArray(meas)) return { kind: 'malformed' };
  const leaf: unknown = (meas as Record<string, unknown>)['leaf'];
  if (leaf === undefined || leaf === null) return keyless;
  return isCollectLeafEndWord(leaf) ? { kind: 'word', word: leaf } : { kind: 'malformed' };
}

/** The two acts whose `done` may END a kept-leaf item, spelled ONCE: this file's decision and the store's read both
 *  take them from here. */
export const CHILD_RECLAIM_LEAF_END_ACTS = { create: 'create', collect: 'collect' } as const
  satisfies Readonly<Record<'create' | 'collect', Extract<LifecycleAct, 'create' | 'collect'>>>;

/** A row that may END a kept-leaf item (`CoordStore.lifecycleLeafEndsFor`): a `done` `create` or `collect` of the id,
 *  with the mirror's id and ccd's nullable clock. A `collect` row carries what its line says of the leaf as a
 *  REQUIRED field, so TypeScript asks it of every `collect` row built anywhere (path-identity spec §3.4). */
export type ChildReclaimLeafEndRow =
  | { readonly id: number; readonly act: Extract<LifecycleAct, 'create'>; readonly at: number | null }
  | { readonly id: number; readonly act: Extract<LifecycleAct, 'collect'>; readonly at: number | null;
      readonly leaf: ChildReclaimLeafEndRead };
```

**6e. The sentence's fifth parameter** (hint :1620). This replaces the whole function and its docstring.

Before:
```ts
/** The kept-leaf item's sentence (spec §5.9): what stands, why, and what ends the line. A cut line says it
 *  was cut. It points to the feed row only when the row carries ccd's `detail`: ccd's last-resort line keeps
 *  neither `meas` nor `detail`, and then the sentence names where to look instead. A temp root that a later
 *  `collect` took is never named as kept, nor as a place to look. */
export function childReclaimLeafKeptSentence(
  sessionId: string, clips: ChildReclaimMirrorLeaf, tmp: ChildReclaimMirrorLeaf | 'collected',
  detail: string | null,
): string {
  if (clips.kind === 'truncated') {
    const where = tmp === 'collected'
      ? `~/.cc-clips/${sessionId}` : `~/.cc-clips/${sessionId} and ~/.cc-tmp/${sessionId}`;
    return 'The reclaim of this child completed, but the journal line ccd wrote for it was cut to fit, so whether '
      + 'its clips directory or its temp root was kept is not known; '
      + (detail !== null && childReclaimDetailText(detail) !== ''
        ? 'the feed row for it carries what ccd said.'
        : `ccd's line kept no detail either, so the feed cannot name it; look for ${where} on the fleet box.`)
      + (tmp === 'collected' ? ' Its temp root has since been collected.' : '') + ` ${LEAF_HORIZON}`;
  }
  const tmpWord = tmp !== 'collected' && tmp.kind === 'kept' ? tmp.word : null;
  const parts = [
    ...(clips.kind === 'kept' ? [leafClipsPart(sessionId, clips.word)] : []),
    ...(tmpWord === null ? [] : [`its temp root ~/.cc-tmp/${sessionId} (${tmpWord}: ${LEAF_PHRASE[tmpWord]})`]),
  ];
  return `The reclaim of this child completed, but ccd kept ${parts.join(' and ')}. What was kept stays on disk.`
    + (clips.kind === 'kept' ? ` ${LEAF_CLIPS_STAYS}` : '')
    + (tmpWord === null ? '' : ` ${LEAF_TMP_COLLECTOR}`) + ` ${LEAF_HORIZON}`;
}
```
After:
```ts
/** The kept-leaf item's sentence (spec §5.9): what stands, why, and what ends the line. A cut line says it
 *  was cut. It points to the feed row only when the row carries ccd's `detail`: ccd's last-resort line keeps
 *  neither `meas` nor `detail`, and then the sentence names where to look instead. A temp root that a later
 *  `collect` took is never named as kept, nor as a place to look. When a later `collect` found nothing at the
 *  temp root (`tmpFoundNothing`), its clause comes before the horizon, in either arm (path-identity spec §3.4). */
export function childReclaimLeafKeptSentence(
  sessionId: string, clips: ChildReclaimMirrorLeaf, tmp: ChildReclaimMirrorLeaf | 'collected',
  detail: string | null, tmpFoundNothing: boolean,
): string {
  const foundNothing = tmpFoundNothing ? ` ${childReclaimLeafFoundNothing(sessionId)}` : '';
  if (clips.kind === 'truncated') {
    const where = tmp === 'collected'
      ? `~/.cc-clips/${sessionId}` : `~/.cc-clips/${sessionId} and ~/.cc-tmp/${sessionId}`;
    return 'The reclaim of this child completed, but the journal line ccd wrote for it was cut to fit, so whether '
      + 'its clips directory or its temp root was kept is not known; '
      + (detail !== null && childReclaimDetailText(detail) !== ''
        ? 'the feed row for it carries what ccd said.'
        : `ccd's line kept no detail either, so the feed cannot name it; look for ${where} on the fleet box.`)
      + (tmp === 'collected' ? ' Its temp root has since been collected.' : '') + foundNothing + ` ${LEAF_HORIZON}`;
  }
  const tmpWord = tmp !== 'collected' && tmp.kind === 'kept' ? tmp.word : null;
  const parts = [
    ...(clips.kind === 'kept' ? [leafClipsPart(sessionId, clips.word)] : []),
    ...(tmpWord === null ? [] : [`its temp root ~/.cc-tmp/${sessionId} (${tmpWord}: ${LEAF_PHRASE[tmpWord]})`]),
  ];
  return `The reclaim of this child completed, but ccd kept ${parts.join(' and ')}. What was kept stays on disk.`
    + (clips.kind === 'kept' ? ` ${LEAF_CLIPS_STAYS}` : '')
    + (tmpWord === null ? '' : ` ${LEAF_TMP_COLLECTOR}`) + foundNothing + ` ${LEAF_HORIZON}`;
}
```

**6g. The end rule in `childReclaimLeafKept`'s docstring** (hint :1668). This is in place. The id-rule bullets below it are Task 15's and stay byte-identical.

Before:
```ts

```
After:
```ts
 *  - A later `collect` `done` ends the temp-root half only, and only when its line says the collection removed the
 *    leaf (`meas.leaf` `removed`), or is an uncut line with no `leaf`, which an older ccd writes (path-identity
 *    spec §3.4). The collector never takes a clips directory. Any such row ends the half, whatever its place.
 *  - Otherwise a later line that says no leaf stood there (`absent`) keeps the half to the horizon with
 *    `childReclaimLeafFoundNothing`'s clause, and marks the item `foundNothing`. A line cut to fit with no `leaf`,
 *    and a `leaf` that is no word of ccd's, neither end the half nor add a clause.
```

```ts
    // the others; otherwise any `absent` adds the clause. Never "the latest wins": a later unread row cannot re-open
```

**7b. The statement and the read** (hint :6251):

Before:
```ts
  static lifecycleLeafEndsSql(sessions: number): string {
    return 'SELECT id, sessionId, act, at FROM lifecycle_events INDEXED BY lifecycle_by_session ' +
      `WHERE sessionId IN (${placeholders(sessions)}) AND act IN (?, ?) AND outcome = ? ORDER BY sessionId, id`;
  }

  /** What may END a kept-leaf item (spec §5.9): each asked id's `done` `create` and `collect` rows, oldest
   *  first, with the mirror's id and ccd's nullable `at`. ONE statement whatever the id count. EVERY asked
   *  id gets an entry, `[]` included (`childReclaimEvents`' rule). Whether a row FOLLOWS an item's source,
   *  and whether a create is placed, are L1's. */
  lifecycleLeafEndsFor(sessionIds: readonly string[]): Map<string, ChildReclaimLeafEndRow[]> {
    const ids = [...new Set(sessionIds)];
    const out = new Map<string, ChildReclaimLeafEndRow[]>(ids.map((id) => [id, []]));
    if (ids.length === 0) return out;
    const create: ChildReclaimLeafEndRow['act'] = 'create';
    const collect: ChildReclaimLeafEndRow['act'] = 'collect';
    const done: LifecycleOutcome = 'done';
    const rows = this.db.prepare(CoordStore.lifecycleLeafEndsSql(ids.length))
      .all(...ids, create, collect, done) as { id: number; sessionId: string; act: string; at: number | null }[];
    for (const r of rows) {
      const act = r.act === create ? create : r.act === collect ? collect : null;
      if (act !== null) out.get(r.sessionId)?.push({ id: r.id, act, at: r.at });
    }
    return out;
  }
```
After:
```ts
  static lifecycleLeafEndsSql(sessions: number): string {
    return 'SELECT id, sessionId, act, at, truncated, measJson FROM lifecycle_events INDEXED BY lifecycle_by_session ' +
      `WHERE sessionId IN (${placeholders(sessions)}) AND act IN (?, ?) AND outcome = ? ORDER BY sessionId, id`;
  }

  /** What may END a kept-leaf item (spec §5.9): each asked id's `done` `create` and `collect` rows, oldest
   *  first, with the mirror's id and ccd's nullable `at`. ONE statement whatever the id count. EVERY asked
   *  id gets an entry, `[]` included (`childReclaimEvents`' rule). Whether a row FOLLOWS an item's source,
   *  and whether a create is placed, are L1's.
   *
   *  A `collect` row's line goes to L1 RAW (path-identity spec §3.4): the stored `measJson` and the cut flag are
   *  handed to `childReclaimLeafEndRead`, never a value revived from them, because the reader needs the cut flag
   *  beside the text. The store decides nothing: what the line says of the leaf, and whether that ends the item,
   *  are L1's. The two acts are L1's one spelling, `CHILD_RECLAIM_LEAF_END_ACTS`. */
  lifecycleLeafEndsFor(sessionIds: readonly string[]): Map<string, ChildReclaimLeafEndRow[]> {
    const ids = [...new Set(sessionIds)];
    const out = new Map<string, ChildReclaimLeafEndRow[]>(ids.map((id) => [id, []]));
    if (ids.length === 0) return out;
    const { create, collect } = CHILD_RECLAIM_LEAF_END_ACTS;
    const done: LifecycleOutcome = 'done';
    const rows = this.db.prepare(CoordStore.lifecycleLeafEndsSql(ids.length))
      .all(...ids, create, collect, done) as
        { id: number; sessionId: string; act: string; at: number | null; truncated: number; measJson: string | null }[];
    for (const r of rows) {
      if (r.act === create) out.get(r.sessionId)?.push({ id: r.id, act: create, at: r.at });
      else if (r.act === collect) {
        out.get(r.sessionId)?.push({ id: r.id, act: collect, at: r.at, leaf: childReclaimLeafEndRead(r.measJson, r.truncated !== 0) });
      }
    }
    return out;
  }
```

```bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(server): a kept-leaf line ends only on a removal, and an absence keeps it with a clause

The store now passes each collect done row's measJson and cut flag raw
to one L1 reader, childReclaimLeafEndRead. It answers four kinds: a
word of ccd's, keyless, truncated-keyless and malformed (path-identity
spec §3.4). The end is monotone. Any removed row ends the temp-root
half wherever it stands, and so does an older ccd's uncut row with no
leaf (TR2 A). Otherwise an absent row keeps the line to the 7-day
horizon, with a clause that names ~/.cc-tmp/<id> and the mount to
check. A cut row with no leaf, and a malformed leaf, fail closed: they
end nothing and add nothing.

An item that ends on absent is marked foundNothing on the L1 type. It
never joins the kept-many collapse, whose sentence promises that the
collector removes each temp root. The two end acts are spelled once,
in CHILD_RECLAIM_LEAF_END_ACTS (leaf-end-acts-spelled-twice, closed).
An appended single-definition block registers the leaf words.

The store's own encoding forces two folds, and both are named rather
than hidden. A stored "leaf":null reads keyless and ends the half
(present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy). A meas that is not a JSON object
is stored as none and also reads keyless
(non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless). Stated residuals:
found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-collector-item,
found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-reclaim-item and
absent-clause-names-a-drop-the-compare-kept.
EOF
```

  - the carry `leaf-end-acts-spelled-twice`, now closed;
  - the corrections below.

**Drafter's corrections (checked against the export):**
1. **T13.2 is split into T13.2a and T13.2b.** The frame's one row expected red on decision case 5 and on the reader's cut rows together, which no single mutation can produce. The decision rows take reads directly and never pass through the reader. So T13.2a mutates the reader (its cut rows and the store's cut no-meas row red), and T13.2b mutates `ends` (case 5 reds).
2. **T13.10 is written as one concrete narrowing.** The store revives `meas.leaf` and maps a revived null to `keyless` itself.
   - Under that mutation, exactly the frame's prediction holds: the `(null,true)` store row reds, and the `7` and `bogus` rows pass.
   - A plain "revive, then re-encode for the reader" is equivalent under P3 on every row the store can hold, so it reds nothing. That is why it is not used.
3. **Cases and rows added.**
   - Reader rows: `('{"resumed":"x"}', false)`, `('{"leaf":7}', false)` and `('null', false)`, plus the vocabulary loop.
   - Two store rows: an older finish line `{resumed}`, and a case that reads the stored `"leaf":null` spelling.
   - A source case for the carry `leaf-end-acts-spelled-twice`.
   - Mutation rows T13.13 (the store re-spells the acts) and T13.14 (the reader folds a present non-word into keyless).
   - The two yield cases assert a CONTROL (`foundNothing` is `[true]`), so neither can pass vacuously.
4. **`child-reclaim-leaf-kept.test.ts` holds 6 `act: 'collect'` literals on 5 lines.** The `for … of` pair has no contextual type, so it needs `leaf: { kind: 'keyless' as const }`. Its untyped `leaf()` helper reaches `childReclaimLeafKeptFeedBody(k: ChildReclaimLeafKept)`, so `foundNothing` is forced there too.
5. **The chain reads raw lines through `generationsOf` and `lcDir`.** The frame's consumed `readJournal` parses each line, and the chain must hand the parser ccd's bytes. ccd's encoder cannot write the non-object `meas` row, so that row is a hand-built line ingested straight into a store.
6. **Gates added:**
   - `collect-leaving-l1` and `child-reclaim-verdict-readers`, both consumers of `childReclaimAttentionWithLeaves`;
   - the five citation passes;
   - the R89 diff check;
   - a check that `child-reclaim-leaf-kept-store.test.ts` is unedited.
7. **Boundary limits.**
   - The docstring of `childReclaimAttentionWithLeaves` is left unedited, because the HARD BOUNDARY names only its one call line. Its bullet "the leaf items left list as `childReclaimLeafKeptList` lists them" stays true.
   - The `childReclaimLeafKept` docstring's id-rule bullet is Task 15's and is untouched.
8. **The red run's shape depends on the module runner.** A missing named export either fails the file at load or fails each case with a `TypeError`. Step 5 accepts either and asks for the measured one.
9. **The yield residual covers both arms.** P12 names only the collector arm, but `childReclaimAttentionWithLeaves` drops a leaf item whose id ANY earlier item took, and a reclaim item (terminal, failing, stuck, kept, or a kept-many member) takes its ids first. The reclaim arm carries only the collector's quarantine-kept sentence and the leaf's clips clause, never the found-nothing clause, so the clause is lost there too. That is named as a second stated residual, `found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-reclaim-item`, and pinned beside the collector case with a stuck item. Spec §3.4's "with one added clause" therefore holds only for a leaf item that lists on its own.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write `server/test/ccd-child-reclaim-sibling-entry.test.ts` (item 34)**

```ts
// C13's reach to ANOTHER admin entry (path-identity spec §3.9, item 34; child reclamation spec §5.5, rung 8's rule:
// a read that failed measured nothing). `_ws_reclaim_admin_entries`, the ONE matcher of git's admin entries to a path,
// tests each entry's `gitdir` for a blank first line BEFORE it compares that entry with the path. So one blank entry
// anywhere in a repository's `worktrees/` makes every walk of that repository answer "never asked": the matcher
// cannot tell whether the blank entry was the path's record. Two walks reach it:
//   - the gone walk (`_ws_reclaim_log_of`'s absent arm), which the vanished arm's PIN runs. The verb stops
//     `pin-failed` before the tombstone, the breadcrumb or any delete, while the ladder, which never walks a record
//     git listed, still mints its token: the stated residual `corrupt-admin-entry-holds-the-repository`;
//   - the ladder's "no record" ask (`_ws_reclaim_no_record`), when git's list printed no record of the tree.
// A STANDING child whose own record git lists runs neither walk. `ccd-child-reclaim-silent-omission.test.ts` pins a
// blank OWN entry; this file pins a blank SIBLING beside an intact own entry.
// FIXTURE HOMEs ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every ccd call runs through the harness, never against $HOME. The unit and the
// pane are stubbed (`CHILD_STUBS`, inside `evalOf` and `childReclaimVerb`), and so is the /proc walk (`NOBODY`).
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CHILD_BRANCH, CHILD_ID, childReclaimVerb, evalOf, makeChild } from './childReclaimFixture.js';
import { verbHelpers } from './childReclaimVerbHelpers.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-child-reclaim-sibling-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });
const { unsupervised } = verbHelpers(() => h);

/** git's admin entry for a checkout: `<main>/.git/worktrees/<basename of its tree>`. */
const adminOf = (main: string, slug: string): string => path.join(main, '.git', 'worktrees', slug);
/** An admin `gitdir` rewritten with `body`. */
const emptyGitdir = (main: string, slug: string, body: string): void => {
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(adminOf(main, slug), 'gitdir'), body);
};
/** A first line that names NO PATH: empty, or blank once git right-trims it. */
const EMPTY_BODIES: [string, string][] = [
  ['empty (`: >`)', ''], ['a lone newline', '\n'], ['spaces', '   '], ['a space and a newline', ' \n'], ['a tab', '\t'],
  ['a blank first line over a second', '\nnot-a-path\n'], ['a carriage return and a newline', '\r\n'],
];
const NAMES_NO_PATH = 'gitdir names no path on its first line';
/** git's list omits the record although every admin entry reads: stubbed at its one reader. */
const LIST_OMITS = '_ws_reclaim_record() { RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH=; RECLAIM_REC_HEAD=; RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=0; RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=0; return 1; };';
/** No process uses any path: the tail's /proc walk, stubbed, so no case here shells it. */
const NOBODY = '_ws_path_users() { _WS_PATH_USERS_PIDS=""; _WS_PATH_USERS_WHY=""; return 0; };';
const SIBLING_BRANCH = 'ws/other';

/** A sibling checkout of the child's OWN repository, at `<HOME>/worktrees/demo/other` on `ws/other`. git names its
 *  admin entry `other`. Answers its path. */
const addSibling = (main: string): string => {
  const other = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'other');
  h.git(main, 'worktree', 'add', '-q', '-b', SIBLING_BRANCH, other);
  return other;
};
/** `_ws_reclaim_log_of`'s walk of a gone tree, asked as the vanished arm's pin asks it (`recorded` 1). */
const walk = (main: string, wt: string): { rc: string; why: string; logs: string[] } => {
  const [rc = '', why = '', logs = ''] = h.sh(`_WS_LOGS=(); _WS_KEEP_WHY=''; _ws_reclaim_log_of '${main}' tree '${wt}' 1;`
    + ' printf \'%s\\x1f%s\\x1f\' "$?" "$_WS_KEEP_WHY"; printf \'%s\\n\' ${_WS_LOGS[@]+"${_WS_LOGS[@]}"}').split('\x1f');
  return { rc, why, logs: logs.split('\n').filter(Boolean) };
};
/** `_ws_reclaim_no_record`'s answer, its reason uncut. */
const noRecord = (main: string, wt: string): { rc: string; why: string } => {
  const [rc = '', why = ''] = h.sh(`_ws_reclaim_no_record "$(_ws_common_dir '${main}')" '${wt}';`
    + ' printf \'%s\\x1f%s\' "$?" "$_WS_NOREC_WHY"').split('\x1f');
  return { rc, why };
};

describe('a blank SIBLING admin entry holds every gone walk of its repository (item 34)', () => {
  it('the CONTROL: an intact sibling, the child’s tree gone: the walk finds the child’s own entry alone, the ladder mints, and the verb reclaims without touching the sibling', () => {
    const { main, wt } = makeChild(h);
    const other = addSibling(main);
    const siblingGitdir = fs.readFileSync(path.join(adminOf(main, 'other'), 'gitdir'), 'utf8');
    const siblingTip = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', `refs/heads/${SIBLING_BRANCH}`);
    fs.rmSync(wt, { recursive: true, force: true });
    const w = walk(main, wt);
    expect(w.rc, w.why).toBe('0');
    expect(w.logs).toEqual([path.join(adminOf(main, 'quiet-basin'), 'logs', 'HEAD'), `gitdir:${adminOf(main, 'quiet-basin')}`]);
    const e = evalOf(h);
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('reclaimable');
    const r = childReclaimVerb(h, e.token, { pre: NOBODY });
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect((JSON.parse(r.stdout) as Record<string, unknown>)['reclaimed']).toBe(CHILD_ID);
    expect(fs.existsSync(other), 'the sibling’s tree stands').toBe(true);
    expect(h.git(main, 'rev-parse', `refs/heads/${SIBLING_BRANCH}`), 'the sibling’s branch stands').toBe(siblingTip);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(adminOf(main, 'other'), 'gitdir'), 'utf8'), 'the sibling’s admin entry stands')
      .toBe(siblingGitdir);
  }, 120_000);

  it('the CONTROL: an intact sibling, and git’s list omits the standing child’s record: unmeasured, naming the child’s own entry', () => {
    const { main, wt } = makeChild(h);
    addSibling(main);
    const e = evalOf(h, { pre: LIST_OMITS });
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(e.token).toBe('');
    expect(e.detail).toMatch(/^git's worktree list omitted a record that exists: /);
    const n = noRecord(main, wt);
    expect(n.rc).toBe('1');
    expect(n.why).toBe(`git's worktree list omitted a record that exists: it printed no record of ${wt},`
      + ` but ${adminOf(main, 'quiet-basin')} names ${wt}/.git`);
  }, 60_000);

  it.each(EMPTY_BODIES)('the SIBLING’s gitdir reads %s, the child’s own entry intact, its tree gone: the walk is never asked, the ladder still mints, and the pin refuses with nothing destroyed', (_label, body) => {
    const { main, wt, tip } = makeChild(h);
    addSibling(main);
    fs.rmSync(wt, { recursive: true, force: true });
    emptyGitdir(main, 'other', body);
    const lead = `${adminOf(main, 'other')}/${NAMES_NO_PATH}`;
    // The gone walk, as the pin asks it: the blank sibling answers before the child's own entry is compared.
    const w = walk(main, wt);
    expect(w.rc, w.why).toBe('1');
    expect(w.why.startsWith(lead), w.why).toBe(true);
    // The ladder never walks a record git listed, so it mints (`corrupt-admin-entry-holds-the-repository`) ...
    const e = evalOf(h);
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('reclaimable');
    // ... and the pin refuses that token, before the tombstone, the breadcrumb or any delete.
    const r = childReclaimVerb(h, e.token, { pre: NOBODY });
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(1);
    const o = JSON.parse(r.stdout) as { failed: string; detail: string };
    expect(o.failed).toBe('pin-failed');
    expect(o.detail.startsWith(lead), o.detail).toBe(true);
    expect(h.git(main, 'rev-parse', `refs/heads/${CHILD_BRANCH}`), 'the branch stands').toBe(tip);
    expect(h.reg(CHILD_ID, 'uuid'), 'the registry row stands').not.toBeNull();
    expect(h.reg(CHILD_ID, 'reaping'), 'no breadcrumb').toBeNull();
    expect(unsupervised(), 'the unit was not touched').toEqual([]);
    expect(fs.existsSync(adminOf(main, 'quiet-basin')), 'git’s record of the child stands').toBe(true);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(adminOf(main, 'other'), 'gitdir'), 'utf8'), 'the sibling’s entry, as it was').toBe(body);
  }, 120_000);

  it.each(EMPTY_BODIES)('the SIBLING’s gitdir reads %s and git’s list omits the standing child’s record: unmeasured, no token, naming the sibling — never no-worktree-record', (_label, body) => {
    const { main, wt } = makeChild(h);
    addSibling(main);
    emptyGitdir(main, 'other', body);
    const lead = `${adminOf(main, 'other')}/${NAMES_NO_PATH}`;
    const e = evalOf(h, { pre: LIST_OMITS });
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(e.token).toBe('');
    expect(e.detail.startsWith(lead), e.detail).toBe(true);
    const n = noRecord(main, wt);
    expect(n.rc).toBe('2');
    expect(n.why.startsWith(lead), n.why).toBe(true);
    expect(n.why).toContain(`so its silence about ${wt} measured nothing`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('the STANDING child, its own record listed, beside the same blank sibling: reclaimable — the reach is the gone walk and the no-record ask only', () => {
    const { main } = makeChild(h);
    addSibling(main);
    emptyGitdir(main, 'other', '\n');
    const e = evalOf(h);
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('reclaimable');
    expect(e.token).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  }, 60_000);
});
```

Notes on these assertions:

```ts
/** ITEM 35 (path-identity spec §3.9): the collector's quarantine maker, `_ws_collect_qdir`, clears the setgid bit a
 *  setgid `~/.cc-tmp` hands the directory it makes, with `chmod -- g-s "$q"`. No case ran that line under BSD argument
 *  order: `ccd-collect-quarantine.test.ts` logs it through a shell function that calls the HOST chmod, which on Linux
 *  is GNU and permutes, so a `--` after the mode would pass there. The literal census below reads one line at a time,

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';

const qdir = (env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): { status: number; rc: string; q: string; why: string; out: string } => {
  const r = shStatus('_ws_collect_qdir; printf "%s\\x1f%s\\x1f%s" "$?" "$_WS_Q" "$_WS_Q_WHY"', env);
  const [rc = '', q = '', why = ''] = r.out.split('\x1f');
  return { status: r.status, rc, q, why, out: r.out };
};
const quarantine = (): string => path.join(fs.realpathSync(tmpRoot()), '.ccd-quarantine');

    const m = qdir(chmodEnv());
    expect(m.status, m.out).toBe(0);
    expect(m.rc, m.why).toBe('0');
    expect(m.q).toBe(quarantine());
    expect(m.why).toBe('');
    expect(fs.statSync(quarantine()).mode & 0o7777).toBe(0o700);
  });
});

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('the collector’s quarantine maker under a setgid ~/.cc-tmp, where Linux hands the new directory the bit (item 35)', () => {

    fs.mkdirSync(tmpRoot(), { mode: 0o755 });
    fs.chmodSync(tmpRoot(), 0o2755);
    expect(fs.statSync(tmpRoot()).mode & 0o7777, 'the CONTROL: ~/.cc-tmp is setgid').toBe(0o2755);
    const m = qdir(chmodEnv());
    expect(m.rc, m.why).toBe('0');
    expect(m.q).toBe(quarantine());
    expect(fs.statSync(quarantine()).mode & 0o7777, 'the setgid bit was cleared').toBe(0o700);
  });
});
```

```ts
/** Comment text as prose: each line's comment leader dropped, then whitespace flattened, so a phrase is matched across a

const prose = (s: string): string => s.replace(/^[ \t]*(?:\/\*\*|\/\/|\*\/|\*)[ \t]?/gm, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ');

/** The docstring directly above `head` in `file`: from the nearest `/**` before it to it; '' when either is missing. */
const docAbove = (file: string, head: string): string => {
  const s = read(file);
  const end = s.indexOf(`\n${head}`);
  const start = end < 0 ? -1 : s.lastIndexOf('/**', end);
  return start < 0 ? '' : s.slice(start, end);
};

  for (let i = title - 2; i >= 0 && /^\s*\/\//.test(lines[i]); i -= 1) out.unshift(lines[i]);
  return out.join('\n');
};
```

**3a. `server/src/coord/collectTempRoot.ts`, `CollectLearnAnswer`** (hint `:202-206`).

Before:
```ts
/** The learning audit's answer: not asked, because the box cannot answer it, or answered, with its generations and
 *  its arrival. */
export type CollectLearnAnswer =
  | { readonly kind: 'not-asked'; readonly why: 'caps' }
  | { readonly kind: 'answered'; readonly audit: CollectAnswer<CollectAudit> };
```
After:
```ts
/** The learning audit's answer: not asked, because the box cannot answer it; `id-refused`, because the id is not one
 *  the collector may name (`isTmpRootId`, asked before any argv: the twin of the act's step-1 check), a DISTINCT arm
 *  and never `not-asked`, whose caller clears every pair; or answered, with its generations and its arrival. */
export type CollectLearnAnswer =
  | { readonly kind: 'not-asked'; readonly why: 'caps' }
  | { readonly kind: 'id-refused' }
  | { readonly kind: 'answered'; readonly audit: CollectAnswer<CollectAudit> };
```

**3b. `server/src/coord/collectTempRoot.ts`, `learnCollect`** (hint `:458-466`).

Before:
```ts
/** The lane's LEARNING audit (spec §5.10). It is read-only on the box: the audit journals a terminal refusal and
 *  nothing else. It sits behind the capability, as the act does. The caller runs it on the id's queue key. */
export async function learnCollect(
  deps: Pick<CollectTempRootDeps, 'runCcd' | 'fleetState' | 'lane'>, id: string,
): Promise<CollectLearnAnswer> {
  const audit = await collectAudit(deps, id);
```
After:
```ts
/** The lane's LEARNING audit (spec §5.10). It is read-only on the box: the audit journals a terminal refusal and
 *  nothing else. It asks the temp-root id predicate FIRST, the twin of the act's step-1 check: the population gated the
 *  id, but path-identity W2 widened that population to an id a compare-and-drop aside is for, so the learning audit no
 *  longer relies on that gate alone. Then it sits behind the capability, as the act does. The caller runs it on the
 *  id's queue key. */
export async function learnCollect(
  deps: Pick<CollectTempRootDeps, 'runCcd' | 'fleetState' | 'lane'>, id: string,
): Promise<CollectLearnAnswer> {
  if (!isTmpRootId(id)) return { kind: 'id-refused' };
  const audit = await collectAudit(deps, id);
```

**3d. `shared/api.ts`, `isRegistryId`'s first bullet**, in place and line-neutral (3 lines for 3; hint `:9805-9807`).

Before:
```ts
 *  - The leading `-` is a SAFETY rule, not defence in depth (spec 2026-10-12 §2.1). ccd's verbs read their decision flags from any
 *    position, `--session`'s value included, and every such flag begins `--`. An id of `--actor` is read as a flag,
 *    and the verb binds another token as its id. The shape refuses `=`, so no `--flag=value` can be an id either.
```
After:
```ts
 *  - The leading `-` is a SAFETY rule (spec 2026-10-12 §2.1). A ccd older than path-identity W1b read its decision flags from any
 *    position, `--session`'s value included, and every such flag begins `--`; since W1b each identity key takes its value whole,
 *    so this rule is the server's half of the same refusal and closes the redirect on an older ccd too. The shape refuses `=`.
```
