```ts
// Path identity W2: what the spec and the programme's rulings file record about the wave as built (path-identity
// spec §3.10 and §7). What the records name is read from the code here, never restated:
// - the leaf words, from `shared/api.ts`'s table and the ccd lines that write them;
// - the mount helper `_ws_leaf_remove` calls, and its Darwin guard, from `ccd/ccd`;
// - the probe word's class, from `server/src/collectLane.ts`;
// - the found-nothing clause, from `childReclaimLeafFoundNothing`.
// So a later change to any of them reds this suite until the record is corrected with it. The four carries that close
// only once the code says so are decided from the code too. W1b's records belong to `path-identity-w1b-prose.test.ts`.
// This file reads §3.10 alone and counts only its own cells, so it never disturbs that suite's §2.9 slice or its count
// of eight `Built (W1b)` cells.
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { childReclaimLeafFoundNothing } from '../src/childReclaimSweep.js';

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const read = (f: string): string => readFileSync(path.join(root, f), 'utf8');
/** Flattened: the records wrap their sentences, so a phrase is matched across line breaks. */
const flat = (s: string): string => s.replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
const SPEC = 'docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-path-identity-design.md';
const CONTRACT = 'docs/superpowers/programs/child-reclamation-contract.md';
const CCD = 'ccd/ccd';
const DEVIATION_TOKEN = /\bD-\d/;
const FOUR_DIGIT_RANGE = /[0-9]{4} ?(–|\.\.|-) ?[0-9]{4}/;
/** A slot the plan's draft left for a measured value, `<n:…>`. None may survive into a record. */
const UNFILLED = /<n:[^>]*>/;
const HEADING = '\n### 3.10 As built (W2)\n';

/** §3.10 alone, from its heading to the next `## ` heading; '' when the heading is missing. */
function asBuilt(): string {
  const s = read(SPEC);
  const at = s.indexOf(HEADING);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const end = s.indexOf('\n## ', at + 1);
  return s.slice(at, end < 0 ? s.length : end);
}

/** TEXT from the line that starts with LEAD to the next line that starts with `**`, flattened; '' when LEAD is
 *  missing. The records' lists are bulleted, so only a bold lead starts a line with `**`. */
function block(text: string, lead: string): string {
  const at = text.indexOf(`\n${lead}`);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const next = text.indexOf('\n**', at + 1);
  return flat(text.slice(at, next < 0 ? text.length : next));
}

/** A shell function's text, from `NAME() {` to the first line that is `}` alone; '' when there is none. */
function shFunction(src: string, name: string): string {
  const at = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const end = src.indexOf('\n}\n', at + 1);
  return end < 0 ? '' : src.slice(at + 1, end + 2);
}

/** A function's code. Its first line (the name and its header comment) is dropped, and so is every blank line and
 *  every whole-line `#` comment. Each remaining line's trailing ` #` comment is cut. */
function codeLines(fn: string): string[] {
  return fn.split('\n').slice(1).map((l) => l.split(' #')[0])
    .filter((l) => l.trim() !== '' && !l.trimStart().startsWith('#'));
}

/** The keys of `COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE`, in its order, read from `shared/api.ts` as text; [] when it is gone. */
function leafWords(): string[] {
  const m = /const COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE\b[^=]*=\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(read('shared/api.ts'));
  return m ? [...m[1].matchAll(/([a-z][a-z-]*)\s*:\s*true\b/g)].map((x) => x[1]) : [];
}

/** `COLLECT_PROBE_CLASS_TABLE`'s body, read from `server/src/collectLane.ts` as text; '' when it is gone. */
function probeClassTable(): string {
  const s = read('server/src/collectLane.ts');
  const at = s.indexOf('const COLLECT_PROBE_CLASS_TABLE = {');
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const end = s.indexOf('} as const', at);
  return end < 0 ? '' : s.slice(at, end);
}

const q = (w: string): string => `\`${w}\``;
const andList = (xs: readonly string[]): string =>
  xs.length < 2 ? xs.join('') : `${xs.slice(0, -1).join(', ')} and ${xs[xs.length - 1]}`;
const COUNT_WORD: Readonly<Record<number, string>> = { 1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three', 4: 'four' };

/** Which ccd function writes each leaf word on its collect `done` line. */
const LEAF_WRITERS = [['removed', '_ws_collect_finish'], ['absent', '_ws_collect_witness_only']] as const;

/** The server names §3.10 cites, each with the file that defines it. */
const SERVER_NAMES = [
  ['childReclaimLeafEndRead', 'server/src/childReclaimSweep.ts'],
  ['lifecycleLeafEndsFor', 'server/src/coord/store.ts'],
  ['COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE', 'shared/api.ts'],
  ['COLLECT_ASIDE_NAME_RE', 'server/src/collectLane.ts'],
  ['parseCollectAsideName', 'server/src/collectLane.ts'],
  ['isTmpRootId', 'shared/api.ts'],
  ['learnCollect', 'server/src/coord/collectTempRoot.ts'],
] as const;

/** The substantive departures this wave made, by slug. */
const DEPARTURES = ['drop-helper-reproves-the-absence', 'kept-witness-reason-in-the-row-not-on-stderr',
  'leaf-mount-ask-before-the-owner-bits', 'aside-joins-the-population', 'aside-probe-word',
  'aside-restore-by-link-not-rename', 'tail-aside-warns-without-keeping', 'present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy'];

/** The residuals that stand whatever the code says next. */
const BASE_RESIDUALS = ['tail-drop-not-noreplace-without-mv-no-copy', 'stale-aside-beside-a-new-leaf-is-a-mismatch',
  'git-mount-crossing-unmeasured', 'audit-normalise-has-no-mount-ask', 'mount-found-after-the-kill-repeats',
  'human-gated-removals-ask-no-mounts', 'no-whole-child-mount-ask-before-step-3', 'vanished-checkout-arms-ask-no-mounts',
  'absent-clause-names-a-drop-the-compare-kept', 'found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-collector-item',
  'found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-reclaim-item',
  'non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless', 'ccrc-timeout-knob-strip-is-quadratic', 'rec-eq-f-recycled-admin',
  'device-test-cannot-see-a-same-device-bind-mount', 'permanent-device-change-holds-every-absence',
  'cc-tmp-deleted-whole-holds-its-witnesses', 'source-parent-without-owner-write-loops',
  'tmproot-probe-misses-the-whole-volume-spelling', 'registry-id-l0-comments-say-ccd-scans-the-session-value'];

/** The carries this wave closes whatever the code says next. */
const CLOSED_CARRIES = ['tail-drop-believes-an-absent-leaf', 'tail-drop-ignores-a-recordless-slot',
  'collector-learning-audit-relies-on-the-population-gate', 'session-shape-prose-predates-the-id-gate',
  'leaf-end-acts-spelled-twice', 'review-335-f9-needle-outgrows-the-cap-under-this-tmpdir'];

/** What each task found while building, by slug. The rulings file's "Found while building" list names every one. */
const FOUND_WHILE_BUILDING = ['read-small-partial-read-cleared', 'nul-why-leads-with-the-admin-path',
  'step-4-unresolvable-workdir-fails-before-keep-of', 'worktree-remove-failed-sentence-covers-a-mount',
  'aside-half-not-in-the-id-argv-census', 'prelock-resets-a-pre-peek-aside-answer'];

/** The four carries that close only once the code says so: the two W1b carries, `_ws_collect_witness_cad`'s header
 *  (R41's slug) and the two test comments that said the learning audit asks no id predicate (R42's slug). Each is open
 *  while the code still shows it, and closed once it does not. W1b's `dotOnly` is copied here, never imported. */
function conditionalCarries(): { open: string[]; closed: string[] } {
  const open: string[] = [];
  const closed: string[] = [];
  const dotOnly = /`_ws_tmproot_id_ok`[\s\S]{0,80}?no leading[\s*]*`\.`(?![\s*]*(?:or|and)[\s*]+(?:a[\s*]+)?(?:leading[\s*]+)?`-`)/;
  (dotOnly.test(read('shared/api.ts')) || dotOnly.test(read('server/src/childReclaimSweep.ts')) ? open : closed)
    .push('server-docstrings-call-ccds-predicate-dot-only');
  const scans = /ccd's (?:destructive )?verbs read their decision flags from any[\s*/]+position/;
  (scans.test(read('shared/api.ts')) || scans.test(read('server/test/collect-l0.test.ts')) ? open : closed)
    .push('comments-say-ccd-scans-the-session-value');
  (/tail's plain unlink/.test(read(CCD)) ? open : closed).push('cad-header-calls-the-tail-drop-a-plain-unlink');
  const noLearnGate = /\(`learnCollect`, which[\s/]+asks no predicate of its own\)|with the record half below, the learning audit's only id check/;
  (noLearnGate.test(read('server/test/collect-id-pins.test.ts')) || noLearnGate.test(read('server/test/id-argv-census.test.ts')) ? open : closed)
    .push('learning-audit-gate-prose-in-two-test-comments');
  return { open, closed };
}
const residualsAtTheTip = (): string[] => [...BASE_RESIDUALS, ...conditionalCarries().open];
const closedAtTheTip = (): string[] => [...CLOSED_CARRIES, ...conditionalCarries().closed];

describe('the path-identity spec records W2 as built (path-identity spec §3.10, §7)', () => {
  const spec = read(SPEC);
  const raw = asBuilt();
  const s = flat(raw);
  const ccd = read(CCD);

  it('§3.10 stands after §3.9 and its closing note, and before §4', () => {
    const p39 = spec.indexOf('\n### 3.9 Proof\n');
    const note = p39 < 0 ? -1 : spec.indexOf('\n> [!NOTE]\n', p39);
    const p310 = spec.indexOf(HEADING);
    const p4 = spec.indexOf('\n## 4. Worktree path identity\n');
    expect(p39, '§3.9 is missing').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(note, "§3.9's closing note is missing").toBeGreaterThan(p39);
    expect(p310, "§3.10 is missing, or stands above §3.9's note").toBeGreaterThan(note);
    expect(p4, '§4 must follow §3.10').toBeGreaterThan(p310);
  });

  it('states the leaf words L0 declares, and the collect line each is written on', () => {
    const words = leafWords();
    expect(words.length, '`COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE` not found in shared/api.ts').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect([...words].sort()).toEqual(LEAF_WRITERS.map(([w]) => w).sort());
    expect(s).toContain(`\`meas.leaf\` takes ${COUNT_WORD[words.length] ?? String(words.length)} words, ${andList(words.map(q))}`);
    for (const [word, fn] of LEAF_WRITERS) {
      expect(shFunction(ccd, fn), `${fn} writes no \`meas.leaf ${word}\``).toMatch(new RegExp(`\\bmeas\\.leaf ${word}\\b`));
      expect(s).toContain(`${q(word)} on ${q(fn)}'s \`done\` line`);
    }

  it('names the mount helper `_ws_leaf_remove` asks twice, and quotes its Darwin guard', () => {
    const leafCode = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_leaf_remove'));
    expect(leafCode.length, '`_ws_leaf_remove` not found in ccd/ccd').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const asked = [...new Set(leafCode.flatMap((l) => [...l.matchAll(/\b(_ws_[a-z_]*mounts_clear)\b/g)].map((m) => m[1])))];
    expect(asked).toEqual(['_ws_removal_mounts_clear']);
    expect(leafCode.filter((l) => /\b_ws_removal_mounts_clear\b/.test(l))).toHaveLength(2);
    const guard = (codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_removal_mounts_clear'))[0] ?? '').trim();
    expect(guard, "the helper's first line of code is not its Darwin guard").toMatch(/\bCCD_OS\b.*\bdarwin\b/);
    expect(s).toContain(q('_ws_removal_mounts_clear'));

    expect(probeClassTable(), '`aside` is not classed per-leaf in collectLane.ts').toMatch(/(?:^|[\s,{])aside:\s*'per-leaf'/);

  it('carries the entry counts as numbers only, and names what was judged instead', () => {
    const lead = 'Measured on the fleet box before the first edit, counts only:';
    const judged = 'Not measured, and judged instead:';
    const at = s.indexOf(lead);
    const to = s.indexOf(judged, at + 1);
    expect(at, 'the entry-counts bullet is missing').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(to, 'the judged bullet must follow the counts').toBeGreaterThan(at);
    const counts = s.slice(at + lead.length, to);
    expect(counts).toMatch(/\d/);
    for (const bad of ['/', '~', 'demo-']) expect(counts, bad).not.toContain(bad);
    expect(counts).not.toMatch(UNFILLED);
    for (const cls of ['an inner-NUL back-link', 'an unresolvable standing workdir',
      'cut keyless collect rows beyond the recorded count']) expect(s.slice(to), cls).toContain(cls);

  it('names every departure, residual and closed carry by slug', () => {
    for (const d of DEPARTURES) expect(s, d).toContain(q(d));
    const residuals = block(raw, '**Stated residuals');
    const closed = block(raw, '**Closed carries');
    expect(residuals, 'the stated-residuals list is missing').not.toBe('');
    expect(closed, 'the closed-carries list is missing').not.toBe('');

    expect(s).not.toMatch(UNFILLED);

    expect(names.length, 'no ccd name read from §3.10').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const n of names) expect(new RegExp(`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])${n}(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`).test(ccd), n).toBe(true);
    for (const [name, file] of SERVER_NAMES) {
      expect(s, name).toContain(q(name));
      expect(read(file), `${name} in ${file}`).toMatch(new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`));
    }
  });

  it('marks items 11, 12, 14, 16 to 19 and 32 to 36 built in W2, and items 38 and 40 built by child-reclamation wave 10', () => {
    const w2 = [11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36];
    for (const n of w2) expect(spec, `item ${n}`).toMatch(new RegExp(`^\\| ${n} \\|[^\\n]*\\| Built \\(W2\\) \\|`, 'm'));
    for (const n of [38, 40]) {
      expect(spec, `item ${n}`).toMatch(new RegExp(`^\\| ${n} \\|[^\\n]*\\| Built \\(child-reclamation wave 10\\) \\|`, 'm'));
    }
    expect(spec.split('| Built (W2) |').length - 1).toBe(w2.length);
    expect(spec.split('| Built (child-reclamation wave 10) |').length - 1).toBe(2);
  });
});

describe('the programme’s rulings file carries the W2 as-built note (path-identity spec §3.10)', () => {
  const c = read(CONTRACT);
  const head = /^### §17 as built \(path-identity W2, run \d+\)$/m.exec(c);
  const at = head ? head.index : -1;
  const next = at < 0 ? -1 : c.slice(at + 1).search(/\n#{2,3} /);
  const raw = at < 0 ? '' : c.slice(at, next < 0 ? c.length : at + 1 + next);
  const note = flat(raw);

  it('stands in §17, after the W1b note, and before any §18', () => {
    expect(at, 'the as-built note is missing, or its heading names no run number').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    const w1b = c.search(/^### §17 as built \(path-identity W1b, run \d+\)$/m);
    expect(w1b, "W1b's note is missing").toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(at).toBeGreaterThan(w1b);
    const s18 = c.search(/^## 18\. /m);
    if (s18 > -1) expect(at).toBeLessThan(s18);

  it('records R93, R95, R89 and R83 as the wave left them', () => {
    for (const lead of ["**R93 (the programme's shape).**", '**R95 as built (the mount question).**',

    const residuals = block(raw, '**Stated residuals');
    const closed = block(raw, '**Closed carries');
    for (const r of residualsAtTheTip()) expect(residuals, r).toContain(q(r));
    for (const k of closedAtTheTip()) {
      expect(closed, k).toContain(q(k));
      expect(residuals, `${k} is closed, so it is no residual`).not.toContain(q(k));

    expect(note).not.toMatch(DEVIATION_TOKEN);
    expect(note).not.toMatch(FOUR_DIGIT_RANGE);
    expect(note).not.toMatch(UNFILLED);
  });

  it('lists what each task found while building, by slug', () => {
    const found = block(raw, '**Found while building');
    expect(found, 'the found-while-building list is missing').not.toBe('');
    for (const slug of FOUND_WHILE_BUILDING) expect(found, slug).toContain(q(slug));
  });
});

```markdown
### 3.10 As built (W2)

W2 built this section's TR1 to TR8 and TR12, and items 32 to 36 of §7: item 32 a prose fix in two test headers, items
33 to 36 test-only. This subsection records where
what it built narrows, corrects or spells out §3.1 to §3.9, and names the residuals it leaves. It amends, and rewrites
none of the text above. Every claim is measured at the wave's tip unless it says otherwise.

**The witness drop (TR3, TR4).**
- All three drops go through one generation-exact `_ws_tmproot_witness_drop`: `_ws_tmproot_remove`'s drop and step
  6's two kept arms. The helper prints nothing. It answers complete (0, with `_WS_WDROP` set to `dropped` or
  `absent`), kept (1) or unmeasured (2), with its reason in `_WS_WDROP_WHY`. Every kept reason begins "its witness was
  kept: ".
- Its order is fixed:
  1. An id no witness is named for is kept, with nothing touched.
  2. No witness standing is complete, `absent`.
  3. A witness that does not parse is unmeasured.
  4. The device the witness records is asked (`_ws_collect_root_dev`). An answer of 1 or 2 is unmeasured.
  5. The id's quarantine slots are listed (`_ws_collect_slots_of`). Any slot of the id keeps the witness, whether or
     not a record names it. A quarantine that cannot be listed is unmeasured.
  6. The leaf is proved absent again.
  7. Only then is exactly the generation read dropped.
- Where a NOREPLACE move exists (`_ws_collect_mv_ok`), the drop is the collector's own compare-and-drop,
  `_ws_collect_witness_cad`, fed the first read's fields, so a newer generation is kept. Where none exists (on Darwin,
  and on a Linux `mv` without `--no-copy`), the helper reads the witness again, compares all six parsed fields with
  its first read, unlinks the live name, and proves it gone. The device and slot checks run on both paths.
- `drop-helper-reproves-the-absence`: Figure 3 goes from the tail's absence proof straight to the parse. As built, the
  helper proves the leaf absent again (`_ws_reclaim_absent`) after its witness read and before the drop. So "kept"
  always means "not proven gone". A leaf that stands again answers kept, never unmeasured.
- `kept-witness-reason-in-the-row-not-on-stderr`: Figure 3's slot arm says "keep witness, warn". As built, the helper
  prints nothing on any arm, and the reason reaches the done row through the tail's `tmpwhy`. The compare-and-drop
  prints one warning when it cannot move a generation back from its aside. The helper silences that warning at its
  call and carries it as its own reason.
- `_ws_tmproot_remove` maps the helper's kept and unmeasured answers to its own 2 (unmeasured). It never maps them to
  its 1, which means the leaf was refused. Its reason leads "no leaf stands, but" (true whether its leaf half removed
  the leaf or proved it absent), followed by the helper's.
- Step 6 has two kept arms: the in-use answer, and the unmeasured answer, which is always the arm on Darwin. Both
  record a drop that is not complete as `tmpRootKept` `unmeasured`, with a reason that leads "no leaf stands, but".
  No `tmpRootKept` word was added. Each of the three callers has a mutation pin of its own, and a scan pin refuses any
  drop call suppressed with `|| :`.
- A `~/.cc-tmp` deleted whole now holds its witnesses, because its device cannot be read.
- So, as the In short says, three W2 changes keep or return an id to the collector's population. TR3 and TR4 keep a
  witness the tail cannot prove it may drop. TR6 returns the id of an orphaned compare-and-drop aside (below). Each
  such id stays collectable only under the collector's full ladder.

**Mounts (TR5).**
- Every new mount question goes through one helper, `_ws_removal_mounts_clear`. It reuses `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`
  rather than copying it. It answers 0 when nothing is mounted at the path or under it. It answers 2 when a mount
  stands there, when the kernel's table could not be read whole, or, in its resolve mode, when the path could not be
  resolved. It never answers 1, so every caller refuses a mount and an unreadable table alike.
- Its first line of code is the one Darwin guard, `[[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || return 0`. On Darwin nothing is
  asked, and "not asked" and "clear" both mean proceed. There are three Darwin pins, one per site: the leaf, a standing
  nested checkout, and the child's own worktree. Each poisons the mount table's reader and proves the clean removal
  still reaches its Darwin path. Deleting the guard reds all three.
- `leaf-mount-ask-before-the-owner-bits`: §3.5 puts the leaf's first ask "immediately after the `lreal` check". As
  built, `_ws_leaf_remove` asks directly after its device compare: before the owner-bits chmod of the leaf itself,
  before `_ws_leaf_checkouts`, and before `_ws_reclaim_normalise`. It asks again directly before `rm`. This is
  stricter: with a same-device bind at the leaf, the chmod would otherwise change the bind source's root first. Either
  ask's refusal becomes the leaf's 2, unmeasured, and nothing under the leaf is touched.
- The leaf's path is physical by construction, because its root is resolved before the leaf is named. So is each
  standing nested checkout's path at step 3. Neither is resolved again, and a mode-000 leaf keeps the answer it had.
  Step 4 asks in the resolve mode, because a workdir may sit under a symlinked ancestor.
- A physical spelling that begins with `//` collapses to `/` before the table is asked, as Linux reads it. It is not
  refused.
- Through the tail's step 6, a mount under the clips leaf or under the temp-root leaf keeps that leaf `unmeasured`
  (`clipsKept`, `tmpRootKept`). The leaf and its witness stay standing.
- The tail asks before `keep_of` and again before `git worktree remove --force`. It does so at every standing nested
  checkout (step 3) and at the child's own worktree (step 4). A mount, or a table that cannot be read, fails the
  reclaim or the expiry as `worktree-remove-failed`, with the breadcrumb and that tree standing. A standing workdir
  that cannot be resolved fails the same way, before `keep_of`. The refusal's existing sentence says ccrc could not
  prove that the tree, or a checkout inside it, is its own. That sentence already covers a mount.
- The collector's step 6 removes through `_ws_leaf_remove`. So a mount that appears after the collector's own step-5
  ask now answers `failed quarantine-kept`, with the record and the slot kept.
- The arms that remove the record of a checkout that is already gone ask nothing. No ask covers the whole child before
  step 3's loop.
- A mount found at step 3 or step 4 is found after the pane kill, so each retry fails the same way until the mount is
  gone.

**The kept-leaf end (TR1, TR2).**
- `meas.leaf` takes two words, `removed` and `absent`: `removed` on `_ws_collect_finish`'s `done` line, and `absent` on
  `_ws_collect_witness_only`'s `done` line. They are spelled once, as the keys of `COLLECT_LEAF_END_TABLE` in
  `shared/api.ts`.
- When `_lc_json`'s meas rung drops the other measurement fields, it keeps `meas.leaf`. Its last-resort line keeps it
  too, so a collect line cut twice stays decided.
- The store reads a collect row raw: `lifecycleLeafEndsFor` passes its `measJson` and `truncated` to
  `childReclaimLeafEndRead`, which answers one of four kinds:
  - a word;
  - keyless: an uncut line with no `leaf`, written by an older ccd. It ends the item, as every collect row did before
    (TR2 A);
  - truncated-keyless: a cut line with no `leaf`. It fails closed;
  - malformed: a `leaf` that is not one of ccd's words, or a `measJson` that is not a JSON object. It fails closed.
- The ends are monotone. A `removed` or keyless row after the source ends the temp-root half, wherever it falls among
  the rows. Otherwise, an `absent` row keeps the item until the 7-day horizon, with one clause added:
  `The collector found nothing at ~/.cc-tmp/<id> and dropped its witness; if ~/.cc-tmp is a mount, check that it is mounted.`
- The clause rides only an item whose temp-root half was reported kept, and never a clips-only item. An item that ends
  on `absent` never joins the `kept-many` collapse; that marker lives on the server's own type, not on the wire. An
  unread collect row (malformed or truncated-keyless) adds no prose: the item reads as if no collect had happened.
- `present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy`: §3.4 says the server fails closed for a present malformed value. As built, a
  stored `"leaf":null` reads keyless, and on an uncut row it ends the item. The reason: the reviver writes every key,
  the store persists that revived object, and ccd's encoder never writes a null value. So `"leaf":null` is the store's
  own spelling of "not carried". A forged one ends the item, as a forged `removed` would. Any other present value is
  carried as its text and never read as absent.
- The deploy is fleet box first. In the window between the two boxes, an old server drops `meas.leaf` at ingest:
  - An uncut collect `done` it stored reads keyless after the upgrade, and ends as every collect row ended before.
  - A collect `done` the encoder cut is stored keyless with `truncated` set. After the upgrade it reads
    truncated-keyless and keeps its item until the horizon.

  Neither ends a line early.

**C5, the compare-and-drop aside (TR6).**
- `aside-joins-the-population`: the server's population admits an id when two things hold. At least one name under
  `tmproots/` parses as that id's `.<id>.drop.<pid>` (`COLLECT_ASIDE_NAME_RE`, `parseCollectAsideName`), and
  `isTmpRootId` holds. Such ids fold into the population's `ids`, with no new field. Every other dot-leading name is
  still dropped uncounted. ccd decides "sole" and "parseable" from the bodies. A parity pin holds the grammar equal to
  ccd's `_ws_collect_aside_id`. This changes the programme contract's population rule, which dropped every
  dot-leading name.
- The audit judges a sole parseable aside as the witness, read-only, so the token it mints equals the verb's token
  after the restore. "Parseable" means the aside would read sound as the witness: one parser,
  `_ws_tmproot_witness_parse`, reads both.
- Before the reap lock, a sole aside that parses as the witness opens the lock at once. Two or more asides, one that
  does not parse, or asides that cannot be listed answer only after the registry peek, so `registered` keeps its
  place ahead of any of those answers.
- `aside-probe-word`: §3.6 calls an ambiguous, malformed or competing aside "unmeasured", and names no word. As built,
  two or more asides, or one that does not parse as a witness of the id, answer the probe word `aside`, which the lane
  classes `per-leaf`. An aside listing that fails keeps the word `witness`.
- An old-generation aside beside a new leaf answers the terminal `witness-mismatch`, and the detail names the aside's
  path.
- `aside-restore-by-link-not-rename`: §3.6 restores the aside "with a NOREPLACE rename". As built,
  `_ws_tmproot_aside_settle` restores it under the reap lock in three steps: `link`, then a dev:ino proof of the
  witness name, then `rm` of the aside. It runs in the verb before its fork, and in the tail before step 6. It is
  portable, so the tail restores on Darwin too. It never clobbers, since `link` fails on a name that exists. A crash
  between `link` and `rm` leaves two names for one inode, which is an equal witness, and the next settle unlinks it.
- Beside a standing witness, an equal aside (the same dev:ino, or the same bytes) is unlinked. Any other aside is left,
  with a warning.
- At the verb, the settle's doubt blocks only an act: it applies only when the fork answers `collectable`.
- `tail-aside-warns-without-keeping`: at the reclaim and expiry tail, an aside the settle can neither restore nor
  unlink prints a warning and never sets `tmpRootKept`. An aside keeps no leaf, and the collector lists it per-leaf.
- The compare-and-drop's warning no longer says that no reader takes a dot-leading name. It says where the aside was
  left, and what the next settle under the reap lock does with it.

  of §3.6's `^0*([0-9]*)$`. The anchored form has exactly one parse, so its answer does not depend on how a regex
  library orders the matches of a starred group. Its results are the old strip's, and its status is read: a capture
  that fails answers 2, unmeasured, never a silent 24 h. Two pins hold it: a row of 200,000 zeros built in the shell,
  and a structure pin. `ccd/ccrc` carries a copy of the old strip, which is left to its

**R83 changed (`aside-joins-the-population`).**
- R83's population drops every dot-leading name. As built, it admits an id when at least one `.<id>.drop.<pid>` name
  under `tmproots/` parses for it and `isTmpRootId` holds. These ids fold into `ids`, with no new field. Every other
  dot-leading name is still dropped uncounted, and so is every dot-leading name in the quarantine listing. The
  coordinator's docs change amends R83's text.

**TR3 and TR4 (the witness drop).**
- One helper drops a witness. In order, it:
  1. asks the device that the witness records;
  2. lists the id's quarantine slots;
  3. proves the leaf absent again;
  4. drops exactly the generation it read. Where a NOREPLACE move exists, it uses the collector's compare-and-drop;
     elsewhere, a field compare.

  Any standing slot keeps the witness.
- `drop-helper-reproves-the-absence`: the re-proof widens the spec's Figure 3. A leaf that stands again answers kept.
- `kept-witness-reason-in-the-row-not-on-stderr`: the helper prints nothing, and its reason reaches the done row.
- `_ws_tmproot_remove` and step 6's two kept arms record a drop that is not complete as `tmpRootKept` `unmeasured`. No
  drop call is suppressed.

**TR6 (the compare-and-drop aside).**
- The audit judges a sole parseable aside as the witness, read-only. Before the reap lock, that aside opens the lock
  at once, and its ambiguity answer (`aside`, or `witness` when the asides cannot be listed) comes only after the
  registry peek.
- `aside-probe-word`: an ambiguous, malformed or competing aside answers the new per-leaf probe word `aside`.
- `aside-restore-by-link-not-rename`: the restore is `link`, then a dev:ino proof, then `rm`. It runs under the reap
  lock: in the verb before its fork, and in the tail before step 6.
- `tail-aside-warns-without-keeping`: at the tail, an unsettled aside warns and never sets `tmpRootKept`. At the verb,
  its doubt applies only when the fork answers `collectable`.

**TR7, TR8 and TR12.**
- The floor knob's zero strip is one anchored capture.
- A back-link with a NUL inside the path it names is refused.
- Six late recycled-spawn boundaries are pinned in a Linux-only file that is on the load-flake list.
- Items 34 to 36 are pinned, item 36 at <n:item36> cases.

**Stated residuals**, named with no number; spec §3.10 says each one in full.
- `tail-drop-not-noreplace-without-mv-no-copy`, `stale-aside-beside-a-new-leaf-is-a-mismatch` and
  `git-mount-crossing-unmeasured`. The operator may measure the last on a throwaway box of their own choosing.
- Forwarded to workspace lifecycle: `audit-normalise-has-no-mount-ask`, `mount-found-after-the-kill-repeats`,
  `human-gated-removals-ask-no-mounts`, `no-whole-child-mount-ask-before-step-3` and
  `vanished-checkout-arms-ask-no-mounts`.
- `absent-clause-names-a-drop-the-compare-kept`, `found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-collector-item`,
  `found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-reclaim-item`, `non-object-meas-reads-as-keyless`,
  `ccrc-timeout-knob-strip-is-quadratic` and `registry-id-l0-comments-say-ccd-scans-the-session-value`.
- Standing from spec §3.7: `rec-eq-f-recycled-admin`, `device-test-cannot-see-a-same-device-bind-mount`,
  `permanent-device-change-holds-every-absence`, `cc-tmp-deleted-whole-holds-its-witnesses`,
  `source-parent-without-owner-write-loops` and `tmproot-probe-misses-the-whole-volume-spelling`.

**Closed carries**, each by slug.
- `tail-drop-believes-an-absent-leaf` and `tail-drop-ignores-a-recordless-slot`, by TR3 and TR4.
- `server-docstrings-call-ccds-predicate-dot-only` and `comments-say-ccd-scans-the-session-value`, the two W1b
  carries. The server's docstrings and `collect-l0.test.ts`'s comment now say what ccd has checked since W1b; two
  comments in `registry-id-l0.test.ts` do not yet, a stated residual.
- `collector-learning-audit-relies-on-the-population-gate`, `session-shape-prose-predates-the-id-gate` and
  `leaf-end-acts-spelled-twice`.
- `cad-header-calls-the-tail-drop-a-plain-unlink`: the compare-and-drop's header no longer calls the tail's drop a
  plain unlink.
- `learning-audit-gate-prose-in-two-test-comments`: two test comments no longer say that the learning audit asks no id
  predicate of its own, and the id census registers its gate.
- `review-335-f9-needle-outgrows-the-cap-under-this-tmpdir`, folded into item 36.

**Found while building, per task.** Task 16's slugs concern this record itself, and only the plan's Task 16 deviation
entry defines them.
- Task 2: `read-small-partial-read-cleared` and `nul-why-leads-with-the-admin-path`. The small-file reader now clears
  what it read when a read fails part-way, so no caller sees part of a file. The NUL refusal's reason leads with the
  admin path, as every sibling reason of the checkout question does, and every pin reads the uncut reason.
- Task 5: `step-4-unresolvable-workdir-fails-before-keep-of` and `worktree-remove-failed-sentence-covers-a-mount`. A
  standing workdir that cannot be resolved now fails `worktree-remove-failed` before `keep_of`. The refusal's
  sentence says ccrc could not prove that the tree at the workspace's path, or a checkout inside it, is its own. That
  sentence already covers a mount, so it was not edited.
- Task 9: `aside-half-not-in-the-id-argv-census`. The id census registers the learning audit's new gate, not the id
  check the population makes on an aside's name, so the census does not cite that check.
- Task 10: `prelock-resets-a-pre-peek-aside-answer`. Before the reap lock, the pass clears the aside judge's first
  answer before the registry peek, so an `in-progress` audit document never carries a stale probe word `aside`.

**(4b) The start-line table, `_lc_json`'s length, and the hunks at or before line 19162 (R43).** Write two scratch scripts once ((4c) writes a third). Each takes its inputs as file paths, so (4h) can feed it a seeded copy.

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-path-identity-w2-absences-and-mounts/task17
cat > "$L/starts.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# base head bound -> the start line of every function that starts at or before line bound of base (R43's corpus
# bound, MAXREF), _lc_json's length, and plan-a's cited line 4896; rc 1 on any move, rc 2 on a bound that is no line
b="$1" h="$2" w="${3-}"; rc=0
[[ "$w" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "W=$w is no line number"; exit 2; }
echo "W=$w"
fns() { awk -v w="$2" '/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(\) *\{/{n=$0; sub(/\(\).*/,"",n); if (w == "" || NR <= w) print n, NR}' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1; }
fns "$b" "$w" > "$b.starts"; fns "$h" "" > "$h.starts"
LC_ALL=C join "$b.starts" "$h.starts" | awk '$2 != $3 { print "MOVED", $0; bad = 1 } END { print (bad ? "starts MOVED" : "starts unmoved"); exit bad }' || rc=1
v=$(LC_ALL=C join -v1 "$b.starts" "$h.starts"); [[ -z "$v" ]] || { echo "VANISHED $v"; rc=1; }
len() { awk '/^_lc_json\(\) *\{/{s=NR} s && /^}/{print NR - s + 1; exit}' "$1"; }
lb=$(len "$b"); lh=$(len "$h"); echo "_lc_json lines base=$lb head=$lh"; [[ -n "$lb" && "$lb" == "$lh" ]] || rc=1
if [[ "$(sed -n 4896p "$b")" == "$(sed -n 4896p "$h")" ]]; then echo "line 4896 unchanged"; else echo "line 4896 CHANGED"; rc=1; fi
exit "$rc"
EOF
cat > "$L/hunks-above.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# base head bound -> every -U0 hunk that changes a line at or before line bound, or inserts before it, as "a,b +c,d ok|SHIFT";
# rc 1 when any is not in place. A hunk that only inserts after line bound lies outside the frozen zone and is not listed
b="$1" h="$2" bound="$3"
git diff --no-index --no-color -U0 -- "$b" "$h" | awk -v bound="$bound" '
  /^@@ / { o = $2; n = $3; sub(/^-/, "", o); sub(/^\+/, "", n); split(o, x, ","); split(n, y, ",")
           a = x[1] + 0; bb = (2 in x) ? x[2] + 0 : 1; c = y[1] + 0; d = (2 in y) ? y[2] + 0 : 1
           if (a < bound || (a == bound && bb > 0)) { k++; v = (a == c && bb == d) ? "ok" : "SHIFT"; if (v != "ok") bad++; print a "," bb " +" c "," d " " v } }
  END { print "hunks at or before line " bound ": " k + 0 ", not in place: " bad + 0; exit (bad > 0) }'
EOF
BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main); git show "$BASE":ccd/ccd > "$L/ccd.base"; git show HEAD:ccd/ccd > "$L/ccd.head"
MAXREF=$(for f in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-graphify-compaction-card-design.md docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-10-graphify-compaction-card-plan-a.md README.md; do grep -ohE ':[0-9]+([-–][0-9]+)?' "$f"; done | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | awk -v max="$(wc -l < "$L/ccd.base")" '$1 <= max' | sort -n | tail -1); echo "MAXREF=$MAXREF"; printf '%s\n' "$MAXREF" > "$L/maxref"; [ "$MAXREF" = 19162 ] && echo "MAXREF is R43's" || echo "MAXREF other than 19162: STOP maxref-unmeasured"
bash "$L/starts.sh" "$L/ccd.base" "$L/ccd.head" "$MAXREF"; echo "starts rc=$?"
bash "$L/hunks-above.sh" "$L/ccd.base" "$L/ccd.head" "$MAXREF"; echo "hunks rc=$?"
awk '/^_lc_json\(\) *\{/{print "lc_json starts", NR} /^_lc_json\(\) *\{/,/^}/{e=NR} END{print "lc_json ends", e}' "$L/ccd.base"
```

**(4c) `shared/api.ts` above its foot, neutral as a whole.** Task 12 Step 3e rewraps the seven-line `tmpRootKept` docstring to six lines and gives the freed line to the `leaf` member, four lines later. So its two hunks are not one line for one, and `hunks-above.sh`, which calls a hunk `ok` only when its two sides have the same size, would call both `SHIFT`. This step writes a third scratch script, which tests the region as a whole. `hunks-above.sh` stays for `ccd/ccd` and `journalparse.ts`, whose edits are one line for one.

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-path-identity-w2-absences-and-mounts/task17; BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
git show "$BASE":shared/api.ts > "$L/api.base"; git show HEAD:shared/api.ts > "$L/api.head"
FOOT=$(grep -n 'APPENDED at the foot, never inserted above' "$L/api.base" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); echo "FOOT=$FOOT"; printf '%s\n' "$FOOT" > "$L/foot"
cat > "$L/api-neutral.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# base head foot -> shared/api.ts is line-neutral above its foot AS A WHOLE: the foot marker, the tmpRootKept
# docstring's first line, LifecycleMeas's closing } and the key map's line each on the same line in both; lines 1 to the
# docstring identical; lines from the closing } through the foot identical but the key map's line; and exactly three -U0
# hunks above the foot: the docstring (a,7 +a,6), the leaf member (b,0 +b,1, inside LifecycleMeas) and the key map's
# line (c,1 +c,1). rc 1 on any other answer
b="$1" h="$2" foot="$3"; rc=0
at() { grep -n -m1 -- "$1" "$2" | cut -d: -f1; }
close() { awk '/^export interface LifecycleMeas \{/{f=1} f&&/^}/{print NR; exit}' "$1"; }
fh=$(at 'APPENDED at the foot, never inserted above' "$h"); echo "foot base=$foot head=$fh"; [[ -n "$fh" && "$fh" == "$foot" ]] || rc=1
db=$(at '^  /\*\* The per-session temp root' "$b"); dh=$(at '^  /\*\* The per-session temp root' "$h")
cb=$(close "$b"); ch=$(close "$h"); kb=$(at '^  unremoved: true, childOf: true,' "$b"); kh=$(at '^  unremoved: true, childOf: true,' "$h")
echo "docstring base=$db head=$dh; close base=$cb head=$ch; key map base=$kb head=$kh"
[[ -n "$db" && -n "$cb" && -n "$kb" && "$db" == "$dh" && "$cb" == "$ch" && "$kb" == "$kh" ]] || { echo "an anchor MOVED or is missing"; exit 1; }
if cmp -s <(sed -n "1,$((db - 1))p" "$b") <(sed -n "1,$((db - 1))p" "$h"); then echo "lines 1-$((db - 1)) identical"; else echo "lines 1-$((db - 1)) DIFFER"; rc=1; fi
if cmp -s <(awk -v c="$cb" -v f="$foot" -v k="$kb" 'NR >= c && NR <= f && NR != k' "$b") <(awk -v c="$cb" -v f="$foot" -v k="$kb" 'NR >= c && NR <= f && NR != k' "$h"); then echo "lines $cb-$foot identical but $kb"; else echo "lines $cb-$foot DIFFER beyond $kb"; rc=1; fi
git diff --no-index --no-color -U0 -- "$b" "$h" | awk -v foot="$foot" -v d="$db" -v c="$cb" -v k="$kb" '
  /^@@ / { o = $2; n = $3; sub(/^-/, "", o); sub(/^\+/, "", n); split(o, x, ","); split(n, y, ",")
           a = x[1] + 0; bb = (2 in x) ? x[2] + 0 : 1; e = y[1] + 0; g = (2 in y) ? y[2] + 0 : 1
           if (a < foot || (a == foot && bb > 0)) { m++
             v = (a == d && bb == 7 && e == d && g == 6) ? "docstring" : (a > d && a < c && bb == 0 && e == a && g == 1) ? "leaf" : (a == k && bb == 1 && e == k && g == 1) ? "key-map" : "UNEXPECTED"
             if (v == "UNEXPECTED") bad++; else seen[v]++
             print a "," bb " +" e "," g " " v } }
  END { ok = (m == 3 && bad == 0 && seen["docstring"] == 1 && seen["leaf"] == 1 && seen["key-map"] == 1)
        print "hunks above the foot: " m + 0 ", unexpected: " bad + 0 ", shape " (ok ? "as Task 12 builds it" : "WRONG"); exit !ok }' || rc=1
exit "$rc"
EOF
bash "$L/api-neutral.sh" "$L/api.base" "$L/api.head" "$FOOT"; echo "api rc=$?"
grep -n '^export interface LifecycleMeas {' "$L/api.base" "$L/api.head"
grep -c 'tmpRootKept: true, clipsKept: true, leaf: true,' "$L/api.head"

The step is two Bash calls, because the mail list must be read BEFORE anything is sent: call A lists mail and does nothing else; call B measures the tip and sends. A coordinator mail that changes the wave is acted on first, and the step then starts again from call A, so the tip is measured afresh.

Write `$L/wave-done-prose.md` with the Write tool. It holds:
- the PR number;
- `N_FILES` and the shard sum;
- the long-TMPDIR file count and its result;
- the citation number, `MAXREF`, and `_lc_json`'s line count;
- the item-36 count;
- the entry counts (numbers only);
- the full run's id and url, or `full-run-id-unlisted`;
- each departure by slug, and each stated residual and each closed carry by slug as spec §3.10 commits them;
- each reading a task named for the coordinator, by slug: `read-small-partial-read-cleared` and `nul-why-leads-with-the-admin-path` (Task 2), `aside-half-not-in-the-id-argv-census` (Task 9) and `prelock-resets-a-pre-peek-aside-answer` (Task 10), each with the coordinator's ruling where one was given;
- any STOP, `main-red` or absorption of `main`.

**Call A: the mail list, and nothing else.** Run one Bash call:

```bash
API="$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc-api"
who=$("$API" whoami) || { printf 'identity refused: %s\n' "$who" >&2; exit 1; }
id=${who#*\"id\":\"}; id=${id%%\"*}
[[ -n "$id" ]] || { echo 'identity missing' >&2; exit 1; }
"$API" mail list --to "$id"
```

Read the list. If it holds a coordinator mail that changes the wave, do NOT run call B: act on that mail, then start this step again from call A. Otherwise run call B.

**Call B: re-derive the identity, measure the tip, compose and send.** Run one Bash call. Set `RUN` to the run id the dispatch brief names and `SUITE` to Step 1's recorded word. Set `FAILURE` to empty, or to `shallow`, `ceiling` or `unclear` when a check failed (clause 15):

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-path-identity-w2-absences-and-mounts/task17
RUN=0; SUITE=green; FAILURE=
API="$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc-api"
who=$("$API" whoami) || { printf 'identity refused: %s\n' "$who" >&2; exit 1; }
id=${who#*\"id\":\"};     id=${id%%\"*}
uuid=${who#*\"uuid\":\"}; uuid=${uuid%%\"*}
[[ -n "$id" && -n "$uuid" && "$RUN" != 0 ]] || { echo 'identity or run id missing' >&2; exit 1; }
TIP=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
test "$(git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$(git branch --show-current)" | cut -f1)" = "$TIP" || { echo 'remote tip is not HEAD' >&2; exit 1; }
PR=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
PHASE=$(gh pr view --json state,isDraft --jq 'if .isDraft then "draft" elif .state=="OPEN" then "open" elif .state=="MERGED" then "merged" elif .state=="CLOSED" then "closed" else "unknown" end')
node -e '
const fs = require("fs");
const [id, uuid, run, suite, failure, tip, pr, phase, prose] = process.argv.slice(1);
const lines = ["suite: " + suite];
if (failure) lines.push("failure: " + failure);
lines.push(JSON.stringify({ branchTip: tip, prNumber: Number(pr), prPhase: phase, handoffCommit: tip }));
lines.push(fs.readFileSync(prose, "utf8"));
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ fromId: id, fromUuid: uuid, toId: "coordinator", runId: Number(run), kind: "status", subject: "wave-done", body: lines.join("\n"), artifacts: [] }));
' "$id" "$uuid" "$RUN" "$SUITE" "$FAILURE" "$TIP" "$PR" "$PHASE" "$L/wave-done-prose.md" > "$L/wave-done.json"
"$API" mail send --json "$L/wave-done.json"
```

Expected:
- The response is `{"ok":true,…}`.
- Read the answer from the body, never from the exit status. A `stale-uuid` means the call is re-run whole, with the identity derived again.
- After sending, stop pushing (clause 9).
- Call B never lists mail: the decision not to send is made on call A's list, before call B runs. A `stale-uuid` re-run of call B is call B alone; any other re-run starts from call A.

## Deviations found

**The block (R37).** Twenty-five numbers were issued on 2026-10-16, before the plan was committed, and each is defined here singly: one per substantive departure, and one per task for its plan-text corrections and extra pins. A departure the wave finds is named by slug in the wave-done, and gets a number issued at its fix round, defined here singly.

**No concrete placeholder stands in this file.** `dtbd.test.ts` reds one in any tracked file (it runs `git grep` over every tracked file), so every slot below carries its issued number, and a task body names its slot by that number or by its bare slug.

How numbers are issued and assigned:
- The coordinator assigns the numbers. Each substantive departure gets its own number, defined here once. Each task gets one number for its plan-text corrections and extra pins.
- A departure the worker finds is named by a short kebab-case slug in the wave-done. The worker never gives it a number, and never calls the allocator.

### Substantive departures, one number each

Each entry names what the spec said, what the code at the tip does, and the ruling.
- **D-5162** (Task 6) `drop-helper-reproves-the-absence`. Figure 3 goes from the tail's absence proof straight to the parse, device, slot and generation checks. As built, the helper proves the leaf absent again (`_ws_reclaim_absent`) after its witness read and before the compare-and-drop. "Kept" therefore always means "not proven gone", and a leaf standing again answers kept, rc 1 (P8). The pins that asserted the old window were rewritten in the same commit (R3).
- **D-5163** (Task 6) `kept-witness-reason-in-the-row-not-on-stderr`. Figure 3's slot arm says "keep witness, warn". As built, the helper prints nothing on any arm: the reason reaches the done row through `tmpwhy` and the detail, the reused compare-and-drop's one move-back warning is silenced at the helper's call and carried as its reason (P15), and the warn-text pins were rewritten (R6).
- **D-5164** (Task 4) `leaf-mount-ask-before-the-owner-bits`. Spec §3.5 puts the leaf's first mount ask "immediately after the `lreal` check". As built, it sits directly after the st_dev compare, before the owner-bits chmod of the leaf itself. That is stricter: with a same-device bind AT the leaf, the chmod would otherwise change the bind source's root first (R8).
- **D-5165** (Task 9) `aside-joins-the-population`. Contract R83 step 3 drops every dot-leading name, the compare-and-drop aside included. As built, the server's population admits an id when at least one `.<id>.drop.<pid>` name parses for it and `isTmpRootId` holds (S2). The ids fold into `ids`, with no new field. ccd decides "sole" and "parseable". The coordinator's docs PR amends R83's text (R22, R24).
- **D-5166** (Task 10) `aside-probe-word`. Spec §3.6 says an ambiguous, malformed or competing aside leaves the attempt "unmeasured", and names no word. As built, it is the new per-leaf probe word `aside`, classed `per-leaf` by the lane in the same PR; a listing failure keeps `witness`. `collect-readers` moved both ways (R20).
- **D-5167** (Task 11) `aside-restore-by-link-not-rename`. Spec §3.6 restores the aside "with a NOREPLACE rename". As built, it is `link`, then a dev:ino proof of the witness name, then `rm` of the aside. That is portable (the tail runs on Darwin) and no-clobber, and a crash between `link` and `rm` leaves an equal witness, which the next settle unlinks (R21).
- **D-5168** (Task 11) `tail-aside-warns-without-keeping`. Spec §3.6 calls an ambiguous, malformed or competing aside "unmeasured". As built, at the reclaim and expiry tail an unsettled aside prints a warning and never sets `tmpRootKept`: an aside keeps no leaf, and the collector lists it per-leaf. At the verb, the doubt applies only when the fork answers `collectable` (R23, R26).
- **D-5169** (Task 13) `present-null-leaf-reads-as-legacy`. Spec §3.4 says the server "fails closed for a present malformed or out-of-vocabulary value". As built, a stored `"leaf":null` reads keyless and, on an uncut row, ends the item: `reviveMeas` writes every key and the store persists that revived object, so `"leaf":null` is the store's own spelling of "not carried", and ccd's encoder never writes a null meas value. A forged one ends the item as a forged `"removed"` would (P3).

A departure the wave finds gets its own number, issued at its fix round and defined here singly.

- `mount-found-after-the-kill-repeats`: a mount found at step 3 or 4 fails `worktree-remove-failed` after the pane kill, on every retry (R12, forwarded).

- `found-nothing-clause-yields-to-a-reclaim-item`: when a reclaim item (terminal, failing, stuck, kept, or a kept-many member) already holds the id, the found-nothing item yields to it whole, and no item carries its clause (Task 13, the yield's second arm).
